constants.name: INVALID_ID
constants.description: Returned by [method play_stream] in case it could not allocate a stream for playback.

methods.name: play_stream
methods.description:
Play an [AudioStream] at a given offset, volume, pitch scale, playback type, and bus. Playback starts immediately.
The return value is a unique integer ID that is associated to this playback stream and which can be used to control it.
This ID becomes invalid when the stream ends (if it does not loop), when the [AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic] is stopped, or when [method stop_stream] is called.
This function returns [constant INVALID_ID] if the amount of streams currently playing equals [member AudioStreamPolyphonic.polyphony]. If you need a higher amount of maximum polyphony, raise this value.

methods.name: set_stream_volume
methods.description: Change the stream volume (in db). The [param stream] argument is an integer ID returned by [method play_stream].

methods.name: set_stream_pitch_scale
methods.description: Change the stream pitch scale. The [param stream] argument is an integer ID returned by [method play_stream].

methods.name: is_stream_playing
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the stream associated with the given integer ID is still playing. Check [method play_stream] for information on when this ID becomes invalid.

methods.name: stop_stream
methods.description: Stop a stream. The [param stream] argument is an integer ID returned by [method play_stream], which becomes invalid after calling this function.

classes.brief_description: Playback instance for [AudioStreamPolyphonic].
classes.description: Playback instance for [AudioStreamPolyphonic]. After setting the [code]stream[/code] property of [AudioStreamPlayer], [AudioStreamPlayer2D], or [AudioStreamPlayer3D], the playback instance can be obtained by calling [method AudioStreamPlayer.get_stream_playback], [method AudioStreamPlayer2D.get_stream_playback] or [method AudioStreamPlayer3D.get_stream_playback] methods.

classes.name: AudioStreamPlaybackResampled

methods.name: _mix_resampled
methods.description: Called by [method begin_resample] to mix an [AudioStream] to [method AudioServer.get_mix_rate]. Uses [method _get_stream_sampling_rate] as the source sample rate. Returns the number of mixed frames.

methods.name: _get_stream_sampling_rate
methods.description: Returns an [AudioStream]'s sample rate, in Hz. Used to perform resampling.

methods.name: begin_resample
methods.description: Called when an [AudioStream] is played. Clears the cubic interpolation history and starts mixing by calling [method _mix_resampled].

classes.brief_description: Playback class used for resampled [AudioStream]s.
classes.description: Playback class used to mix an [AudioStream]'s audio samples to [method AudioServer.get_mix_rate] using cubic interpolation.

classes.name: AudioStreamPlayer

values.name: MIX_TARGET_STEREO
values.description: The audio will be played only on the first channel. This is the default.

values.name: MIX_TARGET_SURROUND
values.description: The audio will be played on all surround channels.

values.name: MIX_TARGET_CENTER
values.description: The audio will be played on the second channel, which is usually the center.

methods.name: play
methods.description: Plays a sound from the beginning, or the given [param from_position] in seconds.

methods.name: seek
methods.description: Restarts all sounds to be played from the given [param to_position], in seconds. Does nothing if no sounds are playing.

methods.name: stop
methods.description: Stops all sounds from this node.

methods.name: get_playback_position
methods.description:
Returns the position in the [AudioStream] of the latest sound, in seconds. Returns [code]0.0[/code] if no sounds are playing.
[b]Note:[/b] The position is not always accurate, as the [AudioServer] does not mix audio every processed frame. To get more accurate results, add [method AudioServer.get_time_since_last_mix] to the returned position.
[b]Note:[/b] This method always returns [code]0.0[/code] if the [member stream] is an [AudioStreamInteractive], since it can have multiple clips playing at once.

methods.name: has_stream_playback
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if any sound is active, even if [member stream_paused] is set to [code]true[/code]. See also [member playing] and [method get_stream_playback].

methods.name: get_stream_playback
methods.description: Returns the latest [AudioStreamPlayback] of this node, usually the most recently created by [method play]. If no sounds are playing, this method fails and returns an empty playback.

signals.name: finished
signals.description: Emitted when a sound finishes playing without interruptions. This signal is [i]not[/i] emitted when calling [method stop], or when exiting the tree while sounds are playing.

properties.name: stream
properties.description: The [AudioStream] resource to be played. Setting this property stops all currently playing sounds. If left empty, the [AudioStreamPlayer] does not work.

properties.name: volume_db
properties.description:
Volume of sound, in decibels. This is an offset of the [member stream]'s volume.
[b]Note:[/b] To convert between decibel and linear energy (like most volume sliders do), use [member volume_linear], or [method @GlobalScope.db_to_linear] and [method @GlobalScope.linear_to_db].

properties.name: volume_linear
properties.description:
Volume of sound, as a linear value.
[b]Note:[/b] This member modifies [member volume_db] for convenience. The returned value is equivalent to the result of [method @GlobalScope.db_to_linear] on [member volume_db]. Setting this member is equivalent to setting [member volume_db] to the result of [method @GlobalScope.linear_to_db] on a value.

properties.name: pitch_scale
properties.description: The audio's pitch and tempo, as a multiplier of the [member stream]'s sample rate. A value of [code]2.0[/code] doubles the audio's pitch, while a value of [code]0.5[/code] halves the pitch.

properties.name: playing
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], this node is playing sounds. Setting this property has the same effect as [method play] and [method stop].

properties.name: autoplay
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], this node calls [method play] when entering the tree.

properties.name: stream_paused
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], the sounds are paused. Setting [member stream_paused] to [code]false[/code] resumes all sounds.
[b]Note:[/b] This property is automatically changed when exiting or entering the tree, or this node is paused (see [member Node.process_mode]).

properties.name: mix_target
properties.description: The mix target channels. Has no effect when two speakers or less are detected (see [enum AudioServer.SpeakerMode]).

properties.name: max_polyphony
properties.description: The maximum number of sounds this node can play at the same time. Calling [method play] after this value is reached will cut off the oldest sounds.

properties.name: bus
properties.description:
The target bus name. All sounds from this node will be playing on this bus.
[b]Note:[/b] At runtime, if no bus with the given name exists, all sounds will fall back on [code]"Master"[/code]. See also [method AudioServer.get_bus_name].

properties.name: playback_type
properties.description: The playback type of the stream player. If set other than to the default value, it will force that playback type.

classes.brief_description: A node for audio playback.
classes.description:
The [AudioStreamPlayer] node plays an audio stream non-positionally. It is ideal for user interfaces, menus, or background music.
To use this node, [member stream] needs to be set to a valid [AudioStream] resource. Playing more than one sound at the same time is also supported, see [member max_polyphony].
If you need to play audio at a specific position, use [AudioStreamPlayer2D] or [AudioStreamPlayer3D] instead.

classes.name: AudioStreamPlayer2D

methods.name: play
methods.description: Queues the audio to play on the next physics frame, from the given position [param from_position], in seconds.

methods.name: seek
methods.description: Sets the position from which audio will be played, in seconds.

methods.name: stop
methods.description: Stops the audio.

methods.name: get_playback_position
methods.description: Returns the position in the [AudioStream].

methods.name: has_stream_playback
methods.description: Returns whether the [AudioStreamPlayer] can return the [AudioStreamPlayback] object or not.

methods.name: get_stream_playback
methods.description: Returns the [AudioStreamPlayback] object associated with this [AudioStreamPlayer2D].

signals.name: finished
signals.description: Emitted when the audio stops playing.

properties.name: stream
properties.description: The [AudioStream] object to be played.

properties.name: volume_db
properties.description: Base volume before attenuation, in decibels.

properties.name: volume_linear
properties.description:
Base volume before attenuation, as a linear value.
[b]Note:[/b] This member modifies [member volume_db] for convenience. The returned value is equivalent to the result of [method @GlobalScope.db_to_linear] on [member volume_db]. Setting this member is equivalent to setting [member volume_db] to the result of [method @GlobalScope.linear_to_db] on a value.

properties.name: pitch_scale
properties.description: The pitch and the tempo of the audio, as a multiplier of the audio sample's sample rate.

properties.name: playing
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], audio is playing or is queued to be played (see [method play]).

properties.name: autoplay
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], audio plays when added to scene tree.

properties.name: stream_paused
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the playback is paused. You can resume it by setting [member stream_paused] to [code]false[/code].

properties.name: max_distance
properties.description: Maximum distance from which audio is still hearable.

properties.name: attenuation
properties.description: The volume is attenuated over distance with this as an exponent.

properties.name: max_polyphony
properties.description: The maximum number of sounds this node can play at the same time. Playing additional sounds after this value is reached will cut off the oldest sounds.

properties.name: panning_strength
properties.description: Scales the panning strength for this node by multiplying the base [member ProjectSettings.audio/general/2d_panning_strength] with this factor. Higher values will pan audio from left to right more dramatically than lower values.

properties.name: bus
properties.description:
Bus on which this audio is playing.
[b]Note:[/b] When setting this property, keep in mind that no validation is performed to see if the given name matches an existing bus. This is because audio bus layouts might be loaded after this property is set. If this given name can't be resolved at runtime, it will fall back to [code]"Master"[/code].

properties.name: area_mask
properties.description: Determines which [Area2D] layers affect the sound for reverb and audio bus effects. Areas can be used to redirect [AudioStream]s so that they play in a certain audio bus. An example of how you might use this is making a "water" area so that sounds played in the water are redirected through an audio bus to make them sound like they are being played underwater.

properties.name: playback_type
properties.description: The playback type of the stream player. If set other than to the default value, it will force that playback type.

classes.brief_description: Plays positional sound in 2D space.
classes.description:
Plays audio that is attenuated with distance to the listener.
By default, audio is heard from the screen center. This can be changed by adding an [AudioListener2D] node to the scene and enabling it by calling [method AudioListener2D.make_current] on it.
See also [AudioStreamPlayer] to play a sound non-positionally.
[b]Note:[/b] Hiding an [AudioStreamPlayer2D] node does not disable its audio output. To temporarily disable an [AudioStreamPlayer2D]'s audio output, set [member volume_db] to a very low value like [code]-100[/code] (which isn't audible to human hearing).

classes.name: AudioStreamPlayer3D

values.name: ATTENUATION_INVERSE_DISTANCE
values.description: Attenuation of loudness according to linear distance.

values.name: ATTENUATION_INVERSE_SQUARE_DISTANCE
values.description: Attenuation of loudness according to squared distance.

values.name: ATTENUATION_LOGARITHMIC
values.description: Attenuation of loudness according to logarithmic distance.

values.name: ATTENUATION_DISABLED
values.description: No attenuation of loudness according to distance. The sound will still be heard positionally, unlike an [AudioStreamPlayer]. [constant ATTENUATION_DISABLED] can be combined with a [member max_distance] value greater than [code]0.0[/code] to achieve linear attenuation clamped to a sphere of a defined size.

values.name: DOPPLER_TRACKING_DISABLED
values.description: Disables doppler tracking.

values.name: DOPPLER_TRACKING_IDLE_STEP
values.description: Executes doppler tracking during process frames (see [constant Node.NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PROCESS]).

values.name: DOPPLER_TRACKING_PHYSICS_STEP
values.description: Executes doppler tracking during physics frames (see [constant Node.NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS]).

methods.name: play
methods.description: Queues the audio to play on the next physics frame, from the given position [param from_position], in seconds.

methods.name: seek
methods.description: Sets the position from which audio will be played, in seconds.

methods.name: stop
methods.description: Stops the audio.

methods.name: get_playback_position
methods.description: Returns the position in the [AudioStream].

methods.description: Returns whether the [AudioStreamPlayer] can return the [AudioStreamPlayback] object or not.

methods.description: Returns the [AudioStreamPlayback] object associated with this [AudioStreamPlayer3D].

signals.name: finished
signals.description: Emitted when the audio stops playing.

properties.name: stream
properties.description: The [AudioStream] resource to be played.

properties.name: attenuation_model
properties.description: Decides if audio should get quieter with distance linearly, quadratically, logarithmically, or not be affected by distance, effectively disabling attenuation.

properties.name: volume_db
properties.description: The base sound level before attenuation, in decibels.

properties.name: volume_linear
properties.description:
The base sound level before attenuation, as a linear value.
[b]Note:[/b] This member modifies [member volume_db] for convenience. The returned value is equivalent to the result of [method @GlobalScope.db_to_linear] on [member volume_db]. Setting this member is equivalent to setting [member volume_db] to the result of [method @GlobalScope.linear_to_db] on a value.

properties.name: unit_size
properties.description: The factor for the attenuation effect. Higher values make the sound audible over a larger distance.

properties.name: max_db
properties.description: Sets the absolute maximum of the sound level, in decibels.

properties.name: pitch_scale
properties.description: The pitch and the tempo of the audio, as a multiplier of the audio sample's sample rate.

properties.name: playing
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], audio is playing or is queued to be played (see [method play]).

properties.name: autoplay
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], audio plays when the AudioStreamPlayer3D node is added to scene tree.

properties.name: stream_paused
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the playback is paused. You can resume it by setting [member stream_paused] to [code]false[/code].

properties.name: max_distance
properties.description: The distance past which the sound can no longer be heard at all. Only has an effect if set to a value greater than [code]0.0[/code]. [member max_distance] works in tandem with [member unit_size]. However, unlike [member unit_size] whose behavior depends on the [member attenuation_model], [member max_distance] always works in a linear fashion. This can be used to prevent the [AudioStreamPlayer3D] from requiring audio mixing when the listener is far away, which saves CPU resources.

properties.name: max_polyphony
properties.description: The maximum number of sounds this node can play at the same time. Playing additional sounds after this value is reached will cut off the oldest sounds.

properties.name: panning_strength
properties.description:
Scales the panning strength for this node by multiplying the base [member ProjectSettings.audio/general/3d_panning_strength] by this factor. If the product is [code]0.0[/code] then stereo panning is disabled and the volume is the same for all channels. If the product is [code]1.0[/code] then one of the channels will be muted when the sound is located exactly to the left (or right) of the listener.
Two speaker stereo arrangements implement the [url=https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#stereopanner-algorithm]WebAudio standard for StereoPannerNode Panning[/url] where the volume is cosine of half the azimuth angle to the ear.
For other speaker arrangements such as the 5.1 and 7.1 the SPCAP (Speaker-Placement Correction Amplitude) algorithm is implemented.

properties.name: bus
properties.description:
The bus on which this audio is playing.
[b]Note:[/b] When setting this property, keep in mind that no validation is performed to see if the given name matches an existing bus. This is because audio bus layouts might be loaded after this property is set. If this given name can't be resolved at runtime, it will fall back to [code]"Master"[/code].

properties.name: area_mask
properties.description: Determines which [Area3D] layers affect the sound for reverb and audio bus effects. Areas can be used to redirect [AudioStream]s so that they play in a certain audio bus. An example of how you might use this is making a "water" area so that sounds played in the water are redirected through an audio bus to make them sound like they are being played underwater.

properties.name: playback_type
properties.description: The playback type of the stream player. If set other than to the default value, it will force that playback type.

properties.name: emission_angle_enabled
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the audio should be attenuated according to the direction of the sound.

properties.name: emission_angle_degrees
properties.description: The angle in which the audio reaches a listener unattenuated.

properties.name: emission_angle_filter_attenuation_db
properties.description: Attenuation factor used if listener is outside of [member emission_angle_degrees] and [member emission_angle_enabled] is set, in decibels.

properties.name: attenuation_filter_cutoff_hz
properties.description: The cutoff frequency of the attenuation low-pass filter, in Hz. A sound above this frequency is attenuated more than a sound below this frequency. To disable this effect, set this to [code]20500[/code] as this frequency is above the human hearing limit.

properties.name: attenuation_filter_db
properties.description: Amount how much the filter affects the loudness, in decibels.

properties.name: doppler_tracking
properties.description:
Decides in which step the Doppler effect should be calculated.
[b]Note:[/b] If [member doppler_tracking] is not [constant DOPPLER_TRACKING_DISABLED] but the current [Camera3D]/[AudioListener3D] has doppler tracking disabled, the Doppler effect will be heard but will not take the movement of the current listener into account. If accurate Doppler effect is desired, doppler tracking should be enabled on both the [AudioStreamPlayer3D] and the current [Camera3D]/[AudioListener3D].

classes.brief_description: Plays positional sound in 3D space.
classes.description:
Plays audio with positional sound effects, based on the relative position of the audio listener. Positional effects include distance attenuation, directionality, and the Doppler effect. For greater realism, a low-pass filter is applied to distant sounds. This can be disabled by setting [member attenuation_filter_cutoff_hz] to [code]20500[/code].
By default, audio is heard from the camera position. This can be changed by adding an [AudioListener3D] node to the scene and enabling it by calling [method AudioListener3D.make_current] on it.
See also [AudioStreamPlayer] to play a sound non-positionally.
[b]Note:[/b] Hiding an [AudioStreamPlayer3D] node does not disable its audio output. To temporarily disable an [AudioStreamPlayer3D]'s audio output, set [member volume_db] to a very low value like [code]-100[/code] (which isn't audible to human hearing).

classes.name: AudioStreamPlaylist

constants.name: MAX_STREAMS
constants.description: Maximum amount of streams supported in the playlist.

methods.name: get_bpm
methods.description: Returns the BPM of the playlist, which can vary depending on the clip being played.

methods.name: set_list_stream
methods.description: Sets the stream at playback position index.

methods.name: get_list_stream
methods.description: Returns the stream at playback position index.

properties.name: shuffle
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the playlist will shuffle each time playback starts and each time it loops.

properties.name: loop
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the playlist will loop, otherwise the playlist will end when the last stream is finished.

properties.name: fade_time
properties.description: Fade time used when a stream ends, when going to the next one. Streams are expected to have an extra bit of audio after the end to help with fading.

properties.name: stream_count
properties.description: Amount of streams in the playlist.

classes.brief_description: [AudioStream] that includes sub-streams and plays them back like a playlist.
classes.description: An audio stream that can play back sub-streams in sequence. Streams can be added to the Playlist with [method set_list_stream], and shuffled with [member shuffle].

classes.name: AudioStreamPolyphonic

properties.name: polyphony
properties.description: Maximum amount of simultaneous streams that can be played.

classes.brief_description: AudioStream that lets the user play custom streams at any time from code, simultaneously using a single player.
classes.description:
AudioStream that lets the user play custom streams at any time from code, simultaneously using a single player.
Playback control is done via the [AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic] instance set inside the player, which can be obtained via [method AudioStreamPlayer.get_stream_playback], [method AudioStreamPlayer2D.get_stream_playback] or [method AudioStreamPlayer3D.get_stream_playback] methods. Obtaining the playback instance is only valid after the [code]stream[/code] property is set as an [AudioStreamPolyphonic] in those players.

classes.name: AudioStreamRandomizer

values.name: PLAYBACK_RANDOM_NO_REPEATS
values.description: Pick a stream at random according to the probability weights chosen for each stream, but avoid playing the same stream twice in a row whenever possible. If only 1 sound is present in the pool, the same sound will always play, effectively allowing repeats to occur.

values.name: PLAYBACK_RANDOM
values.description: Pick a stream at random according to the probability weights chosen for each stream. If only 1 sound is present in the pool, the same sound will always play.

values.name: PLAYBACK_SEQUENTIAL
values.description: Play streams in the order they appear in the stream pool. If only 1 sound is present in the pool, the same sound will always play.

methods.name: add_stream
methods.description: Insert a stream at the specified index. If the index is less than zero, the insertion occurs at the end of the underlying pool.

methods.name: move_stream
methods.description: Move a stream from one index to another.

methods.name: remove_stream
methods.description: Remove the stream at the specified index.

methods.name: set_stream
methods.description: Set the AudioStream at the specified index.

methods.name: get_stream
methods.description: Returns the stream at the specified index.

methods.name: set_stream_probability_weight
methods.description: Set the probability weight of the stream at the specified index. The higher this value, the more likely that the randomizer will choose this stream during random playback modes.

methods.name: get_stream_probability_weight
methods.description: Returns the probability weight associated with the stream at the given index.

properties.name: playback_mode
properties.description: Controls how this AudioStreamRandomizer picks which AudioStream to play next.

properties.name: random_pitch
properties.description:
The largest possible frequency multiplier of the random pitch variation. Pitch will be randomly chosen within a range of [code skip-lint]1.0 / random_pitch[/code] and [code skip-lint]random_pitch[/code]. A value of [code]1.0[/code] means no variation. A value of [code]2.0[/code] means pitch will be randomized between double and half.
[b]Note:[/b] Setting this property also sets [member random_pitch_semitones].

properties.name: random_pitch_semitones
properties.description:
The largest possible distance, in semitones, of the random pitch variation. A value of [code]0.0[/code] means no variation.
[b]Note:[/b] Setting this property also sets [member random_pitch].

properties.name: random_volume_offset_db
properties.description: The intensity of random volume variation. Volume will be increased or decreased by a random value up to [code skip-lint]random_volume_offset_db[/code]. A value of [code]0.0[/code] means no variation. A value of [code]3.0[/code] means volume will be randomized between [code]-3.0 dB[/code] and [code]+3.0 dB[/code].

properties.name: streams_count
properties.description: The number of streams in the stream pool.

classes.brief_description: Wraps a pool of audio streams with pitch and volume shifting.
classes.description: Picks a random AudioStream from the pool, depending on the playback mode, and applies random pitch shifting and volume shifting during playback.

classes.name: AudioStreamSynchronized

constants.name: MAX_STREAMS
constants.description: Maximum amount of streams that can be synchronized.

methods.name: set_sync_stream
methods.description: Set one of the synchronized streams, by index.

methods.name: get_sync_stream
methods.description: Get one of the synchronized streams, by index.

methods.name: set_sync_stream_volume
methods.description: Set the volume of one of the synchronized streams, by index.

methods.name: get_sync_stream_volume
methods.description: Get the volume of one of the synchronized streams, by index.

properties.name: stream_count
properties.description: Set the total amount of streams that will be played back synchronized.

classes.brief_description: Stream that can be fitted with sub-streams, which will be played in-sync.
classes.description: This is a stream that can be fitted with sub-streams, which will be played in-sync. The streams begin at exactly the same time when play is pressed, and will end when the last of them ends. If one of the sub-streams loops, then playback will continue.

classes.name: AudioStreamWAV

values.name: FORMAT_8_BITS
values.description: 8-bit PCM audio codec.

values.name: FORMAT_16_BITS
values.description: 16-bit PCM audio codec.

values.name: FORMAT_IMA_ADPCM
values.description: Audio is lossily compressed as IMA ADPCM.

values.name: FORMAT_QOA
values.description: Audio is lossily compressed as [url=https://qoaformat.org/]Quite OK Audio[/url].

values.name: LOOP_DISABLED
values.description: Audio does not loop.

values.name: LOOP_FORWARD
values.description: Audio loops the data between [member loop_begin] and [member loop_end], playing forward only.

values.name: LOOP_PINGPONG
values.description: Audio loops the data between [member loop_begin] and [member loop_end], playing back and forth.

values.name: LOOP_BACKWARD
values.description: Audio loops the data between [member loop_begin] and [member loop_end], playing backward only.

methods.name: load_from_buffer
methods.description:
Creates a new [AudioStreamWAV] instance from the given buffer. The buffer must contain WAV data.
The keys and values of [param options] match the properties of [ResourceImporterWAV]. The usage of [param options] is identical to [method AudioStreamWAV.load_from_file].

methods.name: load_from_file
save_to_wav
methods.description:
Saves the AudioStreamWAV as a WAV file to [param path]. Samples with IMA ADPCM or Quite OK Audio formats can't be saved.
[b]Note:[/b] A [code].wav[/code] extension is automatically appended to [param path] if it is missing.

properties.name: data
properties.description:
Contains the audio data in bytes.
[b]Note:[/b] If [member format] is set to [constant FORMAT_8_BITS], this property expects signed 8-bit PCM data. To convert from unsigned 8-bit PCM, subtract 128 from each byte.
[b]Note:[/b] If [member format] is set to [constant FORMAT_QOA], this property expects data from a full QOA file.

properties.name: format
properties.description: Audio format.

properties.name: loop_mode
properties.description: The loop mode.

properties.name: loop_begin
properties.description: The loop start point (in number of samples, relative to the beginning of the stream).

properties.name: loop_end
properties.description: The loop end point (in number of samples, relative to the beginning of the stream).

properties.name: mix_rate
properties.description:
The sample rate for mixing this audio. Higher values require more storage space, but result in better quality.
In games, common sample rates in use are [code]11025[/code], [code]16000[/code], [code]22050[/code], [code]32000[/code], [code]44100[/code], and [code]48000[/code].
According to the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyquist%E2%80%93Shannon_sampling_theorem]Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem[/url], there is no quality difference to human hearing when going past 40,000 Hz (since most humans can only hear up to ~20,000 Hz, often less). If you are using lower-pitched sounds such as voices, lower sample rates such as [code]32000[/code] or [code]22050[/code] may be usable with no loss in quality.

properties.name: stereo
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], audio is stereo.

properties.name: tags
properties.description:
Contains user-defined tags if found in the WAV data.
Commonly used tags include [code]title[/code], [code]artist[/code], [code]album[/code], [code]tracknumber[/code], and [code]date[/code] ([code]date[/code] does not have a standard date format).
[b]Note:[/b] No tag is [i]guaranteed[/i] to be present in every file, so make sure to account for the keys not always existing.
[b]Note:[/b] Only WAV files using a [code]LIST[/code] chunk with an identifier of [code]INFO[/code] to encode the tags are currently supported.

classes.brief_description: Stores audio data loaded from WAV files.
classes.description:
AudioStreamWAV stores sound samples loaded from WAV files. To play the stored sound, use an [AudioStreamPlayer] (for non-positional audio) or [AudioStreamPlayer2D]/[AudioStreamPlayer3D] (for positional audio). The sound can be looped.
This class can also be used to store dynamically-generated PCM audio data. See also [AudioStreamGenerator] for procedural audio generation.

classes.name: AwaitTweener

methods.name: set_timeout
methods.description: Sets the maximum time an [AwaitTweener] can wait for the signal. Can be used as a safeguard for signals that may never be emitted. If not specified, the tweener will wait indefinitely.

classes.brief_description: Awaits a specified signal.
classes.description:
[AwaitTweener] is used to await a specified signal, allowing asynchronous steps in [Tween] animation. See [method Tween.tween_await] for more usage information.
The [signal Tweener.finished] signal is emitted when either the awaited signal is received, when timeout is reached, or when the target object is freed.

classes.name: BackBufferCopy

values.name: COPY_MODE_DISABLED
values.description: Disables the buffering mode. This means the [BackBufferCopy] node will directly use the portion of screen it covers.

values.name: COPY_MODE_RECT
values.description: [BackBufferCopy] buffers a rectangular region.

values.name: COPY_MODE_VIEWPORT
values.description: [BackBufferCopy] buffers the entire screen.

properties.name: copy_mode
properties.description: Buffer mode.

properties.name: rect
properties.description: The area covered by the [BackBufferCopy]. Only used if [member copy_mode] is [constant COPY_MODE_RECT].

classes.brief_description: A node that copies a region of the screen to a buffer for access in shader code.
classes.description:
Node for back-buffering the currently-displayed screen. The region defined in the [BackBufferCopy] node is buffered with the content of the screen it covers, or the entire screen according to the [member copy_mode]. It can be accessed in shader scripts using the screen texture (i.e. a uniform sampler with [code]hint_screen_texture[/code]).
[b]Note:[/b] Since this node inherits from [Node2D] (and not [Control]), anchors and margins won't apply to child [Control]-derived nodes. This can be problematic when resizing the window. To avoid this, add [Control]-derived nodes as [i]siblings[/i] to the [BackBufferCopy] node instead of adding them as children.

classes.name: BaseButton

values.name: DRAW_NORMAL
values.description: The normal state (i.e. not pressed, not hovered, not toggled and enabled) of buttons.

values.name: DRAW_PRESSED
values.description: The state of buttons are pressed.

values.name: DRAW_HOVER
values.description: The state of buttons are hovered.

values.name: DRAW_DISABLED
values.description: The state of buttons are disabled.

values.name: DRAW_HOVER_PRESSED
values.description: The state of buttons are both hovered and pressed.

values.name: ACTION_MODE_BUTTON_PRESS
values.description: Require just a press to consider the button clicked.

values.name: ACTION_MODE_BUTTON_RELEASE
values.description: Require a press and a subsequent release before considering the button clicked.

methods.name: _pressed
methods.description: Called when the button is pressed. If you need to know the button's pressed state (and [member toggle_mode] is active), use [method _toggled] instead.

methods.name: _toggled
methods.description: Called when the button is toggled (only if [member toggle_mode] is active).

methods.name: set_pressed_no_signal
methods.description:
Changes the [member button_pressed] state of the button, without emitting [signal toggled]. Use when you just want to change the state of the button without sending the pressed event (e.g. when initializing scene). Only works if [member toggle_mode] is [code]true[/code].
[b]Note:[/b] This method doesn't unpress other buttons in [member button_group].

methods.name: is_hovered
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the mouse has entered the button and has not left it yet.

methods.name: get_draw_mode
methods.description: Returns the visual state used to draw the button. This is useful mainly when implementing your own draw code by either overriding _draw() or connecting to "draw" signal. The visual state of the button is defined by the [enum DrawMode] enum.

signals.name: pressed
signals.description:
Emitted when the button is toggled or pressed. This is on [signal button_down] if [member action_mode] is [constant ACTION_MODE_BUTTON_PRESS] and on [signal button_up] otherwise.
If you need to know the button's pressed state (and [member toggle_mode] is active), use [signal toggled] instead.

signals.name: button_up
signals.description: Emitted when the button stops being held down.

signals.name: button_down
signals.description: Emitted when the button starts being held down.

signals.name: toggled
signals.description: Emitted when the button was just toggled between pressed and normal states (only if [member toggle_mode] is active). The new state is contained in the [param toggled_on] argument.

properties.name: disabled
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], the button is in disabled state and can't be clicked or toggled.
[b]Note:[/b] If the button is disabled while held down, [signal button_up] will be emitted.

properties.name: toggle_mode
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the button is in toggle mode. Makes the button flip state between pressed and unpressed each time its area is clicked.

properties.name: button_pressed
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], the button's state is pressed. Means the button is pressed down or toggled (if [member toggle_mode] is active). Only works if [member toggle_mode] is [code]true[/code].
[b]Note:[/b] Changing the value of [member button_pressed] will result in [signal toggled] to be emitted. If you want to change the pressed state without emitting that signal, use [method set_pressed_no_signal].

properties.name: action_mode
properties.description: Determines when the button is considered clicked.

properties.name: button_mask
properties.description:
Binary mask to choose which mouse buttons this button will respond to.
To allow both left-click and right-click, use [code]MOUSE_BUTTON_MASK_LEFT | MOUSE_BUTTON_MASK_RIGHT[/code].

properties.name: keep_pressed_outside
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], the button stays pressed when moving the cursor outside the button while pressing it.
[b]Note:[/b] This property only affects the button's visual appearance. Signals will be emitted at the same moment regardless of this property's value.

properties.name: button_group
properties.description:
The [ButtonGroup] associated with the button. Not to be confused with node groups.
[b]Note:[/b] The button will be configured as a radio button if a [ButtonGroup] is assigned to it.

properties.name: shortcut
properties.description: [Shortcut] associated to the button.

properties.name: shortcut_feedback
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the button will highlight for a short amount of time when its shortcut is activated. If [code]false[/code] and [member toggle_mode] is [code]false[/code], the shortcut will activate without any visual feedback.

properties.name: shortcut_in_tooltip
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], the button will add information about its shortcut in the tooltip. This includes the shortcut's events and its [member Resource.resource_name]. If both events and name are empty, the shortcut will not be included.
[b]Note:[/b] This property does nothing when the tooltip control is customized using [method Control._make_custom_tooltip].

classes.brief_description: Abstract base class for GUI buttons.
classes.description: [BaseButton] is an abstract base class for GUI buttons. It doesn't display anything by itself.

values.name: TEXTURE_ALBEDO
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel color.

values.name: TEXTURE_METALLIC
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel metallic value.

values.name: TEXTURE_ROUGHNESS
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel roughness value.

values.name: TEXTURE_EMISSION
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel emission color.

values.name: TEXTURE_NORMAL
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel normal vector.

values.name: TEXTURE_BENT_NORMAL
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel bent normal vector.

values.name: TEXTURE_RIM
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel rim value.

values.name: TEXTURE_CLEARCOAT
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel clearcoat value.

values.name: TEXTURE_FLOWMAP
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel flowmap direction for use with [member anisotropy].

values.name: TEXTURE_AMBIENT_OCCLUSION
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel ambient occlusion value.

values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel height.

values.name: TEXTURE_SUBSURFACE_SCATTERING
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel subsurface scattering.

values.name: TEXTURE_SUBSURFACE_TRANSMITTANCE
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel transmittance for subsurface scattering.

values.name: TEXTURE_BACKLIGHT
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel backlight color.

values.name: TEXTURE_REFRACTION
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel refraction strength.

values.name: TEXTURE_DETAIL_MASK
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel detail mask blending value.

values.name: TEXTURE_DETAIL_ALBEDO
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel detail color.

values.name: TEXTURE_DETAIL_NORMAL
values.description: Texture specifying per-pixel detail normal.

values.name: TEXTURE_ORM
values.description: Texture holding ambient occlusion, roughness, and metallic.

values.name: TEXTURE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum TextureParam] enum.

values.name: TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST
values.description: The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel only. This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and grainy from a distance (due to mipmaps not being sampled).

values.name: TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR
values.description: The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels. This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and grainy from a distance (due to mipmaps not being sampled).

values.name: TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST_WITH_MIPMAPS
values.description: The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel and blends between the nearest 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if [member ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter] is [code]true[/code]). This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and smooth from a distance.

values.name: TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS
values.description: The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels and between the nearest 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if [member ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter] is [code]true[/code]). This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and smooth from a distance.

values.name: TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST_WITH_MIPMAPS_ANISOTROPIC
values.description: The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel and blends between 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if [member ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter] is [code]true[/code]) based on the angle between the surface and the camera view. This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and smooth from a distance. Anisotropic filtering improves texture quality on surfaces that are almost in line with the camera, but is slightly slower. The anisotropic filtering level can be changed by adjusting [member ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/anisotropic_filtering_level].

values.name: TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS_ANISOTROPIC
values.description: The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels and blends between 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if [member ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter] is [code]true[/code]) based on the angle between the surface and the camera view. This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and smooth from a distance. Anisotropic filtering improves texture quality on surfaces that are almost in line with the camera, but is slightly slower. The anisotropic filtering level can be changed by adjusting [member ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/anisotropic_filtering_level].

values.name: TEXTURE_FILTER_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum TextureFilter] enum.

values.name: DETAIL_UV_1
values.description: Use [code]UV[/code] with the detail texture.

values.name: DETAIL_UV_2
values.description: Use [code]UV2[/code] with the detail texture.

values.name: TRANSPARENCY_DISABLED
values.description: The material will not use transparency. This is the fastest to render.

values.name: TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA
values.description: The material will use the texture's alpha values for transparency. This is the slowest to render, and disables shadow casting.

values.name: TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA_SCISSOR
values.description: The material will cut off all values below a threshold, the rest will remain opaque. The opaque portions will be rendered in the depth prepass. This is faster to render than alpha blending, but slower than opaque rendering. This also supports casting shadows.

values.name: TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA_HASH
values.description: The material will cut off all values below a spatially-deterministic threshold, the rest will remain opaque. This is faster to render than alpha blending, but slower than opaque rendering. This also supports casting shadows. Alpha hashing is suited for hair rendering.

values.name: TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA_DEPTH_PRE_PASS
values.description: The material will use the texture's alpha value for transparency, but will discard fragments with an alpha of less than 0.99 during the depth prepass and fragments with an alpha less than 0.1 during the shadow pass. This also supports casting shadows.

values.name: TRANSPARENCY_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum Transparency] enum.

values.name: SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED
values.description: The object will not receive shadows. This is the fastest to render, but it disables all interactions with lights.

values.name: SHADING_MODE_PER_PIXEL
values.description: The object will be shaded per pixel. Useful for realistic shading effects.

values.name: SHADING_MODE_PER_VERTEX
values.description: The object will be shaded per vertex. Useful when you want cheaper shaders and do not care about visual quality.

values.name: SHADING_MODE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum ShadingMode] enum.

values.name: FEATURE_EMISSION
values.description: Constant for setting [member emission_enabled].

values.name: FEATURE_NORMAL_MAPPING
values.description: Constant for setting [member normal_enabled].

values.name: FEATURE_RIM
values.description: Constant for setting [member rim_enabled].

values.name: FEATURE_CLEARCOAT
values.description: Constant for setting [member clearcoat_enabled].

values.name: FEATURE_ANISOTROPY
values.description: Constant for setting [member anisotropy_enabled].

values.name: FEATURE_AMBIENT_OCCLUSION
values.description: Constant for setting [member ao_enabled].

values.name: FEATURE_HEIGHT_MAPPING
values.description: Constant for setting [member heightmap_enabled].

values.name: FEATURE_SUBSURFACE_SCATTERING
values.description: Constant for setting [member subsurf_scatter_enabled].

values.name: FEATURE_SUBSURFACE_TRANSMITTANCE
values.description: Constant for setting [member subsurf_scatter_transmittance_enabled].

values.name: FEATURE_BACKLIGHT
values.description: Constant for setting [member backlight_enabled].

values.name: FEATURE_REFRACTION
values.description: Constant for setting [member refraction_enabled].

values.name: FEATURE_DETAIL
values.description: Constant for setting [member detail_enabled].

values.name: FEATURE_BENT_NORMAL_MAPPING
values.description: Constant for setting [member bent_normal_enabled].

values.name: FEATURE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum Feature] enum.

values.name: BLEND_MODE_MIX
values.description: Default blend mode. The color of the object is blended over the background based on the object's alpha value.

values.name: BLEND_MODE_ADD
values.description: The color of the object is added to the background.

values.name: BLEND_MODE_SUB
values.description: The color of the object is subtracted from the background.

values.name: BLEND_MODE_MUL
values.description: The color of the object is multiplied by the background.

values.name: BLEND_MODE_PREMULT_ALPHA
values.description: The color of the object is added to the background and the alpha channel is used to mask out the background. This is effectively a hybrid of the blend mix and add modes, useful for effects like fire where you want the flame to add but the smoke to mix. By default, this works with unshaded materials using premultiplied textures. For shaded materials, use the [code]PREMUL_ALPHA_FACTOR[/code] built-in so that lighting can be modulated as well.

values.name: ALPHA_ANTIALIASING_OFF
values.description: Disables Alpha AntiAliasing for the material.

values.name: ALPHA_ANTIALIASING_ALPHA_TO_COVERAGE
values.description: Enables AlphaToCoverage. Alpha values in the material are passed to the AntiAliasing sample mask.

values.name: ALPHA_ANTIALIASING_ALPHA_TO_COVERAGE_AND_TO_ONE
values.description: Enables AlphaToCoverage and forces all non-zero alpha values to [code]1[/code]. Alpha values in the material are passed to the AntiAliasing sample mask.

values.name: DEPTH_DRAW_OPAQUE_ONLY
values.description: Default depth draw mode. Depth is drawn only for opaque objects during the opaque prepass (if any) and during the opaque pass.

values.name: DEPTH_DRAW_ALWAYS
values.description:
Objects will write to depth during the opaque and the transparent passes. Transparent objects that are close to the camera may obscure other transparent objects behind them.
[b]Note:[/b] This does not influence whether transparent objects are included in the depth prepass or not. For that, see [enum Transparency].

values.name: DEPTH_DRAW_DISABLED
values.description: Objects will not write their depth to the depth buffer, even during the depth prepass (if enabled).

values.name: DEPTH_TEST_DEFAULT
values.description: Depth test will discard the pixel if it is behind other pixels.

values.name: DEPTH_TEST_INVERTED
values.description: Depth test will discard the pixel if it is in front of other pixels. Useful for stencil effects.

values.name: CULL_BACK
values.description: Default cull mode. The back of the object is culled when not visible. Back face triangles will be culled when facing the camera. This results in only the front side of triangles being drawn. For closed-surface meshes, this means that only the exterior of the mesh will be visible.

values.name: CULL_FRONT
values.description: Front face triangles will be culled when facing the camera. This results in only the back side of triangles being drawn. For closed-surface meshes, this means that the interior of the mesh will be drawn instead of the exterior.

values.name: CULL_DISABLED
values.description: No face culling is performed; both the front face and back face will be visible.

values.name: FLAG_DISABLE_DEPTH_TEST
values.description: Disables the depth test, so this object is drawn on top of all others drawn before it. This puts the object in the transparent draw pass where it is sorted based on distance to camera. Objects drawn after it in the draw order may cover it. This also disables writing to depth.

values.name: FLAG_ALBEDO_FROM_VERTEX_COLOR
values.description: Set [code]ALBEDO[/code] to the per-vertex color specified in the mesh.

values.name: FLAG_SRGB_VERTEX_COLOR
values.description:
Vertex colors are considered to be stored in nonlinear sRGB encoding and are converted to linear encoding during rendering. See also [member vertex_color_is_srgb].
[b]Note:[/b] Only effective when using the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods.

values.name: FLAG_USE_POINT_SIZE
values.description: Uses point size to alter the size of primitive points. Also changes the albedo texture lookup to use [code]POINT_COORD[/code] instead of [code]UV[/code].

values.name: FLAG_FIXED_SIZE
values.description: Object is scaled by depth so that it always appears the same size on screen.

values.name: FLAG_BILLBOARD_KEEP_SCALE
values.description: Shader will keep the scale set for the mesh. Otherwise the scale is lost when billboarding. Only applies when [member billboard_mode] is [constant BILLBOARD_ENABLED].

values.name: FLAG_UV1_USE_TRIPLANAR
values.description: Use triplanar texture lookup for all texture lookups that would normally use [code]UV[/code].

values.name: FLAG_UV2_USE_TRIPLANAR
values.description: Use triplanar texture lookup for all texture lookups that would normally use [code]UV2[/code].

values.name: FLAG_UV1_USE_WORLD_TRIPLANAR
values.description: Use triplanar texture lookup for all texture lookups that would normally use [code]UV[/code].

values.name: FLAG_UV2_USE_WORLD_TRIPLANAR
values.description: Use triplanar texture lookup for all texture lookups that would normally use [code]UV2[/code].

values.name: FLAG_AO_ON_UV2
values.description: Use [code]UV2[/code] coordinates to look up from the [member ao_texture].

values.name: FLAG_EMISSION_ON_UV2
values.description: Use [code]UV2[/code] coordinates to look up from the [member emission_texture].

values.name: FLAG_ALBEDO_TEXTURE_FORCE_SRGB
values.description: Forces the shader to convert albedo from nonlinear sRGB encoding to linear encoding. See also [member albedo_texture_force_srgb].

values.name: FLAG_DONT_RECEIVE_SHADOWS
values.description: Disables receiving shadows from other objects.

values.name: FLAG_DISABLE_AMBIENT_LIGHT
values.description: Disables receiving ambient light.

values.name: FLAG_USE_SHADOW_TO_OPACITY
values.description: Enables the shadow to opacity feature.

values.name: FLAG_USE_TEXTURE_REPEAT
values.description: Enables the texture to repeat when UV coordinates are outside the 0-1 range. If using one of the linear filtering modes, this can result in artifacts at the edges of a texture when the sampler filters across the edges of the texture.

values.name: FLAG_INVERT_HEIGHTMAP
values.description: Invert values read from a depth texture to convert them to height values (heightmap).

values.name: FLAG_SUBSURFACE_MODE_SKIN
values.description: Enables the skin mode for subsurface scattering which is used to improve the look of subsurface scattering when used for human skin.

values.name: FLAG_PARTICLE_TRAILS_MODE
values.description: Enables parts of the shader required for [GPUParticles3D] trails to function. This also requires using a mesh with appropriate skinning, such as [RibbonTrailMesh] or [TubeTrailMesh]. Enabling this feature outside of materials used in [GPUParticles3D] meshes will break material rendering.

values.name: FLAG_ALBEDO_TEXTURE_MSDF
values.description: Enables multichannel signed distance field rendering shader.

values.name: FLAG_DISABLE_FOG
values.description: Disables receiving depth-based or volumetric fog.

values.name: FLAG_DISABLE_SPECULAR_OCCLUSION
values.description: Disables specular occlusion.

values.name: FLAG_USE_Z_CLIP_SCALE
values.description: Enables using [member z_clip_scale].

values.name: FLAG_USE_FOV_OVERRIDE
values.description: Enables using [member fov_override].

values.name: FLAG_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum Flags] enum.

values.name: DIFFUSE_BURLEY
values.description: Default diffuse scattering algorithm.

values.name: DIFFUSE_LAMBERT
values.description: Diffuse scattering ignores roughness.

values.name: DIFFUSE_LAMBERT_WRAP
values.description: Extends Lambert to cover more than 90 degrees when roughness increases.

values.name: DIFFUSE_TOON
values.description: Uses a hard cut for lighting, with smoothing affected by roughness.

values.name: SPECULAR_SCHLICK_GGX
values.description:
Default specular blob.
[b]Note:[/b] Forward+ uses multiscattering for more accurate reflections, although the impact of multiscattering is more noticeable on rough metallic surfaces than on smooth, non-metallic surfaces.
[b]Note:[/b] Mobile and Compatibility don't perform multiscattering for performance reasons. Instead, they perform single scattering, which means rough metallic surfaces may look slightly darker than intended.

values.name: SPECULAR_TOON
values.description: Toon blob which changes size based on roughness.

values.name: SPECULAR_DISABLED
values.description: No specular blob. This is slightly faster to render than other specular modes.

values.name: BILLBOARD_DISABLED
values.description: Billboard mode is disabled.

values.name: BILLBOARD_ENABLED
values.description: The object's Z axis will always face the camera.

values.name: BILLBOARD_FIXED_Y
values.description: The object's X axis will always face the camera.

values.name: BILLBOARD_PARTICLES
values.description:
Used for particle systems when assigned to [GPUParticles3D] and [CPUParticles3D] nodes (flipbook animation). Enables [code]particles_anim_*[/code] properties.
The [member ParticleProcessMaterial.anim_speed_min] or [member CPUParticles3D.anim_speed_min] should also be set to a value bigger than zero for the animation to play.

values.name: TEXTURE_CHANNEL_RED
values.description: Used to read from the red channel of a texture.

values.name: TEXTURE_CHANNEL_GREEN
values.description: Used to read from the green channel of a texture.

values.name: TEXTURE_CHANNEL_BLUE
values.description: Used to read from the blue channel of a texture.

values.name: TEXTURE_CHANNEL_ALPHA
values.description: Used to read from the alpha channel of a texture.

values.name: TEXTURE_CHANNEL_GRAYSCALE
values.description: Used to read from the linear (non-perceptual) average of the red, green and blue channels of a texture.

values.name: EMISSION_OP_ADD
values.description: Adds the emission color to the color from the emission texture.

values.name: EMISSION_OP_MULTIPLY
values.description: Multiplies the emission color by the color from the emission texture.

values.name: DISTANCE_FADE_DISABLED
values.description: Do not use distance fade.

values.name: DISTANCE_FADE_PIXEL_ALPHA
values.description: Smoothly fades the object out based on each pixel's distance from the camera using the alpha channel.

values.name: DISTANCE_FADE_PIXEL_DITHER
values.description: Smoothly fades the object out based on each pixel's distance from the camera using a dithering approach. Dithering discards pixels based on a set pattern to smoothly fade without enabling transparency. On certain hardware, this can be faster than [constant DISTANCE_FADE_PIXEL_ALPHA].

values.name: DISTANCE_FADE_OBJECT_DITHER
values.description: Smoothly fades the object out based on the object's distance from the camera using a dithering approach. Dithering discards pixels based on a set pattern to smoothly fade without enabling transparency. On certain hardware, this can be faster than [constant DISTANCE_FADE_PIXEL_ALPHA] and [constant DISTANCE_FADE_PIXEL_DITHER].

values.name: STENCIL_MODE_DISABLED
values.description: Disables stencil operations.

values.name: STENCIL_MODE_OUTLINE
values.description:
Stencil preset which applies an outline to the object.
[b]Note:[/b] Requires a [member Material.next_pass] material which will be automatically applied. Any manual changes made to [member Material.next_pass] will be lost when the stencil properties are modified or the scene is reloaded. To safely apply a [member Material.next_pass] material on a material that uses stencil presets, use [member GeometryInstance3D.material_overlay] instead.

values.name: STENCIL_MODE_XRAY
values.description:
Stencil preset which shows a silhouette of the object behind walls.
[b]Note:[/b] Requires a [member Material.next_pass] material which will be automatically applied. Any manual changes made to [member Material.next_pass] will be lost when the stencil properties are modified or the scene is reloaded. To safely apply a [member Material.next_pass] material on a material that uses stencil presets, use [member GeometryInstance3D.material_overlay] instead.

values.name: STENCIL_MODE_CUSTOM
values.description: Enables stencil operations without a preset.

values.name: STENCIL_FLAG_READ
values.description: The material will only be rendered where it passes a stencil comparison with existing stencil buffer values.

values.name: STENCIL_FLAG_WRITE
values.description: The material will write the reference value to the stencil buffer where it passes the depth test.

values.name: STENCIL_FLAG_WRITE_DEPTH_FAIL
values.description: The material will write the reference value to the stencil buffer where it fails the depth test.

values.name: STENCIL_COMPARE_ALWAYS
values.description: Always passes the stencil test.

values.name: STENCIL_COMPARE_LESS
values.description: Passes the stencil test when the reference value is less than the existing stencil value.

values.name: STENCIL_COMPARE_EQUAL
values.description: Passes the stencil test when the reference value is equal to the existing stencil value.

values.name: STENCIL_COMPARE_LESS_OR_EQUAL
values.description: Passes the stencil test when the reference value is less than or equal to the existing stencil value.

values.name: STENCIL_COMPARE_GREATER
values.description: Passes the stencil test when the reference value is greater than the existing stencil value.

values.name: STENCIL_COMPARE_NOT_EQUAL
values.description: Passes the stencil test when the reference value is not equal to the existing stencil value.

values.name: STENCIL_COMPARE_GREATER_OR_EQUAL
values.description: Passes the stencil test when the reference value is greater than or equal to the existing stencil value.

methods.name: set_flag
methods.description: If [param enable] is [code]true[/code], enables the specified [param flag]. Flags are optional behavior that can be turned on and off. Only one flag can be enabled at a time with this function, the flag enumerators cannot be bit-masked together to enable or disable multiple flags at once. Flags can also be enabled by setting their corresponding property to [code]true[/code].

methods.name: get_flag
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the specified [param flag] is enabled.

methods.name: set_feature
methods.description: If [param enable] is [code]true[/code], enables the specified [param feature]. Many features that are available in [BaseMaterial3D] need to be enabled before use. This way, the cost for using the feature is only incurred when specified. Features can also be enabled by setting their corresponding property to [code]true[/code].

methods.name: get_feature
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the specified [param feature] is enabled.

methods.name: set_texture
methods.description: Sets the texture for the slot specified by [param param].

methods.name: get_texture
methods.description: Returns the [Texture2D] associated with the specified texture [param param].

properties.name: transparency
properties.description: The material's transparency mode. Some transparency modes will disable shadow casting. Any transparency mode other than [constant TRANSPARENCY_DISABLED] has a greater performance impact compared to opaque rendering. See also [member blend_mode].

properties.name: alpha_scissor_threshold
properties.description: Threshold at which the alpha scissor will discard values. Higher values will result in more pixels being discarded. If the material becomes too opaque at a distance, try increasing [member alpha_scissor_threshold]. If the material disappears at a distance, try decreasing [member alpha_scissor_threshold].

properties.name: alpha_hash_scale
properties.description: The hashing scale for Alpha Hash. Recommended values between [code]0[/code] and [code]2[/code].

properties.name: alpha_antialiasing_mode
properties.description: The type of alpha antialiasing to apply.

properties.name: alpha_antialiasing_edge
properties.description: Threshold at which antialiasing will be applied on the alpha channel.

properties.name: blend_mode
properties.description:
The material's blend mode.
[b]Note:[/b] Values other than [code]Mix[/code] force the object into the transparent pipeline.

properties.name: cull_mode
properties.description: Determines which side of the triangle to cull depending on whether the triangle faces towards or away from the camera.

properties.name: depth_draw_mode
properties.description: Determines when depth rendering takes place. See also [member transparency].

properties.name: no_depth_test
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], depth testing is disabled and the object will be drawn in render order.

properties.name: depth_test
properties.description:
Determines which comparison operator is used when testing depth.
[b]Note:[/b] Changing [member depth_test] to a non-default value only has a visible effect when used on a transparent material, or a material that has [member depth_draw_mode] set to [constant DEPTH_DRAW_DISABLED].

properties.name: shading_mode
properties.description: Sets whether the shading takes place, per-pixel, per-vertex or unshaded. Per-vertex lighting is faster, making it the best choice for mobile applications, however it looks considerably worse than per-pixel. Unshaded rendering is the fastest, but disables all interactions with lights.

properties.name: diffuse_mode
properties.description: The algorithm used for diffuse light scattering.

properties.name: specular_mode
properties.description:
The method for rendering the specular blob.
[b]Note:[/b] [member specular_mode] only applies to the specular blob. It does not affect specular reflections from the sky, screen-space reflections, [VoxelGI], SDFGI or [ReflectionProbe]s. To disable reflections from these sources as well, set [member metallic_specular] to [code]0.0[/code] instead.

properties.name: disable_ambient_light
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the object receives no ambient light.

properties.name: disable_fog
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the object will not be affected by fog (neither volumetric nor depth fog). This is useful for unshaded or transparent materials (e.g. particles), which without this setting will be affected even if fully transparent.

properties.name: disable_specular_occlusion
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], disables specular occlusion even if [member ProjectSettings.rendering/reflections/specular_occlusion/enabled] is [code]false[/code].

properties.name: vertex_color_use_as_albedo
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the vertex color is used as albedo color.

properties.name: vertex_color_is_srgb
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], vertex colors are considered to be stored in nonlinear sRGB encoding and are converted to linear encoding during rendering. If [code]false[/code], vertex colors are considered to be stored in linear encoding and are rendered as-is. See also [member albedo_texture_force_srgb].
[b]Note:[/b] Only effective when using the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, not Compatibility.

properties.name: albedo_color
properties.description:
The material's base color.
[b]Note:[/b] If [member detail_enabled] is [code]true[/code] and a [member detail_albedo] texture is specified, [member albedo_color] will [i]not[/i] modulate the detail texture. This can be used to color partial areas of a material by not specifying an albedo texture and using a transparent [member detail_albedo] texture instead.

properties.name: albedo_texture
properties.description:
Texture to multiply by [member albedo_color]. Used for basic texturing of objects.
If the texture appears unexpectedly too dark or too bright, check [member albedo_texture_force_srgb].

properties.name: albedo_texture_force_srgb
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], forces a conversion of the [member albedo_texture] from nonlinear sRGB encoding to linear encoding. See also [member vertex_color_is_srgb].
This should only be enabled when needed (typically when using a [ViewportTexture] as [member albedo_texture]). If [member albedo_texture_force_srgb] is [code]true[/code] when it shouldn't be, the texture will appear to be too dark. If [member albedo_texture_force_srgb] is [code]false[/code] when it shouldn't be, the texture will appear to be too bright.

properties.name: albedo_texture_msdf
properties.description: Enables multichannel signed distance field rendering shader. Use [member msdf_pixel_range] and [member msdf_outline_size] to configure MSDF parameters.

properties.name: orm_texture
properties.description: The Occlusion/Roughness/Metallic texture to use. This is a more efficient replacement of [member ao_texture], [member roughness_texture] and [member metallic_texture] in [ORMMaterial3D]. Ambient occlusion is stored in the red channel. Roughness map is stored in the green channel. Metallic map is stored in the blue channel. The alpha channel is ignored.

properties.name: metallic
properties.description: A high value makes the material appear more like a metal. Non-metals use their albedo as the diffuse color and add diffuse to the specular reflection. With non-metals, the reflection appears on top of the albedo color. Metals use their albedo as a multiplier to the specular reflection and set the diffuse color to black resulting in a tinted reflection. Materials work better when fully metal or fully non-metal, values between [code]0[/code] and [code]1[/code] should only be used for blending between metal and non-metal sections. To alter the amount of reflection use [member roughness].

properties.name: metallic_specular
properties.description:
Adjusts the strength of specular reflections. Specular reflections are composed of scene reflections and the specular lobe which is the bright spot that is reflected from light sources. When set to [code]0.0[/code], no specular reflections will be visible. This differs from the [constant SPECULAR_DISABLED] [enum SpecularMode] as [constant SPECULAR_DISABLED] only applies to the specular lobe from the light source.
[b]Note:[/b] Unlike [member metallic], this is not energy-conserving, so it should be left at [code]0.5[/code] in most cases. See also [member roughness].

properties.name: metallic_texture
properties.description: Texture used to specify metallic for an object. This is multiplied by [member metallic].

properties.name: metallic_texture_channel
properties.description: Specifies the channel of the [member metallic_texture] in which the metallic information is stored. This is useful when you store the information for multiple effects in a single texture. For example if you stored metallic in the red channel, roughness in the blue, and ambient occlusion in the green you could reduce the number of textures you use.

properties.name: roughness
properties.description: Surface reflection. A value of [code]0[/code] represents a perfect mirror while a value of [code]1[/code] completely blurs the reflection. See also [member metallic].

properties.name: roughness_texture
properties.description: Texture used to control the roughness per-pixel. Multiplied by [member roughness].

properties.name: roughness_texture_channel
properties.description: Specifies the channel of the [member roughness_texture] in which the roughness information is stored. This is useful when you store the information for multiple effects in a single texture. For example if you stored metallic in the red channel, roughness in the blue, and ambient occlusion in the green you could reduce the number of textures you use.

properties.name: emission_enabled
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the body emits light. Emitting light makes the object appear brighter. The object can also cast light on other objects if a [VoxelGI], SDFGI, or [LightmapGI] is used and this object is used in baked lighting.

properties.name: emission
properties.description: The emitted light's color. See [member emission_enabled].

properties.name: emission_energy_multiplier
properties.description: Multiplier for emitted light. See [member emission_enabled].

properties.name: emission_intensity
properties.description: Luminance of emitted light, measured in nits (candela per square meter). Only available when [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units] is enabled. The default is roughly equivalent to an indoor lightbulb.

properties.name: emission_operator
properties.description: Sets how [member emission] interacts with [member emission_texture]. Can either add or multiply.

properties.name: emission_on_uv2
properties.description: Use [code]UV2[/code] to read from the [member emission_texture].

properties.name: emission_texture
properties.description: Texture that specifies how much surface emits light at a given point.

properties.name: normal_enabled
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], normal mapping is enabled. This has a slight performance cost, especially on mobile GPUs.

properties.name: normal_scale
properties.description: The strength of the normal map's effect.

properties.name: normal_texture
properties.description:
Texture used to specify the normal at a given pixel. The [member normal_texture] only uses the red and green channels; the blue and alpha channels are ignored. The normal read from [member normal_texture] is oriented around the surface normal provided by the [Mesh].
[b]Note:[/b] The mesh must have both normals and tangents defined in its vertex data. Otherwise, the normal map won't render correctly and will only appear to darken the whole surface. If creating geometry with [SurfaceTool], you can use [method SurfaceTool.generate_normals] and [method SurfaceTool.generate_tangents] to automatically generate normals and tangents respectively.
[b]Note:[/b] Godot expects the normal map to use X+, Y+, and Z+ coordinates. See [url=http://wiki.polycount.com/wiki/Normal_Map_Technical_Details#Common_Swizzle_Coordinates]this page[/url] for a comparison of normal map coordinates expected by popular engines.
[b]Note:[/b] If [member detail_enabled] is [code]true[/code], the [member detail_albedo] texture is drawn [i]below[/i] the [member normal_texture]. To display a normal map [i]above[/i] the [member detail_albedo] texture, use [member detail_normal] instead.

properties.name: bent_normal_enabled
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the bent normal map is enabled. This allows for more accurate indirect lighting and specular occlusion.

properties.name: bent_normal_texture
properties.description:
Texture that specifies the average direction of incoming ambient light at a given pixel. The [member bent_normal_texture] only uses the red and green channels; the blue and alpha channels are ignored. The normal read from [member bent_normal_texture] is oriented around the surface normal provided by the [Mesh].
[b]Note:[/b] A bent normal map is different from a regular normal map. When baking a bent normal map make sure to use [b]a cosine distribution[/b] for the bent normal map to work correctly.
[b]Note:[/b] The mesh must have both normals and tangents defined in its vertex data. Otherwise, the shading produced by the bent normal map will not look correct. If creating geometry with [SurfaceTool], you can use [method SurfaceTool.generate_normals] and [method SurfaceTool.generate_tangents] to automatically generate normals and tangents respectively.
[b]Note:[/b] Godot expects the bent normal map to use X+, Y+, and Z+ coordinates. See [url=http://wiki.polycount.com/wiki/Normal_Map_Technical_Details#Common_Swizzle_Coordinates]this page[/url] for a comparison of normal map coordinates expected by popular engines.

properties.name: rim_enabled
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], rim effect is enabled. Rim lighting increases the brightness at glancing angles on an object.
[b]Note:[/b] Rim lighting is not visible if the material's [member shading_mode] is [constant SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED].

properties.name: rim
properties.description: Sets the strength of the rim lighting effect.

properties.name: rim_tint
properties.description: The amount of to blend light and albedo color when rendering rim effect. If [code]0[/code] the light color is used, while [code]1[/code] means albedo color is used. An intermediate value generally works best.

properties.name: rim_texture
properties.description: Texture used to set the strength of the rim lighting effect per-pixel. Multiplied by [member rim].

properties.name: clearcoat_enabled
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], clearcoat rendering is enabled. Adds a secondary transparent pass to the lighting calculation resulting in an added specular blob. This makes materials appear as if they have a clear layer on them that can be either glossy or rough.
[b]Note:[/b] Clearcoat rendering is not visible if the material's [member shading_mode] is [constant SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED].

properties.name: clearcoat
properties.description: Sets the strength of the clearcoat effect. Setting to [code]0[/code] looks the same as disabling the clearcoat effect.

properties.name: clearcoat_roughness
properties.description: Sets the roughness of the clearcoat pass. A higher value results in a rougher clearcoat while a lower value results in a smoother clearcoat.

properties.name: clearcoat_texture
properties.description: Texture that defines the strength of the clearcoat effect and the glossiness of the clearcoat. Strength is specified in the red channel while glossiness is specified in the green channel.

properties.name: anisotropy_enabled
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], anisotropy is enabled. Anisotropy changes the shape of the specular blob and aligns it to tangent space. This is useful for brushed aluminum and hair reflections.
[b]Note:[/b] Mesh tangents are needed for anisotropy to work. If the mesh does not contain tangents, the anisotropy effect will appear broken.
[b]Note:[/b] Material anisotropy should not to be confused with anisotropic texture filtering, which can be enabled by setting [member texture_filter] to [constant TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS_ANISOTROPIC].

properties.name: anisotropy
properties.description: The strength of the anisotropy effect. This is multiplied by [member anisotropy_flowmap]'s alpha channel if a texture is defined there and the texture contains an alpha channel.

properties.name: anisotropy_flowmap
properties.description:
Texture that offsets the tangent map for anisotropy calculations and optionally controls the anisotropy effect (if an alpha channel is present). The flowmap texture is expected to be a derivative map, with the red channel representing distortion on the X axis and green channel representing distortion on the Y axis. Values below 0.5 will result in negative distortion, whereas values above 0.5 will result in positive distortion.
If present, the texture's alpha channel will be used to multiply the strength of the [member anisotropy] effect. Fully opaque pixels will keep the anisotropy effect's original strength while fully transparent pixels will disable the anisotropy effect entirely. The flowmap texture's blue channel is ignored.

properties.name: ao_enabled
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], ambient occlusion is enabled. Ambient occlusion darkens areas based on the [member ao_texture].

properties.name: ao_light_affect
properties.description: Amount that ambient occlusion affects lighting from lights. If [code]0[/code], ambient occlusion only affects ambient light. If [code]1[/code], ambient occlusion affects lights just as much as it affects ambient light. This can be used to impact the strength of the ambient occlusion effect, but typically looks unrealistic.

properties.name: ao_texture
properties.description: Texture that defines the amount of ambient occlusion for a given point on the object.

properties.name: ao_on_uv2
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], use [code]UV2[/code] coordinates to look up from the [member ao_texture].

properties.name: ao_texture_channel
properties.description: Specifies the channel of the [member ao_texture] in which the ambient occlusion information is stored. This is useful when you store the information for multiple effects in a single texture. For example if you stored metallic in the red channel, roughness in the blue, and ambient occlusion in the green you could reduce the number of textures you use.

properties.name: heightmap_enabled
properties.description:
