If [code]true[/code], height mapping is enabled (also called "parallax mapping" or "depth mapping"). See also [member normal_enabled]. Height mapping is a demanding feature on the GPU, so it should only be used on materials where it makes a significant visual difference.
[b]Note:[/b] Height mapping is not supported if triplanar mapping is used on the same material. The value of [member heightmap_enabled] will be ignored if [member uv1_triplanar] is enabled.

properties.name: heightmap_scale
properties.description:
The heightmap scale to use for the parallax effect (see [member heightmap_enabled]). The default value is tuned so that the highest point (value = 255) appears to be 5 cm higher than the lowest point (value = 0). Higher values result in a deeper appearance, but may result in artifacts appearing when looking at the material from oblique angles, especially when the camera moves. Negative values can be used to invert the parallax effect, but this is different from inverting the texture using [member heightmap_flip_texture] as the material will also appear to be "closer" to the camera. In most cases, [member heightmap_scale] should be kept to a positive value.
[b]Note:[/b] If the height map effect looks strange regardless of this value, try adjusting [member heightmap_flip_binormal] and [member heightmap_flip_tangent]. See also [member heightmap_texture] for recommendations on authoring heightmap textures, as the way the heightmap texture is authored affects how [member heightmap_scale] behaves.

properties.name: heightmap_deep_parallax
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], uses parallax occlusion mapping to represent depth in the material instead of simple offset mapping (see [member heightmap_enabled]). This results in a more convincing depth effect, but is much more expensive on the GPU. Only enable this on materials where it makes a significant visual difference.

properties.name: heightmap_min_layers
properties.description:
The number of layers to use for parallax occlusion mapping when the camera is far away from the material. Higher values result in a more convincing depth effect, especially in materials that have steep height changes. Higher values have a significant cost on the GPU, so it should only be increased on materials where it makes a significant visual difference.
[b]Note:[/b] Only effective if [member heightmap_deep_parallax] is [code]true[/code].

properties.name: heightmap_max_layers
properties.description:
The number of layers to use for parallax occlusion mapping when the camera is up close to the material. Higher values result in a more convincing depth effect, especially in materials that have steep height changes. Higher values have a significant cost on the GPU, so it should only be increased on materials where it makes a significant visual difference.
[b]Note:[/b] Only effective if [member heightmap_deep_parallax] is [code]true[/code].

properties.name: heightmap_flip_tangent
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], flips the mesh's tangent vectors when interpreting the height map. If the heightmap effect looks strange when the camera moves (even with a reasonable [member heightmap_scale]), try setting this to [code]true[/code].

properties.name: heightmap_flip_binormal
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], flips the mesh's binormal vectors when interpreting the height map. If the heightmap effect looks strange when the camera moves (even with a reasonable [member heightmap_scale]), try setting this to [code]true[/code].

properties.name: heightmap_texture
properties.description:
The texture to use as a height map. See also [member heightmap_enabled].
For best results, the texture should be normalized (with [member heightmap_scale] reduced to compensate). In [url=https://gimp.org]GIMP[/url], this can be done using [b]Colors > Auto > Equalize[/b]. If the texture only uses a small part of its available range, the parallax effect may look strange, especially when the camera moves.
[b]Note:[/b] To reduce memory usage and improve loading times, you may be able to use a lower-resolution heightmap texture as most heightmaps are only comprised of low-frequency data.

properties.name: heightmap_flip_texture
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], interprets the height map texture as a depth map, with brighter values appearing to be "lower" in altitude compared to darker values.
This can be enabled for compatibility with some materials authored for Godot 3.x. This is not necessary if the Invert import option was used to invert the depth map in Godot 3.x, in which case [member heightmap_flip_texture] should remain [code]false[/code].

properties.name: subsurf_scatter_enabled
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], subsurface scattering is enabled. Emulates light that penetrates an object's surface, is scattered, and then emerges. Subsurface scattering quality is controlled by [member ProjectSettings.rendering/environment/subsurface_scattering/subsurface_scattering_quality].
[b]Note:[/b] Subsurface scattering is not supported on viewports that have a transparent background (where [member Viewport.transparent_bg] is [code]true[/code]).

properties.name: subsurf_scatter_strength
properties.description: The strength of the subsurface scattering effect. The depth of the effect is also controlled by [member ProjectSettings.rendering/environment/subsurface_scattering/subsurface_scattering_scale], which is set globally.

properties.name: subsurf_scatter_skin_mode
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], subsurface scattering will use a special mode optimized for the color and density of human skin, such as boosting the intensity of the red channel in subsurface scattering.

properties.name: subsurf_scatter_texture
properties.description: Texture used to control the subsurface scattering strength. Stored in the red texture channel. Multiplied by [member subsurf_scatter_strength].

properties.name: subsurf_scatter_transmittance_enabled
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], enables subsurface scattering transmittance. Only effective if [member subsurf_scatter_enabled] is [code]true[/code]. See also [member backlight_enabled].

properties.name: subsurf_scatter_transmittance_color
properties.description: The color to multiply the subsurface scattering transmittance effect with. Ignored if [member subsurf_scatter_skin_mode] is [code]true[/code].

properties.name: subsurf_scatter_transmittance_texture
properties.description: The texture to use for multiplying the intensity of the subsurface scattering transmittance intensity. See also [member subsurf_scatter_texture]. Ignored if [member subsurf_scatter_skin_mode] is [code]true[/code].

properties.name: subsurf_scatter_transmittance_depth
properties.description: The depth of the subsurface scattering transmittance effect.

properties.name: subsurf_scatter_transmittance_boost
properties.description: The intensity of the subsurface scattering transmittance effect.

properties.name: backlight_enabled
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the backlight effect is enabled. See also [member subsurf_scatter_transmittance_enabled].

properties.name: backlight
properties.description: The color used by the backlight effect. Represents the light passing through an object.

properties.name: backlight_texture
properties.description: Texture used to control the backlight effect per-pixel. Added to [member backlight].

properties.name: refraction_enabled
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], the refraction effect is enabled. Distorts transparency based on light from behind the object.
[b]Note:[/b] Refraction is implemented using the screen texture. Only opaque materials will appear in the refraction, since transparent materials do not appear in the screen texture.

properties.name: refraction_scale
properties.description: The strength of the refraction effect.

properties.name: refraction_texture
properties.description: Texture that controls the strength of the refraction per-pixel. Multiplied by [member refraction_scale].

properties.name: refraction_texture_channel
properties.description: Specifies the channel of the [member refraction_texture] in which the refraction information is stored. This is useful when you store the information for multiple effects in a single texture. For example if you stored refraction in the red channel, roughness in the blue, and ambient occlusion in the green you could reduce the number of textures you use.

properties.name: detail_enabled
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], enables the detail overlay. Detail is a second texture that gets mixed over the surface of the object based on [member detail_mask] and [member detail_albedo]'s alpha channel. This can be used to add variation to objects, or to blend between two different albedo/normal textures.

properties.name: detail_mask
properties.description: Texture used to specify how the detail textures get blended with the base textures. [member detail_mask] can be used together with [member detail_albedo]'s alpha channel (if any).

properties.name: detail_blend_mode
properties.description: Specifies how the [member detail_albedo] should blend with the current [code]ALBEDO[/code].

properties.name: detail_uv_layer
properties.description: Specifies whether to use [code]UV[/code] or [code]UV2[/code] for the detail layer.

properties.name: detail_albedo
properties.description:
Texture that specifies the color of the detail overlay. [member detail_albedo]'s alpha channel is used as a mask, even when the material is opaque. To use a dedicated texture as a mask, see [member detail_mask].
[b]Note:[/b] [member detail_albedo] is [i]not[/i] modulated by [member albedo_color].

properties.name: detail_normal
properties.description:
Texture that specifies the per-pixel normal of the detail overlay. The [member detail_normal] texture only uses the red and green channels; the blue and alpha channels are ignored. The normal read from [member detail_normal] is oriented around the surface normal provided by the [Mesh].
[b]Note:[/b] Godot expects the normal map to use X+, Y+, and Z+ coordinates. See [url=http://wiki.polycount.com/wiki/Normal_Map_Technical_Details#Common_Swizzle_Coordinates]this page[/url] for a comparison of normal map coordinates expected by popular engines.

properties.name: uv1_scale
properties.description: How much to scale the [code]UV[/code] coordinates. This is multiplied by [code]UV[/code] in the vertex function. The Z component is used when [member uv1_triplanar] is enabled, but it is not used anywhere else.

properties.name: uv1_offset
properties.description: How much to offset the [code]UV[/code] coordinates. This amount will be added to [code]UV[/code] in the vertex function. This can be used to offset a texture. The Z component is used when [member uv1_triplanar] is enabled, but it is not used anywhere else.

properties.name: uv1_triplanar
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], instead of using [code]UV[/code] textures will use a triplanar texture lookup to determine how to apply textures. Triplanar uses the orientation of the object's surface to blend between texture coordinates. It reads from the source texture 3 times, once for each axis and then blends between the results based on how closely the pixel aligns with each axis. This is often used for natural features to get a realistic blend of materials. Because triplanar texturing requires many more texture reads per-pixel it is much slower than normal UV texturing. Additionally, because it is blending the texture between the three axes, it is unsuitable when you are trying to achieve crisp texturing.

properties.name: uv1_triplanar_sharpness
properties.description:
A lower number blends the texture more softly while a higher number blends the texture more sharply.
[b]Note:[/b] [member uv1_triplanar_sharpness] is clamped between [code]0.0[/code] and [code]150.0[/code] (inclusive) as values outside that range can look broken depending on the mesh.

properties.name: uv1_world_triplanar
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], triplanar mapping for [code]UV[/code] is calculated in world space rather than object local space. See also [member uv1_triplanar].

properties.name: uv2_scale
properties.description: How much to scale the [code]UV2[/code] coordinates. This is multiplied by [code]UV2[/code] in the vertex function. The Z component is used when [member uv2_triplanar] is enabled, but it is not used anywhere else.

properties.name: uv2_offset
properties.description: How much to offset the [code]UV2[/code] coordinates. This amount will be added to [code]UV2[/code] in the vertex function. This can be used to offset a texture. The Z component is used when [member uv2_triplanar] is enabled, but it is not used anywhere else.

properties.name: uv2_triplanar
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], instead of using [code]UV2[/code] textures will use a triplanar texture lookup to determine how to apply textures. Triplanar uses the orientation of the object's surface to blend between texture coordinates. It reads from the source texture 3 times, once for each axis and then blends between the results based on how closely the pixel aligns with each axis. This is often used for natural features to get a realistic blend of materials. Because triplanar texturing requires many more texture reads per-pixel it is much slower than normal UV texturing. Additionally, because it is blending the texture between the three axes, it is unsuitable when you are trying to achieve crisp texturing.

properties.name: uv2_triplanar_sharpness
properties.description:
A lower number blends the texture more softly while a higher number blends the texture more sharply.
[b]Note:[/b] [member uv2_triplanar_sharpness] is clamped between [code]0.0[/code] and [code]150.0[/code] (inclusive) as values outside that range can look broken depending on the mesh.

properties.name: uv2_world_triplanar
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], triplanar mapping for [code]UV2[/code] is calculated in world space rather than object local space. See also [member uv2_triplanar].

properties.name: texture_filter
properties.description:
Filter flags for the texture.
[b]Note:[/b] [member heightmap_texture] is always sampled with linear filtering, even if nearest-neighbor filtering is selected here. This is to ensure the heightmap effect looks as intended. If you need sharper height transitions between pixels, resize the heightmap texture in an image editor with nearest-neighbor filtering.

properties.name: texture_repeat
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the texture repeats when exceeding the texture's size. See [constant FLAG_USE_TEXTURE_REPEAT].

properties.name: disable_receive_shadows
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the object receives no shadow that would otherwise be cast onto it.

properties.name: shadow_to_opacity
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], enables the "shadow to opacity" render mode where lighting modifies the alpha so shadowed areas are opaque and non-shadowed areas are transparent. Useful for overlaying shadows onto a camera feed in AR.

properties.name: billboard_mode
properties.description:
Controls how the object faces the camera.
[b]Note:[/b] Billboard mode is not suitable for VR because the left-right vector of the camera is not horizontal when the screen is attached to your head instead of on the table. See [url=https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/41567]GitHub issue #41567[/url] for details.

properties.name: billboard_keep_scale
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the shader will keep the scale set for the mesh. Otherwise, the scale is lost when billboarding. Only applies when [member billboard_mode] is not [constant BILLBOARD_DISABLED].

properties.name: particles_anim_h_frames
properties.description: The number of horizontal frames in the particle sprite sheet. Only enabled when using [constant BILLBOARD_PARTICLES]. See [member billboard_mode].

properties.name: particles_anim_v_frames
properties.description: The number of vertical frames in the particle sprite sheet. Only enabled when using [constant BILLBOARD_PARTICLES]. See [member billboard_mode].

properties.name: particles_anim_loop
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], particle animations are looped. Only enabled when using [constant BILLBOARD_PARTICLES]. See [member billboard_mode].

properties.name: grow
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], enables the vertex grow setting. This can be used to create mesh-based outlines using a second material pass and its [member cull_mode] set to [constant CULL_FRONT]. See also [member grow_amount].
[b]Note:[/b] Vertex growth cannot create new vertices, which means that visible gaps may occur in sharp corners. This can be alleviated by designing the mesh to use smooth normals exclusively using [url=http://wiki.polycount.com/wiki/Face_weighted_normals]face weighted normals[/url] in the 3D authoring software. In this case, grow will be able to join every outline together, just like in the original mesh.

properties.name: grow_amount
properties.description: Grows object vertices in the direction of their normals. Only effective if [member grow] is [code]true[/code].

properties.name: fixed_size
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the object is rendered at the same size regardless of distance. The object's size on screen is the same as if the camera was [code]1.0[/code] units away from the object's origin, regardless of the actual distance from the camera. The [Camera3D]'s field of view (or [member Camera3D.size] when in orthogonal/frustum mode) still affects the size the object is drawn at.

properties.name: use_point_size
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], render point size can be changed.
[b]Note:[/b] This is only effective for objects whose geometry is point-based rather than triangle-based. See also [member point_size].

properties.name: point_size
properties.description: The point size in pixels. See [member use_point_size].

properties.name: use_particle_trails
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], enables parts of the shader required for [GPUParticles3D] trails to function. This also requires using a mesh with appropriate skinning, such as [RibbonTrailMesh] or [TubeTrailMesh]. Enabling this feature outside of materials used in [GPUParticles3D] meshes will break material rendering.

properties.name: use_z_clip_scale
properties.description: If [code]true[/code] use [member z_clip_scale] to scale the object being rendered towards the camera to avoid clipping into things like walls.

properties.name: z_clip_scale
properties.description: Scales the object being rendered towards the camera to avoid clipping into things like walls. This is intended to be used for objects that are fixed with respect to the camera like player arms, tools, etc. Lighting and shadows will continue to work correctly when this setting is adjusted, but screen-space effects like SSAO and SSR may break with lower scales. Therefore, try to keep this setting as close to [code]1.0[/code] as possible.

properties.name: use_fov_override
properties.description: If [code]true[/code] use [member fov_override] to override the [Camera3D]'s field of view angle.

properties.name: fov_override
properties.description:
Overrides the [Camera3D]'s field of view angle (in degrees).
[b]Note:[/b] This behaves as if the field of view is set on a [Camera3D] with [member Camera3D.keep_aspect] set to [constant Camera3D.KEEP_HEIGHT]. Additionally, it may not look correct on a non-perspective camera where the field of view setting is ignored.

properties.name: proximity_fade_enabled
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the proximity fade effect is enabled. The proximity fade effect fades out each pixel based on its distance to another object.

properties.name: proximity_fade_distance
properties.description: Distance over which the fade effect takes place. The larger the distance the longer it takes for an object to fade.

properties.name: msdf_pixel_range
properties.description: The width of the range around the shape between the minimum and maximum representable signed distance.

properties.name: msdf_outline_size
properties.description: The width of the shape outline.

properties.name: distance_fade_mode
properties.description: Specifies which type of fade to use. Can be any of the [enum DistanceFadeMode]s.

properties.name: distance_fade_min_distance
properties.description:
Distance at which the object starts to become visible. If the object is less than this distance away, it will be invisible.
[b]Note:[/b] If [member distance_fade_min_distance] is greater than [member distance_fade_max_distance], the behavior will be reversed. The object will start to fade away at [member distance_fade_max_distance] and will fully disappear once it reaches [member distance_fade_min_distance].

properties.name: distance_fade_max_distance
properties.description:
Distance at which the object appears fully opaque.
[b]Note:[/b] If [member distance_fade_max_distance] is less than [member distance_fade_min_distance], the behavior will be reversed. The object will start to fade away at [member distance_fade_max_distance] and will fully disappear once it reaches [member distance_fade_min_distance].

properties.name: stencil_mode
properties.description: The stencil effect mode.

properties.name: stencil_flags
properties.description: The flags dictating how the stencil operation behaves.

properties.name: stencil_compare
properties.description: The comparison operator to use for stencil masking operations.

properties.name: stencil_reference
properties.description: The stencil reference value (0-255). Typically a power of 2.

properties.name: stencil_color
properties.description: The primary color of the stencil effect.

properties.name: stencil_outline_thickness
properties.description: The outline thickness for [constant STENCIL_MODE_OUTLINE].

classes.brief_description: Abstract base class for defining the 3D rendering properties of meshes.
classes.description: This class serves as a default material with a wide variety of rendering features and properties without the need to write shader code. See the tutorial below for details.

classes.name: BitMap

methods.name: create
methods.description: Creates a bitmap with the specified size, filled with [code]false[/code].

methods.name: create_from_image_alpha
methods.description: Creates a bitmap that matches the given image dimensions, every element of the bitmap is set to [code]false[/code] if the alpha value of the image at that position is equal to [param threshold] or less, and [code]true[/code] in other case.

methods.name: set_bitv
methods.description: Sets the bitmap's element at the specified position, to the specified value.

methods.name: set_bit
methods.description: Sets the bitmap's element at the specified position, to the specified value.

methods.name: get_bitv
methods.description: Returns bitmap's value at the specified position.

methods.name: get_bit
methods.description: Returns bitmap's value at the specified position.

methods.name: set_bit_rect
methods.description: Sets a rectangular portion of the bitmap to the specified value.

methods.name: get_true_bit_count
methods.description: Returns the number of bitmap elements that are set to [code]true[/code].

methods.name: get_size
methods.description: Returns bitmap's dimensions.

methods.name: resize
methods.description: Resizes the image to [param new_size].

methods.name: grow_mask
methods.description: Applies morphological dilation or erosion to the bitmap. If [param pixels] is positive, dilation is applied to the bitmap. If [param pixels] is negative, erosion is applied to the bitmap. [param rect] defines the area where the morphological operation is applied. Pixels located outside the [param rect] are unaffected by [method grow_mask].

methods.name: convert_to_image
methods.description: Returns an image of the same size as the bitmap and with an [enum Image.Format] of type [constant Image.FORMAT_L8]. [code]true[/code] bits of the bitmap are being converted into white pixels, and [code]false[/code] bits into black.

methods.name: opaque_to_polygons
methods.description:
Creates an [Array] of polygons covering a rectangular portion of the bitmap. It uses a marching squares algorithm, followed by Ramer-Douglas-Peucker (RDP) reduction of the number of vertices. Each polygon is described as a [PackedVector2Array] of its vertices.
To get polygons covering the whole bitmap, pass:
[codeblock]
Rect2(Vector2(), get_size())
[/codeblock]
[param epsilon] is passed to RDP to control how accurately the polygons cover the bitmap: a lower [param epsilon] corresponds to more points in the polygons.

classes.brief_description: Boolean matrix.
classes.description: A two-dimensional array of boolean values, can be used to efficiently store a binary matrix (every matrix element takes only one bit) and query the values using natural cartesian coordinates.

classes.name: BlitMaterial

values.name: BLEND_MODE_MIX
values.description: Mix blending mode. Colors are assumed to be independent of the alpha (opacity) value.

values.name: BLEND_MODE_ADD
values.description: Additive blending mode.

values.name: BLEND_MODE_SUB
values.description: Subtractive blending mode.

values.name: BLEND_MODE_MUL
values.description: Multiplicative blending mode.

values.name: BLEND_MODE_DISABLED
values.description: No blending mode, direct color copy.

properties.name: blend_mode
properties.description: The manner in which the newly blitted texture is blended with the original DrawableTexture.

classes.brief_description: A material that processes blit calls to a DrawableTexture.
classes.description: A material resource that can be used by DrawableTextures when processing blit calls to draw.

classes.name: Bone2D

methods.name: apply_rest
methods.description: Resets the bone to the rest pose. This is equivalent to setting [member Node2D.transform] to [member rest].

methods.name: get_skeleton_rest
methods.description: Returns the node's [member rest] [Transform2D] if it doesn't have a parent, or its rest pose relative to its parent.

methods.name: get_index_in_skeleton
methods.description: Returns the node's index as part of the entire skeleton. See [Skeleton2D].

methods.name: set_autocalculate_length_and_angle
methods.description: When set to [code]true[/code], the [Bone2D] node will attempt to automatically calculate the bone angle and length using the first child [Bone2D] node, if one exists. If none exist, the [Bone2D] cannot automatically calculate these values and will print a warning.

methods.name: get_autocalculate_length_and_angle
methods.description: Returns whether this [Bone2D] is going to autocalculate its length and bone angle using its first [Bone2D] child node, if one exists. If there are no [Bone2D] children, then it cannot autocalculate these values and will print a warning.

methods.name: set_length
methods.description: Sets the length of the bone in the [Bone2D].

methods.name: get_length
methods.description: Returns the length of the bone in the [Bone2D] node.

methods.name: set_bone_angle
methods.description:
Sets the bone angle for the [Bone2D]. This is typically set to the rotation from the [Bone2D] to a child [Bone2D] node.
[b]Note:[/b] This is different from the [Bone2D]'s rotation. The bone's angle is the rotation of the bone shown by the gizmo, which is unaffected by the [Bone2D]'s [member Node2D.transform].

methods.name: get_bone_angle
methods.description:
Returns the angle of the bone in the [Bone2D].
[b]Note:[/b] This is different from the [Bone2D]'s rotation. The bone's angle is the rotation of the bone shown by the gizmo, which is unaffected by the [Bone2D]'s [member Node2D.transform].

properties.name: rest
properties.description: Rest transform of the bone. You can reset the node's transforms to this value using [method apply_rest].

classes.brief_description: A joint used with [Skeleton2D] to control and animate other nodes.
classes.description:
A hierarchy of [Bone2D]s can be bound to a [Skeleton2D] to control and animate other [Node2D] nodes.
You can use [Bone2D] and [Skeleton2D] nodes to animate 2D meshes created with the [Polygon2D] UV editor.
Each bone has a [member rest] transform that you can reset to with [method apply_rest]. These rest poses are relative to the bone's parent.
If in the editor, you can set the rest pose of an entire skeleton using a menu option, from the code, you need to iterate over the bones to set their individual rest poses.

classes.name: BoneAttachment3D

methods.name: get_skeleton
methods.description: Returns the parent or external [Skeleton3D] node if it exists, otherwise returns [code]null[/code].

methods.name: on_skeleton_update
methods.description: A function that is called automatically when the [Skeleton3D] is updated. This function is where the [BoneAttachment3D] node updates its position so it is correctly bound when it is [i]not[/i] set to override the bone pose.

properties.name: bone_name
properties.description: The name of the attached bone.

properties.name: bone_idx
properties.description: The index of the attached bone.

properties.name: override_pose
properties.description:
Whether the [BoneAttachment3D] node will override the bone pose of the bone it is attached to. When set to [code]true[/code], the [BoneAttachment3D] node can change the pose of the bone. When set to [code]false[/code], the [BoneAttachment3D] will always be set to the bone's transform.
[b]Note:[/b] This override performs interruptively in the skeleton update process using signals due to the old design. It may cause unintended behavior when used at the same time with [SkeletonModifier3D].

properties.name: use_external_skeleton
properties.description: Whether the [BoneAttachment3D] node will use an external [Skeleton3D] node rather than attempting to use its parent node as the [Skeleton3D]. When set to [code]true[/code], the [BoneAttachment3D] node will use the external [Skeleton3D] node set in [member external_skeleton].

properties.name: external_skeleton
properties.description: The [NodePath] to the external [Skeleton3D] node.

classes.brief_description: А node that dynamically copies or overrides the 3D transform of a bone in its parent [Skeleton3D].
classes.description: This node selects a bone in a [Skeleton3D] and attaches to it. This means that the [BoneAttachment3D] node will either dynamically copy or override the 3D transform of the selected bone.

classes.name: BoneConstraint3D

values.name: REFERENCE_TYPE_BONE
values.description: The reference target is a bone. In this case, the reference target spaces is local space.

values.name: REFERENCE_TYPE_NODE
values.description:
The reference target is a [Node3D]. In this case, the reference target spaces is model space.
In other words, the reference target's coordinates are treated as if it were placed directly under [Skeleton3D] which parent of the [BoneConstraint3D].

methods.name: set_amount
methods.description: Sets the apply amount of the setting at [param index] to [param amount].

methods.name: get_amount
methods.description: Returns the apply amount of the setting at [param index].

methods.name: set_apply_bone_name
methods.description: Sets the apply bone of the setting at [param index] to [param bone_name]. This bone will be modified.

methods.name: get_apply_bone_name
methods.description: Returns the apply bone name of the setting at [param index]. This bone will be modified.

methods.name: set_apply_bone
methods.description: Sets the apply bone of the setting at [param index] to [param bone]. This bone will be modified.

methods.name: get_apply_bone
methods.description: Returns the apply bone of the setting at [param index]. This bone will be modified.

methods.name: set_reference_type
methods.description: Sets the reference target type of the setting at [param index] to [param type]. See also [enum ReferenceType].

methods.name: get_reference_type
methods.description: Returns the reference target type of the setting at [param index]. See also [enum ReferenceType].

methods.name: set_reference_bone_name
methods.description:
Sets the reference bone of the setting at [param index] to [param bone_name].
This bone will be only referenced and not modified by this modifier.

methods.name: get_reference_bone_name
methods.description:
Returns the reference bone name of the setting at [param index].
This bone will be only referenced and not modified by this modifier.

methods.name: set_reference_bone
methods.description:
Sets the reference bone of the setting at [param index] to [param bone].
This bone will be only referenced and not modified by this modifier.

methods.name: get_reference_bone
methods.description:
Returns the reference bone of the setting at [param index].
This bone will be only referenced and not modified by this modifier.

methods.name: set_reference_node
methods.description:
Sets the reference node path of the setting at [param index] to [param node].
This node will be only referenced and not modified by this modifier.

methods.name: get_reference_node
methods.description:
Returns the reference node path of the setting at [param index].
This node will be only referenced and not modified by this modifier.

methods.name: set_setting_count
methods.description: Sets the number of settings in the modifier.

methods.name: get_setting_count
methods.description: Returns the number of settings in the modifier.

methods.name: clear_setting
methods.description: Clear all settings.

classes.brief_description: A node that may modify Skeleton3D's bone with associating the two bones.
classes.description:
Base class of [SkeletonModifier3D] that modifies the bone set in [method set_apply_bone] based on the transform of the bone retrieved by [method get_reference_bone].
[b]Note:[/b] Most methods in this class take an [code]index[/code] parameter. This parameter specifies which setting list entry to return if the IK has multiple entries (e.g. [code]settings/<index>/amount[/code]).

classes.name: BoneMap

methods.name: get_skeleton_bone_name
methods.description:
Returns a skeleton bone name is mapped to [param profile_bone_name].
In the retargeting process, the returned bone name is the bone name of the source skeleton.

methods.name: set_skeleton_bone_name
methods.description:
Maps a skeleton bone name to [param profile_bone_name].
In the retargeting process, the setting bone name is the bone name of the source skeleton.

methods.name: find_profile_bone_name
methods.description:
Returns a profile bone name having [param skeleton_bone_name]. If not found, an empty [StringName] will be returned.
In the retargeting process, the returned bone name is the bone name of the target skeleton.

signals.name: bone_map_updated
signals.description: This signal is emitted when change the key value in the [BoneMap]. This is used to validate mapping and to update [BoneMap] editor.

signals.name: profile_updated
signals.description: This signal is emitted when change the value in profile or change the reference of profile. This is used to update key names in the [BoneMap] and to redraw the [BoneMap] editor.

properties.name: profile
properties.description: A [SkeletonProfile] of the mapping target. Key names in the [BoneMap] are synchronized with it.

classes.brief_description: Describes a mapping of bone names for retargeting [Skeleton3D] into common names defined by a [SkeletonProfile].
classes.description:
This class contains a dictionary that uses a list of bone names in [SkeletonProfile] as key names.
By assigning the actual [Skeleton3D] bone name as the key value, it maps the [Skeleton3D] to the [SkeletonProfile].

classes.name: BoneTwistDisperser3D

values.name: DISPERSE_MODE_EVEN
values.description: Assign amounts so that they monotonically increase from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code], ensuring all weights are equal. For example, with five joints, the amounts would be [code]0.2[/code], [code]0.4[/code], [code]0.6[/code], [code]0.8[/code], and [code]1.0[/code] starting from the root bone.

values.name: DISPERSE_MODE_WEIGHTED
values.description: Assign amounts so that they monotonically increase from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code], based on the length of the bones between joint segments. See also [method set_weight_position].

values.name: DISPERSE_MODE_CUSTOM
values.description:
You can assign arbitrary amounts to the joint list. See also [method set_joint_twist_amount].
When [method is_end_bone_extended] is [code]false[/code], a child of the reference bone exists solely to determine the twist axis, so its custom amount has absolutely no effect at all.

methods.name: clear_settings
methods.description: Clears all settings.

methods.name: set_root_bone_name
methods.description: Sets the root bone name of the bone chain.

methods.name: get_root_bone_name
methods.description: Returns the root bone name of the bone chain.

methods.name: set_root_bone
methods.description: Sets the root bone index of the bone chain.

methods.name: get_root_bone
methods.description: Returns the root bone index of the bone chain.

methods.name: set_end_bone_name
methods.description:
Sets the end bone name of the bone chain.
[b]Note:[/b] The end bone must be a child of the root bone.

methods.name: get_end_bone_name
methods.description: Returns the end bone name of the bone chain.

methods.name: set_end_bone
methods.description: Sets the end bone index of the bone chain.

methods.name: get_end_bone
methods.description: Returns the end bone index of the bone chain.

methods.name: get_reference_bone_name
methods.description:
Returns the reference bone name to extract twist of the setting at [param index].
This bone is either the end of the chain or its parent, depending on [method is_end_bone_extended].

methods.name: get_reference_bone
methods.description:
Returns the reference bone to extract twist of the setting at [param index].
This bone is either the end of the chain or its parent, depending on [method is_end_bone_extended].

methods.name: set_extend_end_bone
methods.description:
If [param enabled] is [code]true[/code], the end bone is extended to have a tail.
If [param enabled] is [code]false[/code], [method get_reference_bone] becomes a parent of the end bone and it uses the vector to the end bone as a twist axis.

methods.name: is_end_bone_extended
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the end bone is extended to have a tail.

methods.name: set_end_bone_direction
methods.description: Sets the end bone tail direction of the bone chain when [method is_end_bone_extended] is [code]true[/code].

methods.name: get_end_bone_direction
methods.description: Returns the tail direction of the end bone of the bone chain when [method is_end_bone_extended] is [code]true[/code].

methods.name: set_twist_from_rest
methods.description:
If [param enabled] is [code]true[/code], it extracts the twist amount from the difference between the bone rest and the current bone pose.
If [param enabled] is [code]false[/code], it extracts the twist amount from the difference between [method get_twist_from] and the current bone pose. See also [method set_twist_from].

methods.name: is_twist_from_rest
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if extracting the twist amount from the difference between the bone rest and the current bone pose.

methods.name: set_twist_from
methods.description:
Sets the rotation to an arbitrary state before twisting for the current bone pose to extract the twist when [method is_twist_from_rest] is [code]false[/code].
In other words, by calling [method set_twist_from] by [signal SkeletonModifier3D.modification_processed] of a specific [SkeletonModifier3D], you can extract only the twists generated by modifiers processed after that but before this [BoneTwistDisperser3D].

methods.name: get_twist_from
methods.description: Returns the rotation to an arbitrary state before twisting for the current bone pose to extract the twist when [method is_twist_from_rest] is [code]false[/code].

methods.name: set_disperse_mode
methods.description: Sets whether to use automatic amount assignment or to allow manual assignment.

methods.name: get_disperse_mode
methods.description: Returns whether to use automatic amount assignment or to allow manual assignment.

methods.name: set_weight_position
methods.description:
Sets the position at which to divide the segment between joints for weight assignment when [method get_disperse_mode] is [constant DISPERSE_MODE_WEIGHTED].
For example, when [param weight_position] is [code]0.5[/code], if two bone segments with a length of [code]1.0[/code] exist between three joints, weights are assigned to each joint from root to end at ratios of [code]0.5[/code], [code]1.0[/code], and [code]0.5[/code]. Then amounts become [code]0.25[/code], [code]0.75[/code], and [code]1.0[/code] respectively.

methods.name: get_weight_position
methods.description: Returns the position at which to divide the segment between joints for weight assignment when [method get_disperse_mode] is [constant DISPERSE_MODE_WEIGHTED].

methods.name: set_damping_curve
methods.description: Sets the damping curve when [method get_disperse_mode] is [constant DISPERSE_MODE_CUSTOM].

methods.name: get_damping_curve
methods.description: Returns the damping curve when [method get_disperse_mode] is [constant DISPERSE_MODE_CUSTOM].

methods.name: get_joint_bone_name
methods.description: Returns the bone name at [param joint] in the bone chain's joint list.

methods.name: get_joint_bone
methods.description: Returns the bone index at [param joint] in the bone chain's joint list.

methods.name: get_joint_twist_amount
methods.description: Returns the twist amount at [param joint] in the bone chain's joint list when [method get_disperse_mode] is [constant DISPERSE_MODE_CUSTOM].

methods.name: set_joint_twist_amount
methods.description: Sets the twist amount at [param joint] in the bone chain's joint list when [method get_disperse_mode] is [constant DISPERSE_MODE_CUSTOM].

methods.name: get_joint_count
methods.description: Returns the joint count of the bone chain's joint list.

properties.name: mutable_bone_axes
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], the solver retrieves the bone axis from the bone pose every frame.
If [code]false[/code], the solver retrieves the bone axis from the bone rest and caches it.

properties.name: setting_count
properties.description: The number of settings.

classes.brief_description: A node that propagates and disperses the child bone's twist to the parent bones.
classes.description:
This [BoneTwistDisperser3D] allows for smooth twist interpolation between multiple bones by dispersing the end bone's twist to the parents. This only changes the twist without changing the global position of each joint.
This is useful for smoothly twisting bones in combination with [CopyTransformModifier3D] and IK.
[b]Note:[/b] If an extracted twist is greater than 180 degrees, flipping occurs. This is similar to [ConvertTransformModifier3D].
[b]Note:[/b] Most methods in this class take an [code]index[/code] parameter. This parameter specifies which setting list entry to return if the IK has multiple entries (e.g. [code]settings/<index>/root_bone_name[/code]).

classes.name: BoxContainer

values.name: ALIGNMENT_BEGIN
values.description: The child controls will be arranged at the beginning of the container, i.e. top if orientation is vertical, left if orientation is horizontal (right for RTL layout).

values.name: ALIGNMENT_CENTER
values.description: The child controls will be centered in the container.

values.name: ALIGNMENT_END
values.description: The child controls will be arranged at the end of the container, i.e. bottom if orientation is vertical, right if orientation is horizontal (left for RTL layout).

methods.name: add_spacer
methods.description: Adds a [Control] node to the box as a spacer. If [param begin] is [code]true[/code], it will insert the [Control] node in front of all other children.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment of the container's children (must be one of [constant ALIGNMENT_BEGIN], [constant ALIGNMENT_CENTER], or [constant ALIGNMENT_END]).

properties.name: vertical
properties.description:
If [code]true[/code], the [BoxContainer] will arrange its children vertically, rather than horizontally.
Can't be changed when using [HBoxContainer] and [VBoxContainer].

classes.brief_description: A container that arranges its child controls horizontally or vertically.
classes.description: A container that arranges its child controls horizontally or vertically, rearranging them automatically when their minimum size changes.

classes.name: BoxMesh

properties.name: size
properties.description: The box's width, height and depth.

properties.name: subdivide_width
properties.description: Number of extra edge loops inserted along the X axis.

properties.name: subdivide_height
properties.description: Number of extra edge loops inserted along the Y axis.

properties.name: subdivide_depth
properties.description: Number of extra edge loops inserted along the Z axis.

classes.brief_description: Generate an axis-aligned box [PrimitiveMesh].
classes.description:
Generate an axis-aligned box [PrimitiveMesh].
The box's UV layout is arranged in a 3×2 layout that allows texturing each face individually. To apply the same texture on all faces, change the material's UV property to [code]Vector3(3, 2, 1)[/code]. This is equivalent to adding [code]UV *= vec2(3.0, 2.0)[/code] in a vertex shader.
[b]Note:[/b] When using a large textured [BoxMesh] (e.g. as a floor), you may stumble upon UV jittering issues depending on the camera angle. To solve this, increase [member subdivide_depth], [member subdivide_height] and [member subdivide_width] until you no longer notice UV jittering.

classes.name: BoxOccluder3D

properties.name: size
properties.description: The box's size in 3D units.

classes.brief_description: Cuboid shape for use with occlusion culling in [OccluderInstance3D].
classes.description:
[BoxOccluder3D] stores a cuboid shape that can be used by the engine's occlusion culling system.
See [OccluderInstance3D]'s documentation for instructions on setting up occlusion culling.

classes.name: BoxShape3D

properties.name: size
properties.description: The box's width, height and depth.

classes.brief_description: A 3D box shape used for physics collision.
classes.description:
A 3D box shape, intended for use in physics. Usually used to provide a shape for a [CollisionShape3D].
[b]Performance:[/b] [BoxShape3D] is fast to check collisions against. It is faster than [CapsuleShape3D] and [CylinderShape3D], but slower than [SphereShape3D].

classes.name: Button

properties.name: text
properties.description: The button's text that will be displayed inside the button's area.

properties.name: icon
properties.description:
Button's icon, if text is present the icon will be placed before the text.
To edit margin and spacing of the icon, use [theme_item h_separation] theme property and [code]content_margin_*[/code] properties of the used [StyleBox]es.

properties.name: flat
properties.description: Flat buttons don't display decoration.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: Text alignment policy for the button's text.

properties.name: text_overrun_behavior
properties.description: Sets the clipping behavior when the text exceeds the node's bounding rectangle.

properties.name: autowrap_mode
properties.description: If set to something other than [constant TextServer.AUTOWRAP_OFF], the text gets wrapped inside the node's bounding rectangle.

properties.name: autowrap_trim_flags
properties.description: Autowrap space trimming flags. See [constant TextServer.BREAK_TRIM_START_EDGE_SPACES] and [constant TextServer.BREAK_TRIM_END_EDGE_SPACES] for more info.

properties.name: clip_text
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], text that is too large to fit the button is clipped horizontally. If [code]false[/code], the button will always be wide enough to hold the text. The text is not vertically clipped, and the button's height is not affected by this property.

properties.name: icon_alignment
properties.description: Specifies if the icon should be aligned horizontally to the left, right, or center of a button. Uses the same [enum HorizontalAlignment] constants as the text alignment. If centered horizontally and vertically, text will draw on top of the icon.

properties.name: vertical_icon_alignment
properties.description: Specifies if the icon should be aligned vertically to the top, bottom, or center of a button. Uses the same [enum VerticalAlignment] constants as the text alignment. If centered horizontally and vertically, text will draw on top of the icon.

properties.name: expand_icon
properties.description: When enabled, the button's icon will expand/shrink to fit the button's size while keeping its aspect. See also [theme_item icon_max_width].

properties.name: text_direction
properties.description: Base text writing direction.

properties.name: language
properties.description: Language code used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If left empty, the current locale is used instead.

classes.brief_description: A themed button that can contain text and an icon.

classes.name: ButtonGroup

methods.name: get_pressed_button
methods.description: Returns the current pressed button.

methods.name: get_buttons
methods.description: Returns an [Array] of [Button]s who have this as their [ButtonGroup] (see [member BaseButton.button_group]).

signals.name: pressed
signals.description: Emitted when one of the buttons of the group is pressed.

properties.name: allow_unpress
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], it is possible to unpress all buttons in this [ButtonGroup].

classes.brief_description: A group of buttons that doesn't allow more than one button to be pressed at a time.
classes.description:
A group of [BaseButton]-derived buttons. The buttons in a [ButtonGroup] are treated like radio buttons: No more than one button can be pressed at a time. Some types of buttons (such as [CheckBox]) may have a special appearance in this state.
Every member of a [ButtonGroup] should have [member BaseButton.toggle_mode] set to [code]true[/code].

classes.name: CCDIK3D
classes.brief_description: Rotation based cyclic coordinate descent inverse kinematics solver.
classes.description:
[CCDIK3D] is rotation based IK, enabling fast and effective tracking even with large joint rotations. It's especially suitable for chains with limitations, providing smoother and more stable target tracking compared to [FABRIK3D].
The resulting twist around the forward vector will always be kept from the previous pose.
[b]Note:[/b] When the target is close to the root, it can cause unnatural movement, including joint flips and oscillations.

classes.name: CPUParticles2D

values.name: DRAW_ORDER_INDEX
values.description: Particles are drawn in the order emitted.

values.name: DRAW_ORDER_LIFETIME
values.description: Particles are drawn in order of remaining lifetime. In other words, the particle with the highest lifetime is drawn at the front.

values.name: PARAM_INITIAL_LINEAR_VELOCITY
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set initial velocity properties.

values.name: PARAM_ANGULAR_VELOCITY
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set angular velocity properties.

values.name: PARAM_ORBIT_VELOCITY
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set orbital velocity properties.

values.name: PARAM_LINEAR_ACCEL
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set linear acceleration properties.

values.name: PARAM_RADIAL_ACCEL
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set radial acceleration properties.

values.name: PARAM_TANGENTIAL_ACCEL
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set tangential acceleration properties.

values.name: PARAM_DAMPING
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set damping properties.

values.name: PARAM_ANGLE
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set angle properties.

values.name: PARAM_SCALE
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set scale properties.

values.name: PARAM_HUE_VARIATION
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set hue variation properties.

values.name: PARAM_ANIM_SPEED
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set animation speed properties.

values.name: PARAM_ANIM_OFFSET
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set animation offset properties.

values.name: PARAM_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum Parameter] enum.

values.name: PARTICLE_FLAG_ALIGN_Y_TO_VELOCITY
values.description: Use with [method set_particle_flag] to set [member particle_flag_align_y].

values.name: PARTICLE_FLAG_ROTATE_Y
values.description: Present for consistency with 3D particle nodes, not used in 2D.

values.name: PARTICLE_FLAG_DISABLE_Z
values.description: Present for consistency with 3D particle nodes, not used in 2D.

values.name: PARTICLE_FLAG_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum ParticleFlags] enum.

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_POINT
values.description: All particles will be emitted from a single point.

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_SPHERE
values.description: Particles will be emitted in the volume of a sphere flattened to two dimensions.

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_SPHERE_SURFACE
values.description: Particles will be emitted on the surface of a sphere flattened to two dimensions.

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_RECTANGLE
values.description: Particles will be emitted in the area of a rectangle.

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_POINTS
values.description: Particles will be emitted at a position chosen randomly among [member emission_points]. Particle color will be modulated by [member emission_colors].

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_DIRECTED_POINTS
values.description: Particles will be emitted at a position chosen randomly among [member emission_points]. Particle velocity and rotation will be set based on [member emission_normals]. Particle color will be modulated by [member emission_colors].

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_RING
values.description: Particles will be emitted in the area of a ring parameterized by its outer and inner radius.

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum EmissionShape] enum.

methods.name: request_particles_process
methods.description:
Requests the particles to process for extra process time during a single frame.
[param process_time] defines the time that the particles will process while emitting is on. [param process_time_residual] defines the time that particles will process with emitting turned off for the simulation. When combined with [member speed_scale] set to [code]0.0[/code], this is useful to be able to seek a particle system timeline.

methods.name: restart
methods.description:
Restarts the particle emitter.
If [param keep_seed] is [code]true[/code], the current random seed will be preserved. Useful for seeking and playback.

methods.name: set_param_min
methods.description: Sets the minimum value for the given parameter.

methods.name: get_param_min
methods.description: Returns the minimum value range for the given parameter.

methods.name: set_param_max
methods.description: Sets the maximum value for the given parameter.

methods.name: get_param_max
methods.description: Returns the maximum value range for the given parameter.

methods.name: set_param_curve
methods.description: Sets the [Curve] of the parameter specified by [enum Parameter]. Should be a unit [Curve].

methods.name: get_param_curve
methods.description: Returns the [Curve] of the parameter specified by [enum Parameter].

methods.name: set_particle_flag
methods.description: Enables or disables the given particle flag.

methods.name: get_particle_flag
methods.description: Returns the enabled state of the given particle flag.

methods.name: convert_from_particles
methods.description: Sets this node's properties to match a given [GPUParticles2D] node with an assigned [ParticleProcessMaterial].

signals.name: finished
signals.description: Emitted when all active particles have finished processing. When [member one_shot] is disabled, particles will process continuously, so this is never emitted.

properties.name: emitting
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], particles are being emitted. [member emitting] can be used to start and stop particles from emitting. However, if [member one_shot] is [code]true[/code] setting [member emitting] to [code]true[/code] will not restart the emission cycle until after all active particles finish processing. You can use the [signal finished] signal to be notified once all active particles finish processing.

properties.name: amount
properties.description: Number of particles emitted in one emission cycle.

properties.name: texture
properties.description: Particle texture. If [code]null[/code], particles will be squares.

properties.name: lifetime
properties.description: Amount of time each particle will exist.

properties.name: one_shot
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], only one emission cycle occurs. If set [code]true[/code] during a cycle, emission will stop at the cycle's end.

properties.name: preprocess
properties.description: Particle system starts as if it had already run for this many seconds.

properties.name: speed_scale
properties.description: Particle system's running speed scaling ratio. A value of [code]0[/code] can be used to pause the particles.

properties.name: explosiveness
properties.description: How rapidly particles in an emission cycle are emitted. If greater than [code]0[/code], there will be a gap in emissions before the next cycle begins.

properties.name: randomness
properties.description: Emission lifetime randomness ratio.

properties.name: use_fixed_seed
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], particles will use the same seed for every simulation using the seed defined in [member seed]. This is useful for situations where the visual outcome should be consistent across replays, for example when using Movie Maker mode.

properties.name: seed
properties.description: Sets the random seed used by the particle system. Only effective if [member use_fixed_seed] is [code]true[/code].

properties.name: lifetime_randomness
properties.description: Particle lifetime randomness ratio.

properties.name: fixed_fps
properties.description: The particle system's frame rate is fixed to a value. For example, changing the value to 2 will make the particles render at 2 frames per second. Note this does not slow down the simulation of the particle system itself.

properties.name: fract_delta
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], results in fractional delta calculation which has a smoother particles display effect.

properties.name: local_coords
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], particles use the parent node's coordinate space (known as local coordinates). This will cause particles to move and rotate along the [CPUParticles2D] node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated. If [code]false[/code], particles use global coordinates; they will not move or rotate along the [CPUParticles2D] node (and its parents) when it is moved or rotated.

properties.name: draw_order
properties.description: Particle draw order.

properties.name: emission_shape
properties.description: Particles will be emitted inside this region.

properties.name: emission_sphere_radius
properties.description: The sphere's radius if [member emission_shape] is set to [constant EMISSION_SHAPE_SPHERE].

properties.name: emission_rect_extents
properties.description: The rectangle's extents if [member emission_shape] is set to [constant EMISSION_SHAPE_RECTANGLE].

properties.name: emission_points
properties.description: Sets the initial positions to spawn particles when using [constant EMISSION_SHAPE_POINTS] or [constant EMISSION_SHAPE_DIRECTED_POINTS].

properties.name: emission_normals
properties.description: Sets the direction the particles will be emitted in when using [constant EMISSION_SHAPE_DIRECTED_POINTS].

properties.name: emission_colors
properties.description: Sets the [Color]s to modulate particles by when using [constant EMISSION_SHAPE_POINTS] or [constant EMISSION_SHAPE_DIRECTED_POINTS].

properties.name: emission_ring_inner_radius
properties.description: The ring's inner radius if [member emission_shape] is set to [constant EMISSION_SHAPE_RING].

properties.name: emission_ring_radius
properties.description: The ring's outer radius if [member emission_shape] is set to [constant EMISSION_SHAPE_RING].

properties.name: particle_flag_align_y
properties.description: Align Y axis of particle with the direction of its velocity.

properties.name: direction
properties.description: Unit vector specifying the particles' emission direction.

properties.name: spread
properties.description: Each particle's initial direction range from [code]+spread[/code] to [code]-spread[/code] degrees.

properties.name: gravity
properties.description: Gravity applied to every particle.

properties.name: initial_velocity_min
properties.description: Minimum equivalent of [member initial_velocity_max].

properties.name: initial_velocity_max
properties.description: Maximum initial velocity magnitude for each particle. Direction comes from [member direction] and [member spread].

properties.name: angular_velocity_min
properties.description: Minimum equivalent of [member angular_velocity_max].

properties.name: angular_velocity_max
properties.description: Maximum initial angular velocity (rotation speed) applied to each particle in [i]degrees[/i] per second.

properties.name: angular_velocity_curve
properties.description: Each particle's angular velocity will vary along this [Curve]. Should be a unit [Curve].

properties.name: orbit_velocity_min
properties.description: Minimum equivalent of [member orbit_velocity_max].

properties.name: orbit_velocity_max
properties.description: Maximum orbital velocity applied to each particle. Makes the particles circle around origin. Specified in number of full rotations around origin per second.

properties.name: orbit_velocity_curve
properties.description: Each particle's orbital velocity will vary along this [Curve]. Should be a unit [Curve].

properties.name: linear_accel_min
properties.description: Minimum equivalent of [member linear_accel_max].

properties.name: linear_accel_max
properties.description: Maximum linear acceleration applied to each particle in the direction of motion.

properties.name: linear_accel_curve
properties.description: Each particle's linear acceleration will vary along this [Curve]. Should be a unit [Curve].

properties.name: radial_accel_min
properties.description: Minimum equivalent of [member radial_accel_max].

properties.name: radial_accel_max
properties.description: Maximum radial acceleration applied to each particle. Makes particle accelerate away from the origin or towards it if negative.

properties.name: radial_accel_curve
properties.description: Each particle's radial acceleration will vary along this [Curve]. Should be a unit [Curve].

properties.name: tangential_accel_min
properties.description: Minimum equivalent of [member tangential_accel_max].

properties.name: tangential_accel_max
properties.description: Maximum tangential acceleration applied to each particle. Tangential acceleration is perpendicular to the particle's velocity giving the particles a swirling motion.

properties.name: tangential_accel_curve
properties.description: Each particle's tangential acceleration will vary along this [Curve]. Should be a unit [Curve].

properties.name: damping_min
properties.description: Minimum equivalent of [member damping_max].

properties.name: damping_max
properties.description: The maximum rate at which particles lose velocity. For example value of [code]100[/code] means that the particle will go from [code]100[/code] velocity to [code]0[/code] in [code]1[/code] second.

properties.name: damping_curve
properties.description: Damping will vary along this [Curve]. Should be a unit [Curve].

properties.name: angle_min
properties.description: Minimum equivalent of [member angle_max].

properties.name: angle_max
properties.description: Maximum initial rotation applied to each particle, in degrees.

properties.name: angle_curve
properties.description: Each particle's rotation will be animated along this [Curve]. Should be a unit [Curve].

properties.name: scale_amount_min
properties.description: Minimum equivalent of [member scale_amount_max].

properties.name: scale_amount_max
properties.description: Maximum initial scale applied to each particle.

properties.name: scale_amount_curve
properties.description: Each particle's scale will vary along this [Curve]. Should be a unit [Curve].

properties.name: split_scale
properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the scale curve will be split into x and y components. See [member scale_curve_x] and [member scale_curve_y].

properties.name: scale_curve_x
properties.description:
Each particle's horizontal scale will vary along this [Curve]. Should be a unit [Curve].
[member split_scale] must be enabled.

properties.name: scale_curve_y
properties.description:
Each particle's vertical scale will vary along this [Curve]. Should be a unit [Curve].
[member split_scale] must be enabled.

properties.name: color
properties.description: Each particle's initial color. If [member texture] is defined, it will be multiplied by this color.

properties.name: color_ramp
properties.description: Each particle's color will vary along this [Gradient] over its lifetime (multiplied with [member color]).

properties.name: color_initial_ramp
properties.description: Each particle's initial color will vary along this [Gradient] (multiplied with [member color]).

properties.name: hue_variation_min
properties.description: Minimum equivalent of [member hue_variation_max].

properties.name: hue_variation_max
properties.description: Maximum initial hue variation applied to each particle. It will shift the particle color's hue.

properties.name: hue_variation_curve
properties.description: Each particle's hue will vary along this [Curve]. Should be a unit [Curve].

properties.name: anim_speed_min
properties.description: Minimum equivalent of [member anim_speed_max].

properties.name: anim_speed_max
properties.description:
Maximum particle animation speed. Animation speed of [code]1[/code] means that the particles will make full [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code] offset cycle during lifetime, [code]2[/code] means [code]2[/code] cycles etc.
With animation speed greater than [code]1[/code], remember to enable [member CanvasItemMaterial.particles_anim_loop] property if you want the animation to repeat.

properties.name: anim_speed_curve
properties.description: Each particle's animation speed will vary along this [Curve]. Should be a unit [Curve].

properties.name: anim_offset_min
properties.description: Minimum equivalent of [member anim_offset_max].

properties.name: anim_offset_max
properties.description: Maximum animation offset that corresponds to frame index in the texture. [code]0[/code] is the first frame, [code]1[/code] is the last one. See [member CanvasItemMaterial.particles_animation].

properties.name: anim_offset_curve
properties.description: Each particle's animation offset will vary along this [Curve]. Should be a unit [Curve].

classes.brief_description: A CPU-based 2D particle emitter.

See also [GPUParticles2D], which provides the same functionality with hardware acceleration, but may not run on older devices.

values.name: DRAW_ORDER_INDEX
values.description: Particles are drawn in the order emitted.

values.name: DRAW_ORDER_LIFETIME
values.description: Particles are drawn in order of remaining lifetime. In other words, the particle with the highest lifetime is drawn at the front.

values.name: DRAW_ORDER_VIEW_DEPTH
values.description: Particles are drawn in order of depth.

values.name: PARAM_INITIAL_LINEAR_VELOCITY
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set initial velocity properties.

values.name: PARAM_ANGULAR_VELOCITY
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set angular velocity properties.

values.name: PARAM_ORBIT_VELOCITY
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set orbital velocity properties.

values.name: PARAM_LINEAR_ACCEL
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set linear acceleration properties.

values.name: PARAM_RADIAL_ACCEL
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set radial acceleration properties.

values.name: PARAM_TANGENTIAL_ACCEL
values.description: Use with [method set_param_min], [method set_param_max], and [method set_param_curve] to set tangential acceleration properties.

values.name: PARAM_DAMPING

values.name: PARAM_ANGLE

values.name: PARAM_SCALE

values.description: Represents the size of the [enum Parameter] enum.

values.name: PARTICLE_FLAG_ALIGN_Y_TO_VELOCITY
values.description: Use with [method set_particle_flag] to set [member particle_flag_align_y].

values.name: PARTICLE_FLAG_ROTATE_Y

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_POINT
values.description: All particles will be emitted from a single point.

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_SPHERE
values.description: Particles will be emitted in the volume of a sphere.

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_SPHERE_SURFACE
values.description: Particles will be emitted on the surface of a sphere.

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_BOX
values.description: Particles will be emitted in the volume of a box.

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_POINTS
values.description: Particles will be emitted at a position chosen randomly among [member emission_points]. Particle color will be modulated by [member emission_colors].

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_DIRECTED_POINTS
values.description: Particles will be emitted at a position chosen randomly among [member emission_points]. Particle velocity and rotation will be set based on [member emission_normals]. Particle color will be modulated by [member emission_colors].

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_RING
values.description: Particles will be emitted in a ring or cylinder.

values.name: EMISSION_SHAPE_MAX
