values.name: SPACE_PARAM_CONTACT_RECYCLE_RADIUS
values.description: Constant to set/get the maximum distance a pair of bodies has to move before their collision status has to be recalculated. The default value of this parameter is [member ProjectSettings.physics/2d/solver/contact_recycle_radius].

values.name: SPACE_PARAM_CONTACT_MAX_SEPARATION
values.description: Constant to set/get the maximum distance a shape can be from another before they are considered separated and the contact is discarded. The default value of this parameter is [member ProjectSettings.physics/2d/solver/contact_max_separation].

values.name: SPACE_PARAM_CONTACT_MAX_ALLOWED_PENETRATION
values.description: Constant to set/get the maximum distance a shape can penetrate another shape before it is considered a collision. The default value of this parameter is [member ProjectSettings.physics/2d/solver/contact_max_allowed_penetration].

values.name: SPACE_PARAM_CONTACT_DEFAULT_BIAS
values.description: Constant to set/get the default solver bias for all physics contacts. A solver bias is a factor controlling how much two objects "rebound", after overlapping, to avoid leaving them in that state because of numerical imprecision. The default value of this parameter is [member ProjectSettings.physics/2d/solver/default_contact_bias].

values.name: SPACE_PARAM_BODY_LINEAR_VELOCITY_SLEEP_THRESHOLD
values.description: Constant to set/get the threshold linear velocity of activity. A body marked as potentially inactive for both linear and angular velocity will be put to sleep after the time given. The default value of this parameter is [member ProjectSettings.physics/2d/sleep_threshold_linear].

values.name: SPACE_PARAM_BODY_ANGULAR_VELOCITY_SLEEP_THRESHOLD
values.description: Constant to set/get the threshold angular velocity of activity. A body marked as potentially inactive for both linear and angular velocity will be put to sleep after the time given. The default value of this parameter is [member ProjectSettings.physics/2d/sleep_threshold_angular].

values.name: SPACE_PARAM_BODY_TIME_TO_SLEEP
values.description: Constant to set/get the maximum time of activity. A body marked as potentially inactive for both linear and angular velocity will be put to sleep after this time. The default value of this parameter is [member ProjectSettings.physics/2d/time_before_sleep].

values.name: SPACE_PARAM_CONSTRAINT_DEFAULT_BIAS
values.description: Constant to set/get the default solver bias for all physics constraints. A solver bias is a factor controlling how much two objects "rebound", after violating a constraint, to avoid leaving them in that state because of numerical imprecision. The default value of this parameter is [member ProjectSettings.physics/2d/solver/default_constraint_bias].

values.name: SPACE_PARAM_SOLVER_ITERATIONS
values.description: Constant to set/get the number of solver iterations for all contacts and constraints. The greater the number of iterations, the more accurate the collisions will be. However, a greater number of iterations requires more CPU power, which can decrease performance. The default value of this parameter is [member ProjectSettings.physics/2d/solver/solver_iterations].

values.name: SHAPE_WORLD_BOUNDARY
values.description: This is the constant for creating world boundary shapes. A world boundary shape is an [i]infinite[/i] line with an origin point, and a normal. Thus, it can be used for front/behind checks.

values.name: SHAPE_SEPARATION_RAY
values.description: This is the constant for creating separation ray shapes. A separation ray is defined by a length and separates itself from what is touching its far endpoint. Useful for character controllers.

values.name: SHAPE_SEGMENT
values.description: This is the constant for creating segment shapes. A segment shape is a [i]finite[/i] line from a point A to a point B. It can be checked for intersections.

values.name: SHAPE_CIRCLE
values.description: This is the constant for creating circle shapes. A circle shape only has a radius. It can be used for intersections and inside/outside checks.

values.name: SHAPE_RECTANGLE
values.description: This is the constant for creating rectangle shapes. A rectangle shape is defined by a width and a height. It can be used for intersections and inside/outside checks.

values.name: SHAPE_CAPSULE
values.description: This is the constant for creating capsule shapes. A capsule shape is defined by a radius and a length. It can be used for intersections and inside/outside checks.

values.name: SHAPE_CONVEX_POLYGON
values.description: This is the constant for creating convex polygon shapes. A polygon is defined by a list of points. It can be used for intersections and inside/outside checks.

values.name: SHAPE_CONCAVE_POLYGON
values.description: This is the constant for creating concave polygon shapes. A polygon is defined by a list of points. It can be used for intersections checks, but not for inside/outside checks.

values.name: SHAPE_CUSTOM
values.description: This constant is used internally by the engine. Any attempt to create this kind of shape results in an error.

values.name: AREA_PARAM_GRAVITY_OVERRIDE_MODE
values.description: Constant to set/get gravity override mode in an area. See [enum AreaSpaceOverrideMode] for possible values. The default value of this parameter is [constant AREA_SPACE_OVERRIDE_DISABLED].

values.name: AREA_PARAM_GRAVITY
values.description: Constant to set/get gravity strength in an area. The default value of this parameter is [code]9.80665[/code].

values.name: AREA_PARAM_GRAVITY_VECTOR
values.description: Constant to set/get gravity vector/center in an area. The default value of this parameter is [code]Vector2(0, -1)[/code].

values.name: AREA_PARAM_GRAVITY_IS_POINT
values.description: Constant to set/get whether the gravity vector of an area is a direction, or a center point. The default value of this parameter is [code]false[/code].

values.name: AREA_PARAM_GRAVITY_POINT_UNIT_DISTANCE
values.description:
Constant to set/get the distance at which the gravity strength is equal to the gravity controlled by [constant AREA_PARAM_GRAVITY]. For example, on a planet 100 pixels in radius with a surface gravity of 4.0 px/s², set the gravity to 4.0 and the unit distance to 100.0. The gravity will have falloff according to the inverse square law, so in the example, at 200 pixels from the center the gravity will be 1.0 px/s² (twice the distance, 1/4th the gravity), at 50 pixels it will be 16.0 px/s² (half the distance, 4x the gravity), and so on.
The above is true only when the unit distance is a positive number. When the unit distance is set to 0.0, the gravity will be constant regardless of distance. The default value of this parameter is [code]0.0[/code].

values.name: AREA_PARAM_LINEAR_DAMP_OVERRIDE_MODE
values.description: Constant to set/get linear damping override mode in an area. See [enum AreaSpaceOverrideMode] for possible values. The default value of this parameter is [constant AREA_SPACE_OVERRIDE_DISABLED].

values.name: AREA_PARAM_LINEAR_DAMP
values.description: Constant to set/get the linear damping factor of an area. The default value of this parameter is [code]0.1[/code].

values.name: AREA_PARAM_ANGULAR_DAMP_OVERRIDE_MODE
values.description: Constant to set/get angular damping override mode in an area. See [enum AreaSpaceOverrideMode] for possible values. The default value of this parameter is [constant AREA_SPACE_OVERRIDE_DISABLED].

values.name: AREA_PARAM_ANGULAR_DAMP
values.description: Constant to set/get the angular damping factor of an area. The default value of this parameter is [code]1.0[/code].

values.name: AREA_PARAM_PRIORITY
values.description: Constant to set/get the priority (order of processing) of an area. The default value of this parameter is [code]0[/code].

values.name: AREA_SPACE_OVERRIDE_DISABLED
values.description: This area does not affect gravity/damp. These are generally areas that exist only to detect collisions, and objects entering or exiting them.

values.name: AREA_SPACE_OVERRIDE_COMBINE
values.description: This area adds its gravity/damp values to whatever has been calculated so far. This way, many overlapping areas can combine their physics to make interesting effects.

values.name: AREA_SPACE_OVERRIDE_COMBINE_REPLACE
values.description: This area adds its gravity/damp values to whatever has been calculated so far. Then stops taking into account the rest of the areas, even the default one.

values.name: AREA_SPACE_OVERRIDE_REPLACE
values.description: This area replaces any gravity/damp, even the default one, and stops taking into account the rest of the areas.

values.name: AREA_SPACE_OVERRIDE_REPLACE_COMBINE
values.description: This area replaces any gravity/damp calculated so far, but keeps calculating the rest of the areas, down to the default one.

values.name: BODY_MODE_STATIC
values.description: Constant for static bodies. In this mode, a body can be only moved by user code and doesn't collide with other bodies along its path when moved.

values.name: BODY_MODE_KINEMATIC
values.description: Constant for kinematic bodies. In this mode, a body can be only moved by user code and collides with other bodies along its path.

values.name: BODY_MODE_RIGID
values.description: Constant for rigid bodies. In this mode, a body can be pushed by other bodies and has forces applied.

values.name: BODY_MODE_RIGID_LINEAR
values.description: Constant for linear rigid bodies. In this mode, a body can not rotate, and only its linear velocity is affected by external forces.

values.name: BODY_PARAM_BOUNCE
values.description: Constant to set/get a body's bounce factor. The default value of this parameter is [code]0.0[/code].

values.name: BODY_PARAM_FRICTION
values.description: Constant to set/get a body's friction. The default value of this parameter is [code]1.0[/code].

values.name: BODY_PARAM_MASS
values.description:
Constant to set/get a body's mass. The default value of this parameter is [code]1.0[/code]. If the body's mode is set to [constant BODY_MODE_RIGID], then setting this parameter will have the following additional effects:
- If the parameter [constant BODY_PARAM_CENTER_OF_MASS] has never been set explicitly, then the value of that parameter will be recalculated based on the body's shapes.
- If the parameter [constant BODY_PARAM_INERTIA] is set to a value [code]<= 0.0[/code], then the value of that parameter will be recalculated based on the body's shapes, mass, and center of mass.

values.name: BODY_PARAM_INERTIA
values.description: Constant to set/get a body's inertia. The default value of this parameter is [code]0.0[/code]. If the body's inertia is set to a value [code]<= 0.0[/code], then the inertia will be recalculated based on the body's shapes, mass, and center of mass.

values.name: BODY_PARAM_CENTER_OF_MASS
values.description: Constant to set/get a body's center of mass position in the body's local coordinate system. The default value of this parameter is [code]Vector2(0, 0)[/code]. If this parameter is never set explicitly, then it is recalculated based on the body's shapes when setting the parameter [constant BODY_PARAM_MASS] or when calling [method body_set_space].

values.name: BODY_PARAM_GRAVITY_SCALE
values.description: Constant to set/get a body's gravity multiplier. The default value of this parameter is [code]1.0[/code].

values.name: BODY_PARAM_LINEAR_DAMP_MODE
values.description: Constant to set/get a body's linear damping mode. See [enum BodyDampMode] for possible values. The default value of this parameter is [constant BODY_DAMP_MODE_COMBINE].

values.name: BODY_PARAM_ANGULAR_DAMP_MODE
values.description: Constant to set/get a body's angular damping mode. See [enum BodyDampMode] for possible values. The default value of this parameter is [constant BODY_DAMP_MODE_COMBINE].

values.name: BODY_PARAM_LINEAR_DAMP
values.description: Constant to set/get a body's linear damping factor. The default value of this parameter is [code]0.0[/code].

values.name: BODY_PARAM_ANGULAR_DAMP
values.description: Constant to set/get a body's angular damping factor. The default value of this parameter is [code]0.0[/code].

values.name: BODY_PARAM_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum BodyParameter] enum.

values.name: BODY_DAMP_MODE_COMBINE
values.description: The body's damping value is added to any value set in areas or the default value.

values.name: BODY_DAMP_MODE_REPLACE
values.description: The body's damping value replaces any value set in areas or the default value.

values.name: BODY_STATE_TRANSFORM
values.description: Constant to set/get the current transform matrix of the body.

values.name: BODY_STATE_LINEAR_VELOCITY
values.description: Constant to set/get the current linear velocity of the body.

values.name: BODY_STATE_ANGULAR_VELOCITY
values.description: Constant to set/get the current angular velocity of the body.

values.name: BODY_STATE_SLEEPING
values.description: Constant to sleep/wake up a body, or to get whether it is sleeping.

values.name: BODY_STATE_CAN_SLEEP
values.description: Constant to set/get whether the body can sleep.

values.name: JOINT_TYPE_PIN
values.description: Constant to create pin joints.

values.name: JOINT_TYPE_GROOVE
values.description: Constant to create groove joints.

values.name: JOINT_TYPE_DAMPED_SPRING
values.description: Constant to create damped spring joints.

values.name: JOINT_TYPE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum JointType] enum.

values.name: JOINT_PARAM_BIAS
values.description:
Constant to set/get how fast the joint pulls the bodies back to satisfy the joint constraint. The lower the value, the more the two bodies can pull on the joint. The default value of this parameter is [code]0.0[/code].
[b]Note:[/b] In Godot Physics, this parameter is only used for pin joints and groove joints.

values.name: JOINT_PARAM_MAX_BIAS
values.description:
Constant to set/get the maximum speed with which the joint can apply corrections. The default value of this parameter is [code]3.40282e+38[/code].
[b]Note:[/b] In Godot Physics, this parameter is only used for groove joints.

values.name: JOINT_PARAM_MAX_FORCE
values.description:
Constant to set/get the maximum force that the joint can use to act on the two bodies. The default value of this parameter is [code]3.40282e+38[/code].
[b]Note:[/b] In Godot Physics, this parameter is only used for groove joints.

values.name: PIN_JOINT_SOFTNESS
values.description: Constant to set/get a how much the bond of the pin joint can flex. The default value of this parameter is [code]0.0[/code].

values.name: PIN_JOINT_LIMIT_UPPER
values.description: The maximum rotation around the pin.

values.name: PIN_JOINT_LIMIT_LOWER
values.description: The minimum rotation around the pin.

values.name: PIN_JOINT_MOTOR_TARGET_VELOCITY
values.description: Target speed for the motor. In radians per second.

values.name: PIN_JOINT_FLAG_ANGULAR_LIMIT_ENABLED
values.description: If [code]true[/code], the pin has a maximum and a minimum rotation.

values.name: PIN_JOINT_FLAG_MOTOR_ENABLED
values.description: If [code]true[/code], a motor turns the pin.

values.name: DAMPED_SPRING_REST_LENGTH
values.description: Sets the resting length of the spring joint. The joint will always try to go to back this length when pulled apart. The default value of this parameter is the distance between the joint's anchor points.

values.name: DAMPED_SPRING_STIFFNESS
values.description: Sets the stiffness of the spring joint. The joint applies a force equal to the stiffness times the distance from its resting length. The default value of this parameter is [code]20.0[/code].

values.name: DAMPED_SPRING_DAMPING
values.description: Sets the damping ratio of the spring joint. A value of 0 indicates an undamped spring, while 1 causes the system to reach equilibrium as fast as possible (critical damping). The default value of this parameter is [code]1.5[/code].

values.name: CCD_MODE_DISABLED
values.description: Disables continuous collision detection. This is the fastest way to detect body collisions, but it can miss small and/or fast-moving objects.

values.name: CCD_MODE_CAST_RAY
values.description: Enables continuous collision detection by raycasting. It is faster than shapecasting, but less precise.

values.name: CCD_MODE_CAST_SHAPE
values.description: Enables continuous collision detection by shapecasting. It is the slowest CCD method, and the most precise.

values.name: AREA_BODY_ADDED
values.description: The value of the first parameter and area callback function receives, when an object enters one of its shapes.

values.name: AREA_BODY_REMOVED
values.description: The value of the first parameter and area callback function receives, when an object exits one of its shapes.

values.name: INFO_ACTIVE_OBJECTS
values.description: Constant to get the number of objects that are not sleeping.

values.name: INFO_COLLISION_PAIRS
values.description: Constant to get the number of possible collisions.

values.name: INFO_ISLAND_COUNT
values.description: Constant to get the number of space regions where a collision could occur.

methods.name: world_boundary_shape_create
methods.description: Creates a 2D world boundary shape in the physics server, and returns the [RID] that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the shape's normal direction and distance properties.

methods.name: separation_ray_shape_create
methods.description: Creates a 2D separation ray shape in the physics server, and returns the [RID] that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the shape's [code]length[/code] and [code]slide_on_slope[/code] properties.

methods.name: segment_shape_create
methods.description: Creates a 2D segment shape in the physics server, and returns the [RID] that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the segment's start and end points.

methods.name: circle_shape_create
methods.description: Creates a 2D circle shape in the physics server, and returns the [RID] that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the circle's radius.

methods.name: rectangle_shape_create
methods.description: Creates a 2D rectangle shape in the physics server, and returns the [RID] that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the rectangle's half-extents.

methods.name: capsule_shape_create
methods.description: Creates a 2D capsule shape in the physics server, and returns the [RID] that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the capsule's height and radius.

methods.name: convex_polygon_shape_create
methods.description: Creates a 2D convex polygon shape in the physics server, and returns the [RID] that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the convex polygon's points.

methods.name: concave_polygon_shape_create
methods.description: Creates a 2D concave polygon shape in the physics server, and returns the [RID] that identifies it. Use [method shape_set_data] to set the concave polygon's segments.

methods.name: shape_set_data
methods.description:
Sets the shape data that defines the configuration of the shape. The [param data] to be passed depends on the shape's type (see [method shape_get_type]):
- [constant SHAPE_WORLD_BOUNDARY]: an array of length two containing a [Vector2] [code]normal[/code] direction and a [float] distance [code]d[/code],
- [constant SHAPE_SEPARATION_RAY]: a dictionary containing the key [code]length[/code] with a [float] value and the key [code]slide_on_slope[/code] with a [bool] value,
- [constant SHAPE_SEGMENT]: a [Rect2] [code]rect[/code] containing the first point of the segment in [code]rect.position[/code] and the second point of the segment in [code]rect.size[/code],
- [constant SHAPE_CIRCLE]: a [float] [code]radius[/code],
- [constant SHAPE_RECTANGLE]: a [Vector2] [code]half_extents[/code],
- [constant SHAPE_CAPSULE]: an array of length two (or a [Vector2]) containing a [float] [code]height[/code] and a [float] [code]radius[/code],
- [constant SHAPE_CONVEX_POLYGON]: either a [PackedVector2Array] of points defining a convex polygon in counterclockwise order (the clockwise outward normal of each segment formed by consecutive points is calculated internally), or a [PackedFloat32Array] of length divisible by four so that every 4-tuple of [float]s contains the coordinates of a point followed by the coordinates of the clockwise outward normal vector to the segment between the current point and the next point,
- [constant SHAPE_CONCAVE_POLYGON]: a [PackedVector2Array] of length divisible by two (each pair of points forms one segment).
[b]Warning:[/b] In the case of [constant SHAPE_CONVEX_POLYGON], this method does not check if the points supplied actually form a convex polygon (unlike the [member CollisionPolygon2D.polygon] property).

methods.name: shape_get_type
methods.description: Returns the shape's type.

methods.name: shape_get_data
methods.description: Returns the shape data that defines the configuration of the shape, such as the half-extents of a rectangle or the segments of a concave shape. See [method shape_set_data] for the precise format of this data in each case.

methods.name: space_create
methods.description: Creates a 2D space in the physics server, and returns the [RID] that identifies it. A space contains bodies and areas, and controls the stepping of the physics simulation of the objects in it.

methods.name: space_set_active
methods.description: Activates or deactivates the space. If [param active] is [code]false[/code], then the physics server will not do anything with this space in its physics step.

methods.name: space_is_active
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the space is active.

methods.name: space_set_param
methods.description: Sets the value of the given space parameter.

methods.name: space_get_param
methods.description: Returns the value of the given space parameter.

methods.name: space_get_direct_state
methods.description: Returns the state of a space, a [PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D]. This object can be used for collision/intersection queries.

methods.name: area_create
methods.description:
Creates a 2D area object in the physics server, and returns the [RID] that identifies it. The default settings for the created area include a collision layer and mask set to [code]1[/code], and [code]monitorable[/code] set to [code]false[/code].
Use [method area_add_shape] to add shapes to it, use [method area_set_transform] to set its transform, and use [method area_set_space] to add the area to a space. If you want the area to be detectable use [method area_set_monitorable].

methods.name: area_set_space
methods.description:
Adds the area to the given space, after removing the area from the previously assigned space (if any).
[b]Note:[/b] To remove an area from a space without immediately adding it back elsewhere, use [code]PhysicsServer2D.area_set_space(area, RID())[/code].

methods.name: area_get_space
methods.description: Returns the [RID] of the space assigned to the area. Returns an empty [RID] if no space is assigned.

methods.name: area_add_shape
methods.description: Adds a shape to the area, with the given local transform. The shape (together with its [param transform] and [param disabled] properties) is added to an array of shapes, and the shapes of an area are usually referenced by their index in this array.

methods.name: area_set_shape
methods.description: Replaces the area's shape at the given index by another shape, while not affecting the [code]transform[/code] and [code]disabled[/code] properties at the same index.

methods.name: area_set_shape_transform
methods.description: Sets the local transform matrix of the area's shape with the given index.

methods.name: area_set_shape_disabled
methods.description: Sets the disabled property of the area's shape with the given index. If [param disabled] is [code]true[/code], then the shape will not detect any other shapes entering or exiting it.

methods.name: area_get_shape_count
methods.description: Returns the number of shapes added to the area.

methods.name: area_get_shape
methods.description: Returns the [RID] of the shape with the given index in the area's array of shapes.

methods.name: area_get_shape_transform
methods.description: Returns the local transform matrix of the shape with the given index in the area's array of shapes.

methods.name: area_remove_shape
methods.description: Removes the shape with the given index from the area's array of shapes. The shape itself is not deleted, so it can continue to be used elsewhere or added back later. As a result of this operation, the area's shapes which used to have indices higher than [param shape_idx] will have their index decreased by one.

methods.name: area_clear_shapes
methods.description: Removes all shapes from the area. This does not delete the shapes themselves, so they can continue to be used elsewhere or added back later.

methods.name: area_set_collision_layer
methods.description: Assigns the area to one or many physics layers, via a bitmask.

methods.name: area_get_collision_layer
methods.description: Returns the physics layer or layers the area belongs to, as a bitmask.

methods.name: area_set_collision_mask
methods.description: Sets which physics layers the area will monitor, via a bitmask.

methods.name: area_get_collision_mask
methods.description: Returns the physics layer or layers the area can contact with, as a bitmask.

methods.name: area_set_param
methods.description: Sets the value of the given area parameter.

methods.name: area_set_transform
methods.description: Sets the transform matrix of the area.

methods.name: area_get_param
methods.description: Returns the value of the given area parameter.

methods.name: area_get_transform
methods.description: Returns the transform matrix of the area.

methods.name: area_attach_object_instance_id
methods.description: Attaches the [code]ObjectID[/code] of an [Object] to the area. Use [method Object.get_instance_id] to get the [code]ObjectID[/code] of a [CollisionObject2D].

methods.name: area_get_object_instance_id
methods.description: Returns the [code]ObjectID[/code] attached to the area. Use [method @GlobalScope.instance_from_id] to retrieve an [Object] from a nonzero [code]ObjectID[/code].

methods.name: area_attach_canvas_instance_id
methods.description: Attaches the [code]ObjectID[/code] of a canvas to the area. Use [method Object.get_instance_id] to get the [code]ObjectID[/code] of a [CanvasLayer].

methods.name: area_get_canvas_instance_id
methods.description: Returns the [code]ObjectID[/code] of the canvas attached to the area. Use [method @GlobalScope.instance_from_id] to retrieve a [CanvasLayer] from a nonzero [code]ObjectID[/code].

methods.name: area_set_monitor_callback
methods.description:
Sets the area's body monitor callback. This callback will be called when any other (shape of a) body enters or exits (a shape of) the given area, and must take the following five parameters:
1. an integer [code]status[/code]: either [constant AREA_BODY_ADDED] or [constant AREA_BODY_REMOVED] depending on whether the other body shape entered or exited the area,
2. an [RID] [code]body_rid[/code]: the [RID] of the body that entered or exited the area,
3. an integer [code]instance_id[/code]: the [code]ObjectID[/code] attached to the body,
4. an integer [code]body_shape_idx[/code]: the index of the shape of the body that entered or exited the area,
5. an integer [code]self_shape_idx[/code]: the index of the shape of the area where the body entered or exited.
By counting (or keeping track of) the shapes that enter and exit, it can be determined if a body (with all its shapes) is entering for the first time or exiting for the last time.

methods.name: area_set_area_monitor_callback
methods.description:
Sets the area's area monitor callback. This callback will be called when any other (shape of an) area enters or exits (a shape of) the given area, and must take the following five parameters:
1. an integer [code]status[/code]: either [constant AREA_BODY_ADDED] or [constant AREA_BODY_REMOVED] depending on whether the other area's shape entered or exited the area,
2. an [RID] [code]area_rid[/code]: the [RID] of the other area that entered or exited the area,
3. an integer [code]instance_id[/code]: the [code]ObjectID[/code] attached to the other area,
4. an integer [code]area_shape_idx[/code]: the index of the shape of the other area that entered or exited the area,
5. an integer [code]self_shape_idx[/code]: the index of the shape of the area where the other area entered or exited.
By counting (or keeping track of) the shapes that enter and exit, it can be determined if an area (with all its shapes) is entering for the first time or exiting for the last time.

methods.name: area_set_monitorable
methods.description: Sets whether the area is monitorable or not. If [param monitorable] is [code]true[/code], the area monitoring callback of other areas will be called when this area enters or exits them.

methods.name: body_create
methods.description:
Creates a 2D body object in the physics server, and returns the [RID] that identifies it. The default settings for the created area include a collision layer and mask set to [code]1[/code], and body mode set to [constant BODY_MODE_RIGID].
Use [method body_add_shape] to add shapes to it, use [method body_set_state] to set its transform, and use [method body_set_space] to add the body to a space.

methods.name: body_set_space
methods.description:
Adds the body to the given space, after removing the body from the previously assigned space (if any). If the body's mode is set to [constant BODY_MODE_RIGID], then adding the body to a space will have the following additional effects:
- If the parameter [constant BODY_PARAM_CENTER_OF_MASS] has never been set explicitly, then the value of that parameter will be recalculated based on the body's shapes.
- If the parameter [constant BODY_PARAM_INERTIA] is set to a value [code]<= 0.0[/code], then the value of that parameter will be recalculated based on the body's shapes, mass, and center of mass.
[b]Note:[/b] To remove a body from a space without immediately adding it back elsewhere, use [code]PhysicsServer2D.body_set_space(body, RID())[/code].

methods.name: body_get_space
methods.description: Returns the [RID] of the space assigned to the body. Returns an empty [RID] if no space is assigned.

methods.name: body_set_mode
methods.description: Sets the body's mode.

methods.name: body_get_mode
methods.description: Returns the body's mode.

methods.name: body_add_shape
methods.description: Adds a shape to the area, with the given local transform. The shape (together with its [param transform] and [param disabled] properties) is added to an array of shapes, and the shapes of a body are usually referenced by their index in this array.

methods.name: body_set_shape
methods.description: Replaces the body's shape at the given index by another shape, while not affecting the [code]transform[/code], [code]disabled[/code], and one-way collision properties at the same index.

methods.name: body_set_shape_transform
methods.description: Sets the local transform matrix of the body's shape with the given index.

methods.name: body_get_shape_count
methods.description: Returns the number of shapes added to the body.

methods.name: body_get_shape
methods.description: Returns the [RID] of the shape with the given index in the body's array of shapes.

methods.name: body_get_shape_transform
methods.description: Returns the local transform matrix of the shape with the given index in the area's array of shapes.

methods.name: body_remove_shape
methods.description: Removes the shape with the given index from the body's array of shapes. The shape itself is not deleted, so it can continue to be used elsewhere or added back later. As a result of this operation, the body's shapes which used to have indices higher than [param shape_idx] will have their index decreased by one.

methods.name: body_clear_shapes
methods.description: Removes all shapes from the body. This does not delete the shapes themselves, so they can continue to be used elsewhere or added back later.

methods.name: body_set_shape_disabled
methods.description: Sets the disabled property of the body's shape with the given index. If [param disabled] is [code]true[/code], then the shape will be ignored in all collision detection.

methods.name: body_set_shape_as_one_way_collision
methods.description: Sets the one-way collision properties of the body's shape with the given index. If [param enable] is [code]true[/code], the one-way collision direction given by [param direction] in the shape's local space (that is [code]body_get_shape_transform(body, shape_idx).basis_xform(direction).normalized()[/code] in the body's local space) will be used to ignore collisions with the shape in the opposite direction, and to ensure depenetration of kinematic bodies happens in this direction.

methods.name: body_attach_object_instance_id
methods.description: Attaches the [code]ObjectID[/code] of an [Object] to the body. Use [method Object.get_instance_id] to get the [code]ObjectID[/code] of a [CollisionObject2D].

methods.name: body_get_object_instance_id
methods.description: Returns the [code]ObjectID[/code] attached to the body. Use [method @GlobalScope.instance_from_id] to retrieve an [Object] from a nonzero [code]ObjectID[/code].

methods.name: body_attach_canvas_instance_id
methods.description: Attaches the [code]ObjectID[/code] of a canvas to the body. Use [method Object.get_instance_id] to get the [code]ObjectID[/code] of a [CanvasLayer].

methods.name: body_get_canvas_instance_id
methods.description: Returns the [code]ObjectID[/code] of the canvas attached to the body. Use [method @GlobalScope.instance_from_id] to retrieve a [CanvasLayer] from a nonzero [code]ObjectID[/code].

methods.name: body_set_continuous_collision_detection_mode
methods.description:
Sets the continuous collision detection mode.
Continuous collision detection tries to predict where a moving body would collide in between physics updates, instead of moving it and correcting its movement if it collided.

methods.name: body_get_continuous_collision_detection_mode
methods.description: Returns the body's continuous collision detection mode.

methods.name: body_set_collision_layer
methods.description: Sets the physics layer or layers the body belongs to, via a bitmask.

methods.name: body_get_collision_layer
methods.description: Returns the physics layer or layers the body belongs to, as a bitmask.

methods.name: body_set_collision_mask
methods.description: Sets the physics layer or layers the body can collide with, via a bitmask.

methods.name: body_get_collision_mask
methods.description: Returns the physics layer or layers the body can collide with, as a bitmask.

methods.name: body_set_collision_priority
methods.description: Sets the body's collision priority. This is used in the depenetration phase of [method body_test_motion]. The higher the priority is, the lower the penetration into the body will be.

methods.name: body_get_collision_priority
methods.description: Returns the body's collision priority. This is used in the depenetration phase of [method body_test_motion]. The higher the priority is, the lower the penetration into the body will be.

methods.name: body_set_param
methods.description: Sets the value of the given body parameter.

methods.name: body_get_param
methods.description: Returns the value of the given body parameter.

methods.name: body_reset_mass_properties
methods.description: Restores the default inertia and center of mass of the body based on its shapes. This undoes any custom values previously set using [method body_set_param].

methods.name: body_set_state
methods.description:
Sets the value of a body's state.
[b]Note:[/b] The state change doesn't take effect immediately. The state will change on the next physics frame.

methods.name: body_get_state
methods.description: Returns the value of the given state of the body.

methods.name: body_apply_central_impulse
methods.description:
Applies a directional impulse to the body, at the body's center of mass. The impulse does not affect rotation.
An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise).
This is equivalent to using [method body_apply_impulse] at the body's center of mass.

methods.name: body_apply_torque_impulse
methods.description:
Applies a rotational impulse to the body. The impulse does not affect position.
An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise).

methods.name: body_apply_impulse
methods.description:
Applies a positioned impulse to the body. The impulse can affect rotation if [param position] is different from the body's center of mass.
An impulse is time-independent! Applying an impulse every frame would result in a framerate-dependent force. For this reason, it should only be used when simulating one-time impacts (use the "_force" functions otherwise).
[param position] is the offset from the body origin in global coordinates.

methods.name: body_apply_central_force
methods.description:
Applies a directional force to the body, at the body's center of mass. The force does not affect rotation. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.
This is equivalent to using [method body_apply_force] at the body's center of mass.

methods.name: body_apply_force
methods.description:
Applies a positioned force to the body. The force can affect rotation if [param position] is different from the body's center of mass. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.
[param position] is the offset from the body origin in global coordinates.

methods.name: body_apply_torque
methods.description: Applies a rotational force to the body. The force does not affect position. A force is time dependent and meant to be applied every physics update.

methods.name: body_add_constant_central_force
methods.description:
Adds a constant directional force to the body. The force does not affect rotation. The force remains applied over time until cleared with [code]PhysicsServer2D.body_set_constant_force(body, Vector2(0, 0))[/code].
This is equivalent to using [method body_add_constant_force] at the body's center of mass.

methods.name: body_add_constant_force
methods.description:
Adds a constant positioned force to the body. The force can affect rotation if [param position] is different from the body's center of mass. The force remains applied over time until cleared with [code]PhysicsServer2D.body_set_constant_force(body, Vector2(0, 0))[/code].
[param position] is the offset from the body origin in global coordinates.

methods.name: body_add_constant_torque
methods.description: Adds a constant rotational force to the body. The force does not affect position. The force remains applied over time until cleared with [code]PhysicsServer2D.body_set_constant_torque(body, 0)[/code].

methods.name: body_set_constant_force
methods.description:
Sets the body's total constant positional force applied during each physics update.
See [method body_add_constant_force] and [method body_add_constant_central_force].

methods.name: body_get_constant_force
methods.description:
Returns the body's total constant positional force applied during each physics update.
See [method body_add_constant_force] and [method body_add_constant_central_force].

methods.name: body_set_constant_torque
methods.description:
Sets the body's total constant rotational force applied during each physics update.
See [method body_add_constant_torque].

methods.name: body_get_constant_torque
methods.description:
Returns the body's total constant rotational force applied during each physics update.
See [method body_add_constant_torque].

methods.name: body_set_axis_velocity
methods.description: Modifies the body's linear velocity so that its projection to the axis [code]axis_velocity.normalized()[/code] is exactly [code]axis_velocity.length()[/code]. This is useful for jumping behavior.

methods.name: body_add_collision_exception
methods.description: Adds [param excepted_body] to the body's list of collision exceptions, so that collisions with it are ignored.

methods.name: body_remove_collision_exception
methods.description: Removes [param excepted_body] from the body's list of collision exceptions, so that collisions with it are no longer ignored.

methods.name: body_set_max_contacts_reported
methods.description: Sets the maximum number of contacts that the body can report. If [param amount] is greater than zero, then the body will keep track of at most this many contacts with other bodies.

methods.name: body_get_max_contacts_reported
methods.description: Returns the maximum number of contacts that the body can report. See [method body_set_max_contacts_reported].

methods.name: body_set_omit_force_integration
methods.description:
Sets whether the body omits the standard force integration. If [param enable] is [code]true[/code], the body will not automatically use applied forces, torques, and damping to update the body's linear and angular velocity. In this case, [method body_set_force_integration_callback] can be used to manually update the linear and angular velocity instead.
This method is called when the property [member RigidBody2D.custom_integrator] is set.

methods.name: body_is_omitting_force_integration
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the body is omitting the standard force integration. See [method body_set_omit_force_integration].

methods.name: body_set_state_sync_callback
methods.description:
Sets the body's state synchronization callback function to [param callable]. Use an empty [Callable] ([code skip-lint]Callable()[/code]) to clear the callback.
The function [param callable] will be called every physics frame, assuming that the body was active during the previous physics tick, and can be used to fetch the latest state from the physics server.
The function [param callable] must take the following parameters:
1. [code]state[/code]: a [PhysicsDirectBodyState2D], used to retrieve the body's state.

methods.name: body_set_force_integration_callback
methods.description:
Sets the body's custom force integration callback function to [param callable]. Use an empty [Callable] ([code skip-lint]Callable()[/code]) to clear the custom callback.
The function [param callable] will be called every physics tick, before the standard force integration (see [method body_set_omit_force_integration]). It can be used for example to update the body's linear and angular velocity based on contact with other bodies.
If [param userdata] is not [code]null[/code], the function [param callable] must take the following two parameters:
1. [code]state[/code]: a [PhysicsDirectBodyState2D] used to retrieve and modify the body's state,
2. [code skip-lint]userdata[/code]: a [Variant]; its value will be the [param userdata] passed into this method.
If [param userdata] is [code]null[/code], then [param callable] must take only the [code]state[/code] parameter.

methods.name: body_test_motion
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if a collision would result from moving the body along a motion vector from a given point in space. See [PhysicsTestMotionParameters2D] for the available motion parameters. Optionally a [PhysicsTestMotionResult2D] object can be passed, which will be used to store the information about the resulting collision.

methods.name: body_get_direct_state
methods.description: Returns the [PhysicsDirectBodyState2D] of the body. Returns [code]null[/code] if the body is destroyed or not assigned to a space.

methods.name: joint_create
methods.description: Creates a 2D joint in the physics server, and returns the [RID] that identifies it. To set the joint type, use [method joint_make_damped_spring], [method joint_make_groove] or [method joint_make_pin]. Use [method joint_set_param] to set generic joint parameters.

methods.name: joint_clear
methods.description: Destroys the joint with the given [RID], creates a new uninitialized joint, and makes the [RID] refer to this new joint.

methods.name: joint_set_param
methods.description: Sets the value of the given joint parameter.

methods.name: joint_get_param
methods.description: Returns the value of the given joint parameter.

methods.name: joint_disable_collisions_between_bodies
methods.description: Sets whether the bodies attached to the [Joint2D] will collide with each other.

methods.name: joint_is_disabled_collisions_between_bodies
methods.description: Returns whether the bodies attached to the [Joint2D] will collide with each other.

methods.name: joint_make_pin
methods.description: Makes the joint a pin joint. If [param body_b] is an empty [RID], then [param body_a] is pinned to the point [param anchor] (given in global coordinates); otherwise, [param body_a] is pinned to [param body_b] at the point [param anchor] (given in global coordinates). To set the parameters which are specific to the pin joint, see [method pin_joint_set_param].

methods.name: joint_make_groove
methods.description: Makes the joint a groove joint.

methods.name: joint_make_damped_spring
methods.description: Makes the joint a damped spring joint, attached at the point [param anchor_a] (given in global coordinates) on the body [param body_a] and at the point [param anchor_b] (given in global coordinates) on the body [param body_b]. To set the parameters which are specific to the damped spring, see [method damped_spring_joint_set_param].

methods.name: pin_joint_set_flag
methods.description: Sets a pin joint flag.

methods.name: pin_joint_get_flag
methods.description: Gets a pin joint flag.

methods.name: pin_joint_set_param
methods.description: Sets a pin joint parameter.

methods.name: pin_joint_get_param
methods.description: Returns the value of a pin joint parameter.

methods.name: damped_spring_joint_set_param
methods.description: Sets the value of the given damped spring joint parameter.

methods.name: damped_spring_joint_get_param
methods.description: Returns the value of the given damped spring joint parameter.

methods.name: joint_get_type
methods.description: Returns the joint's type.

methods.name: free_rid
methods.description: Destroys any of the objects created by PhysicsServer2D. If the [RID] passed is not one of the objects that can be created by PhysicsServer2D, an error will be printed to the console.

methods.name: set_active
methods.description: Activates or deactivates the 2D physics server. If [param active] is [code]false[/code], then the physics server will not do anything in its physics step.

methods.name: get_process_info
methods.description: Returns the value of a physics engine state specified by [param process_info].

classes.brief_description: A server interface for low-level 2D physics access.
classes.description:
PhysicsServer2D is the server responsible for all 2D physics. It can directly create and manipulate all physics objects:
- A [i]space[/i] is a self-contained world for a physics simulation. It contains bodies, areas, and joints. Its state can be queried for collision and intersection information, and several parameters of the simulation can be modified.
- A [i]shape[/i] is a geometric shape such as a circle, a rectangle, a capsule, or a polygon. It can be used for collision detection by adding it to a body/area, possibly with an extra transformation relative to the body/area's origin. Bodies/areas can have multiple (transformed) shapes added to them, and a single shape can be added to bodies/areas multiple times with different local transformations.
- A [i]body[/i] is a physical object which can be in static, kinematic, or rigid mode. Its state (such as position and velocity) can be queried and updated. A force integration callback can be set to customize the body's physics.
- An [i]area[/i] is a region in space which can be used to detect bodies and areas entering and exiting it. A body monitoring callback can be set to report entering/exiting body shapes, and similarly an area monitoring callback can be set. Gravity and damping can be overridden within the area by setting area parameters.
- A [i]joint[/i] is a constraint, either between two bodies or on one body relative to a point. Parameters such as the joint bias and the rest length of a spring joint can be adjusted.
Physics objects in [PhysicsServer2D] may be created and manipulated independently; they do not have to be tied to nodes in the scene tree.
[b]Note:[/b] All the 2D physics nodes use the physics server internally. Adding a physics node to the scene tree will cause a corresponding physics object to be created in the physics server. A rigid body node registers a callback that updates the node's transform with the transform of the respective body object in the physics server (every physics update). An area node registers a callback to inform the area node about overlaps with the respective area object in the physics server. The raycast node queries the direct state of the relevant space in the physics server.

methods.name: _step
methods.description:
Called every physics step to process the physics simulation. [param step] is the time elapsed since the last physics step, in seconds. It is usually the same as the value returned by [method Node.get_physics_process_delta_time].
Overridable version of [PhysicsServer2D]'s internal [code skip-lint]step[/code] method.

methods.name: _sync
methods.description:

methods.name: _end_sync
methods.description:
Called to indicate that the physics server has stopped synchronizing. It is in the loop's iteration/physics phase, and can access physics objects even if running on a separate thread. See also [method _sync].
Overridable version of [PhysicsServer2D]'s internal [code]end_sync[/code] method.

methods.name: _finish
methods.description:

Overridable version of [PhysicsServer2D]'s internal [code]finish[/code] method.

classes.brief_description: Provides virtual methods that can be overridden to create custom [PhysicsServer2D] implementations.
classes.description:
This class extends [PhysicsServer2D] by providing additional virtual methods that can be overridden. When these methods are overridden, they will be called instead of the internal methods of the physics server.
Intended for use with GDExtension to create custom implementations of [PhysicsServer2D].

classes.name: PhysicsServer2DManager

methods.name: register_server
methods.description: Register a [PhysicsServer2D] implementation by passing a [param name] and a [Callable] that returns a [PhysicsServer2D] object.

methods.name: set_default_server
methods.description: Set the default [PhysicsServer2D] implementation to the one identified by [param name], if [param priority] is greater than the priority of the current default implementation.

classes.brief_description: A singleton for managing [PhysicsServer2D] implementations.
classes.description:
[PhysicsServer2DManager] is the API for registering [PhysicsServer2D] implementations and for setting the default implementation.
[b]Note:[/b] It is not possible to switch physics servers at runtime. This class is only used on startup at the server initialization level, by Godot itself and possibly by GDExtensions.

values.description: The [Joint3D] is a [PinJoint3D].

values.description: The [Joint3D] is a [HingeJoint3D].

values.name: JOINT_TYPE_SLIDER
values.description: The [Joint3D] is a [SliderJoint3D].

values.name: JOINT_TYPE_CONE_TWIST
values.description: The [Joint3D] is a [ConeTwistJoint3D].

values.name: JOINT_TYPE_6DOF
values.description: The [Joint3D] is a [Generic6DOFJoint3D].

values.name: JOINT_TYPE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum JointType] enum.

values.name: PIN_JOINT_BIAS
values.description:
The strength with which the pinned objects try to stay in positional relation to each other. The higher, the stronger.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: PIN_JOINT_DAMPING
values.description:
The strength with which the pinned objects try to stay in velocity relation to each other. The higher, the stronger.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: PIN_JOINT_IMPULSE_CLAMP
values.description:
If above 0, this value is the maximum value for an impulse that this Joint3D puts on its ends.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: HINGE_JOINT_BIAS
values.description:
The speed with which the two bodies get pulled together when they move in different directions.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: HINGE_JOINT_LIMIT_UPPER
values.description: The maximum rotation across the Hinge.

values.name: HINGE_JOINT_LIMIT_LOWER
values.description: The minimum rotation across the Hinge.

values.name: HINGE_JOINT_LIMIT_BIAS
values.description:
The speed with which the rotation across the axis perpendicular to the hinge gets corrected.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: HINGE_JOINT_LIMIT_SOFTNESS
values.description: [b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: HINGE_JOINT_LIMIT_RELAXATION
values.description:
The lower this value, the more the rotation gets slowed down.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: HINGE_JOINT_MOTOR_TARGET_VELOCITY
values.description: Target speed for the motor.

values.name: HINGE_JOINT_MOTOR_MAX_IMPULSE
values.description: Maximum acceleration for the motor.

values.name: HINGE_JOINT_FLAG_USE_LIMIT
values.description: If [code]true[/code], the Hinge has a maximum and a minimum rotation.

values.name: HINGE_JOINT_FLAG_ENABLE_MOTOR
values.description: If [code]true[/code], a motor turns the Hinge.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_LINEAR_LIMIT_UPPER
values.description: The maximum difference between the pivot points on their X axis before damping happens.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_LINEAR_LIMIT_LOWER
values.description: The minimum difference between the pivot points on their X axis before damping happens.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_LINEAR_LIMIT_SOFTNESS
values.description:
A factor applied to the movement across the slider axis once the limits get surpassed. The lower, the slower the movement.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_LINEAR_LIMIT_RESTITUTION
values.description:
The amount of restitution once the limits are surpassed. The lower, the more velocity-energy gets lost.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_LINEAR_LIMIT_DAMPING
values.description:
The amount of damping once the slider limits are surpassed.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_LINEAR_MOTION_SOFTNESS
values.description:
A factor applied to the movement across the slider axis as long as the slider is in the limits. The lower, the slower the movement.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_LINEAR_MOTION_RESTITUTION
values.description:
The amount of restitution inside the slider limits.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_LINEAR_MOTION_DAMPING
values.description:
The amount of damping inside the slider limits.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_LINEAR_ORTHOGONAL_SOFTNESS
values.description:
A factor applied to the movement across axes orthogonal to the slider.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_LINEAR_ORTHOGONAL_RESTITUTION
values.description:
The amount of restitution when movement is across axes orthogonal to the slider.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_LINEAR_ORTHOGONAL_DAMPING
values.description:
The amount of damping when movement is across axes orthogonal to the slider.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_ANGULAR_LIMIT_UPPER
values.description:
The upper limit of rotation in the slider.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_ANGULAR_LIMIT_LOWER
values.description:
The lower limit of rotation in the slider.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_ANGULAR_LIMIT_SOFTNESS
values.description:
A factor applied to the all rotation once the limit is surpassed.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_ANGULAR_LIMIT_RESTITUTION
values.description:
The amount of restitution of the rotation when the limit is surpassed.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_ANGULAR_LIMIT_DAMPING
values.description:
The amount of damping of the rotation when the limit is surpassed.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_ANGULAR_MOTION_SOFTNESS
values.description:
A factor that gets applied to the all rotation in the limits.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_ANGULAR_MOTION_RESTITUTION
values.description:
The amount of restitution of the rotation in the limits.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_ANGULAR_MOTION_DAMPING
values.description:
The amount of damping of the rotation in the limits.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_ANGULAR_ORTHOGONAL_SOFTNESS
values.description:
A factor that gets applied to the all rotation across axes orthogonal to the slider.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_ANGULAR_ORTHOGONAL_RESTITUTION
values.description:
The amount of restitution of the rotation across axes orthogonal to the slider.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_ANGULAR_ORTHOGONAL_DAMPING
values.description:
The amount of damping of the rotation across axes orthogonal to the slider.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: SLIDER_JOINT_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum SliderJointParam] enum.

values.name: CONE_TWIST_JOINT_SWING_SPAN
values.description:
Swing is rotation from side to side, around the axis perpendicular to the twist axis.
The swing span defines, how much rotation will not get corrected along the swing axis.
Could be defined as looseness in the [ConeTwistJoint3D]. If below 0.05, this behavior is locked.

values.name: CONE_TWIST_JOINT_TWIST_SPAN
values.description: Twist is the rotation around the twist axis, this value defined how far the joint can twist. Twist is locked if below 0.05.

values.name: CONE_TWIST_JOINT_BIAS
values.description:
The speed with which the swing or twist will take place. The higher, the faster.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: CONE_TWIST_JOINT_SOFTNESS
values.description:
The ease with which the Joint3D twists, if it's too low, it takes more force to twist the joint.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: CONE_TWIST_JOINT_RELAXATION
values.description:
Defines, how fast the swing- and twist-speed-difference on both sides gets synced.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_LINEAR_LOWER_LIMIT
values.description: The minimum difference between the pivot points' axes.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_LINEAR_UPPER_LIMIT
values.description: The maximum difference between the pivot points' axes.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_LINEAR_LIMIT_SOFTNESS
values.description:
A factor that gets applied to the movement across the axes. The lower, the slower the movement.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_LINEAR_RESTITUTION
values.description:
The amount of restitution on the axes movement. The lower, the more velocity-energy gets lost.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_LINEAR_DAMPING
values.description:
The amount of damping that happens at the linear motion across the axes.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_LINEAR_MOTOR_TARGET_VELOCITY
values.description: The velocity that the joint's linear motor will attempt to reach.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_LINEAR_MOTOR_FORCE_LIMIT
values.description: The maximum force that the linear motor can apply while trying to reach the target velocity.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_ANGULAR_LOWER_LIMIT
values.description: The minimum rotation in negative direction to break loose and rotate around the axes.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_ANGULAR_UPPER_LIMIT
values.description: The minimum rotation in positive direction to break loose and rotate around the axes.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_ANGULAR_LIMIT_SOFTNESS
values.description:
A factor that gets multiplied onto all rotations across the axes.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_ANGULAR_DAMPING
values.description:
The amount of rotational damping across the axes. The lower, the more damping occurs.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_ANGULAR_RESTITUTION
values.description:
The amount of rotational restitution across the axes. The lower, the more restitution occurs.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_ANGULAR_FORCE_LIMIT
values.description:
The maximum amount of force that can occur, when rotating around the axes.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_ANGULAR_ERP
values.description:
When correcting the crossing of limits in rotation across the axes, this error tolerance factor defines how much the correction gets slowed down. The lower, the slower.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using GodotPhysics3D. This parameter is ignored when using Jolt Physics.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_ANGULAR_MOTOR_TARGET_VELOCITY
values.description: Target speed for the motor at the axes.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_ANGULAR_MOTOR_FORCE_LIMIT
values.description: Maximum acceleration for the motor at the axes.

values.description: Represents the size of the [enum G6DOFJointAxisParam] enum.

values.description: If set, linear motion is possible within the given limits.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_FLAG_ENABLE_ANGULAR_LIMIT
values.description: If set, rotational motion is possible.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_FLAG_ENABLE_MOTOR
values.description: If set, there is a rotational motor across these axes.

values.name: G6DOF_JOINT_FLAG_ENABLE_LINEAR_MOTOR
values.description: If set, there is a linear motor on this axis that targets a specific velocity.

values.description: Constant for creating a capsule shape (used by the [CapsuleShape3D] resource).
