values.name: LIGHT_PARAM_SPOT_ATTENUATION
values.description: The spotlight's attenuation.

values.name: LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_MAX_DISTANCE
values.description: The maximum distance for shadow splits. Increasing this value will make directional shadows visible from further away, at the cost of lower overall shadow detail and performance (since more objects need to be included in the directional shadow rendering).

values.name: LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_SPLIT_1_OFFSET
values.description: Proportion of shadow atlas occupied by the first split.

values.name: LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_SPLIT_2_OFFSET
values.description: Proportion of shadow atlas occupied by the second split.

values.name: LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_SPLIT_3_OFFSET
values.description: Proportion of shadow atlas occupied by the third split. The fourth split occupies the rest.

values.name: LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_FADE_START
values.description: Proportion of shadow max distance where the shadow will start to fade out.

values.name: LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_NORMAL_BIAS
values.description: Normal bias used to offset shadow lookup by object normal. Can be used to fix self-shadowing artifacts.

values.name: LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_BIAS
values.description: Bias for the shadow lookup to fix self-shadowing artifacts.

values.name: LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_PANCAKE_SIZE
values.description: Sets the size of the directional shadow pancake. The pancake offsets the start of the shadow's camera frustum to provide a higher effective depth resolution for the shadow. However, a high pancake size can cause artifacts in the shadows of large objects that are close to the edge of the frustum. Reducing the pancake size can help. Setting the size to [code]0[/code] turns off the pancaking effect.

values.name: LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_OPACITY
values.description: The light's shadow opacity. Values lower than [code]1.0[/code] make the light appear through shadows. This can be used to fake global illumination at a low performance cost.

values.name: LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_BLUR
values.description: Blurs the edges of the shadow. Can be used to hide pixel artifacts in low resolution shadow maps. A high value can make shadows appear grainy and can cause other unwanted artifacts. Try to keep as near default as possible.

values.name: LIGHT_PARAM_INTENSITY
values.description: Constant representing the intensity of the light, measured in Lumens when dealing with a [SpotLight3D] or [OmniLight3D], or measured in Lux with a [DirectionalLight3D]. Only used when [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units] is [code]true[/code].

values.name: LIGHT_PARAM_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum LightParam] enum.

values.name: LIGHT_BAKE_DISABLED
values.description: Light is ignored when baking. This is the fastest mode, but the light will be taken into account when baking global illumination. This mode should generally be used for dynamic lights that change quickly, as the effect of global illumination is less noticeable on those lights.

values.name: LIGHT_BAKE_STATIC
values.description: Light is taken into account in static baking ([VoxelGI], [LightmapGI], SDFGI ([member Environment.sdfgi_enabled])). The light can be moved around or modified, but its global illumination will not update in real-time. This is suitable for subtle changes (such as flickering torches), but generally not large changes such as toggling a light on and off.

values.name: LIGHT_BAKE_DYNAMIC
values.description: Light is taken into account in dynamic baking ([VoxelGI] and SDFGI ([member Environment.sdfgi_enabled]) only). The light can be moved around or modified with global illumination updating in real-time. The light's global illumination appearance will be slightly different compared to [constant LIGHT_BAKE_STATIC]. This has a greater performance cost compared to [constant LIGHT_BAKE_STATIC]. When using SDFGI, the update speed of dynamic lights is affected by [member ProjectSettings.rendering/global_illumination/sdfgi/frames_to_update_lights].

values.name: LIGHT_OMNI_SHADOW_DUAL_PARABOLOID
values.description: Use a dual paraboloid shadow map for omni lights.

values.name: LIGHT_OMNI_SHADOW_CUBE
values.description: Use a cubemap shadow map for omni lights. Slower but better quality than dual paraboloid.

values.name: LIGHT_DIRECTIONAL_SHADOW_ORTHOGONAL
values.description: Use orthogonal shadow projection for directional light.

values.name: LIGHT_DIRECTIONAL_SHADOW_PARALLEL_2_SPLITS
values.description: Use 2 splits for shadow projection when using directional light.

values.name: LIGHT_DIRECTIONAL_SHADOW_PARALLEL_4_SPLITS
values.description: Use 4 splits for shadow projection when using directional light.

values.name: LIGHT_DIRECTIONAL_SKY_MODE_LIGHT_AND_SKY
values.description: Use DirectionalLight3D in both sky rendering and scene lighting.

values.name: LIGHT_DIRECTIONAL_SKY_MODE_LIGHT_ONLY
values.description: Only use DirectionalLight3D in scene lighting.

values.name: LIGHT_DIRECTIONAL_SKY_MODE_SKY_ONLY
values.description: Only use DirectionalLight3D in sky rendering.

values.name: SHADOW_QUALITY_HARD
values.description:
Lowest shadow filtering quality (fastest). Soft shadows are not available with this quality setting, which means the [member Light3D.shadow_blur] property is ignored if [member Light3D.light_size] and [member Light3D.light_angular_distance] is [code]0.0[/code].
[b]Note:[/b] The variable shadow blur performed by [member Light3D.light_size] and [member Light3D.light_angular_distance] is still effective when using hard shadow filtering. In this case, [member Light3D.shadow_blur] [i]is[/i] taken into account. However, the results will not be blurred, instead the blur amount is treated as a maximum radius for the penumbra.

values.name: SHADOW_QUALITY_SOFT_VERY_LOW
values.description: Very low shadow filtering quality (faster). When using this quality setting, [member Light3D.shadow_blur] is automatically multiplied by 0.75× to avoid introducing too much noise. This division only applies to lights whose [member Light3D.light_size] or [member Light3D.light_angular_distance] is [code]0.0[/code]).

values.name: SHADOW_QUALITY_SOFT_LOW
values.description: Low shadow filtering quality (fast).

values.name: SHADOW_QUALITY_SOFT_MEDIUM
values.description: Medium low shadow filtering quality (average).

values.name: SHADOW_QUALITY_SOFT_HIGH
values.description: High low shadow filtering quality (slow). When using this quality setting, [member Light3D.shadow_blur] is automatically multiplied by 1.5× to better make use of the high sample count. This increased blur also improves the stability of dynamic object shadows. This multiplier only applies to lights whose [member Light3D.light_size] or [member Light3D.light_angular_distance] is [code]0.0[/code]).

values.name: SHADOW_QUALITY_SOFT_ULTRA
values.description: Highest low shadow filtering quality (slowest). When using this quality setting, [member Light3D.shadow_blur] is automatically multiplied by 2× to better make use of the high sample count. This increased blur also improves the stability of dynamic object shadows. This multiplier only applies to lights whose [member Light3D.light_size] or [member Light3D.light_angular_distance] is [code]0.0[/code]).

values.name: SHADOW_QUALITY_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum ShadowQuality] enum.

values.name: REFLECTION_PROBE_UPDATE_ONCE
values.description: Reflection probe will update reflections once and then stop.

values.name: REFLECTION_PROBE_UPDATE_ALWAYS
values.description: Reflection probe will update each frame. This mode is necessary to capture moving objects.

values.name: REFLECTION_PROBE_AMBIENT_DISABLED
values.description: Do not apply any ambient lighting inside the reflection probe's box defined by its size.

values.name: REFLECTION_PROBE_AMBIENT_ENVIRONMENT
values.description: Apply automatically-sourced environment lighting inside the reflection probe's box defined by its size.

values.name: REFLECTION_PROBE_AMBIENT_COLOR
values.description: Apply custom ambient lighting inside the reflection probe's box defined by its size. See [method reflection_probe_set_ambient_color] and [method reflection_probe_set_ambient_energy].

values.name: DECAL_TEXTURE_ALBEDO
values.description: Albedo texture slot in a decal ([member Decal.texture_albedo]).

values.name: DECAL_TEXTURE_NORMAL
values.description: Normal map texture slot in a decal ([member Decal.texture_normal]).

values.name: DECAL_TEXTURE_ORM
values.description: Occlusion/Roughness/Metallic texture slot in a decal ([member Decal.texture_orm]).

values.name: DECAL_TEXTURE_EMISSION
values.description: Emission texture slot in a decal ([member Decal.texture_emission]).

values.name: DECAL_TEXTURE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum DecalTexture] enum.

values.name: DECAL_FILTER_NEAREST
values.description: Nearest-neighbor filter for decals (use for pixel art decals). No mipmaps are used for rendering, which means decals at a distance will look sharp but grainy. This has roughly the same performance cost as using mipmaps.

values.name: DECAL_FILTER_LINEAR
values.description: Linear filter for decals (use for non-pixel art decals). No mipmaps are used for rendering, which means decals at a distance will look smooth but blurry. This has roughly the same performance cost as using mipmaps.

values.name: DECAL_FILTER_NEAREST_MIPMAPS
values.description: Nearest-neighbor filter for decals (use for pixel art decals). Isotropic mipmaps are used for rendering, which means decals at a distance will look smooth but blurry. This has roughly the same performance cost as not using mipmaps.

values.name: DECAL_FILTER_LINEAR_MIPMAPS
values.description: Linear filter for decals (use for non-pixel art decals). Isotropic mipmaps are used for rendering, which means decals at a distance will look smooth but blurry. This has roughly the same performance cost as not using mipmaps.

values.name: DECAL_FILTER_NEAREST_MIPMAPS_ANISOTROPIC
values.description: Nearest-neighbor filter for decals (use for pixel art decals). Anisotropic mipmaps are used for rendering, which means decals at a distance will look smooth and sharp when viewed from oblique angles. This looks better compared to isotropic mipmaps, but is slower. The level of anisotropic filtering is defined by [member ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/anisotropic_filtering_level].

values.name: DECAL_FILTER_LINEAR_MIPMAPS_ANISOTROPIC
values.description: Linear filter for decals (use for non-pixel art decals). Anisotropic mipmaps are used for rendering, which means decals at a distance will look smooth and sharp when viewed from oblique angles. This looks better compared to isotropic mipmaps, but is slower. The level of anisotropic filtering is defined by [member ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/anisotropic_filtering_level].

values.name: VOXEL_GI_QUALITY_LOW
values.description: Low [VoxelGI] rendering quality using 4 cones.

values.name: VOXEL_GI_QUALITY_HIGH
values.description: High [VoxelGI] rendering quality using 6 cones.

values.name: PARTICLES_MODE_2D
values.description: 2D particles.

values.name: PARTICLES_MODE_3D
values.description: 3D particles.

values.name: PARTICLES_TRANSFORM_ALIGN_DISABLED
values.description: Do not align particle transforms relative to the camera or velocity.

values.name: PARTICLES_TRANSFORM_ALIGN_Z_BILLBOARD
values.description: Align each particle's Z axis to face the camera.

values.name: PARTICLES_TRANSFORM_ALIGN_Y_TO_VELOCITY
values.description: Align each particle's Y axis to the velocity vector.

values.name: PARTICLES_TRANSFORM_ALIGN_Z_BILLBOARD_Y_TO_VELOCITY
values.description: Align each particle's Z axis to face the camera and Y axis to the velocity vector.

values.name: PARTICLES_TRANSFORM_ALIGN_LOCAL_BILLBOARD
values.description: Billboard each particles around a local axis.

values.name: PARTICLES_ALIGN_CHANNEL_FILTER_DISABLED
values.description: Do not read from CUSTOM when performing billboarding.

values.name: PARTICLES_ALIGN_CHANNEL_FILTER_X
values.description: Read from [code]CUSTOM.x[/code] when performing billboarding and use it as an angle, in radians.

values.name: PARTICLES_ALIGN_CHANNEL_FILTER_Y
values.description: Read from [code]CUSTOM.y[/code] when performing billboarding and use it as an angle, in radians.

values.name: PARTICLES_ALIGN_CHANNEL_FILTER_Z
values.description: Read from [code]CUSTOM.z[/code] when performing billboarding and use it as an angle, in radians.

values.name: PARTICLES_ALIGN_CHANNEL_FILTER_W
values.description: Read from [code]CUSTOM.w[/code] when performing billboarding and use it as an angle, in radians.

values.name: PARTICLES_ALIGN_AXIS_X
values.description: Use the X axis for local billboarding.

values.name: PARTICLES_ALIGN_AXIS_Y
values.description: Use the Y axis for local billboarding.

values.name: PARTICLES_DRAW_ORDER_INDEX
values.description: Draw particles in the order that they appear in the particles array.

values.name: PARTICLES_DRAW_ORDER_LIFETIME
values.description: Sort particles based on their lifetime. In other words, the particle with the highest lifetime is drawn at the front.

values.name: PARTICLES_DRAW_ORDER_REVERSE_LIFETIME
values.description: Sort particles based on the inverse of their lifetime. In other words, the particle with the lowest lifetime is drawn at the front.

values.name: PARTICLES_DRAW_ORDER_VIEW_DEPTH
values.description: Sort particles based on their distance to the camera.

values.name: PARTICLES_COLLISION_TYPE_SPHERE_ATTRACT
values.description: Sphere attractor type for [GPUParticles3D] (see [GPUParticlesAttractorSphere3D]).

values.name: PARTICLES_COLLISION_TYPE_BOX_ATTRACT
values.description: Box attractor type for [GPUParticles3D] (see [GPUParticlesAttractorBox3D]).

values.name: PARTICLES_COLLISION_TYPE_VECTOR_FIELD_ATTRACT
values.description: Vector field attractor type for [GPUParticles3D] (see [GPUParticlesAttractorVectorField3D]).

values.name: PARTICLES_COLLISION_TYPE_SPHERE_COLLIDE
values.description: Sphere collision type for [GPUParticles3D] (see [GPUParticlesCollisionSphere3D]).

values.name: PARTICLES_COLLISION_TYPE_BOX_COLLIDE
values.description: Box collision type for [GPUParticles3D] (see [GPUParticlesCollisionBox3D]).

values.name: PARTICLES_COLLISION_TYPE_SDF_COLLIDE
values.description: Signed distance field collision type for [GPUParticles3D] (see [GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D]).

values.name: PARTICLES_COLLISION_TYPE_HEIGHTFIELD_COLLIDE
values.description: Heightfield collision type for [GPUParticles3D] (see [GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D]).

values.name: PARTICLES_COLLISION_HEIGHTFIELD_RESOLUTION_256
values.description: 256×256 heightfield resolution for [GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D].

values.name: PARTICLES_COLLISION_HEIGHTFIELD_RESOLUTION_512
values.description: 512×512 heightfield resolution for [GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D].

values.name: PARTICLES_COLLISION_HEIGHTFIELD_RESOLUTION_1024
values.description: 1024×1024 heightfield resolution for [GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D].

values.name: PARTICLES_COLLISION_HEIGHTFIELD_RESOLUTION_2048
values.description: 2048×2048 heightfield resolution for [GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D].

values.name: PARTICLES_COLLISION_HEIGHTFIELD_RESOLUTION_4096
values.description: 4096×4096 heightfield resolution for [GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D].

values.name: PARTICLES_COLLISION_HEIGHTFIELD_RESOLUTION_8192
values.description: 8192×8192 heightfield resolution for [GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D].

values.name: PARTICLES_COLLISION_HEIGHTFIELD_RESOLUTION_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum ParticlesCollisionHeightfieldResolution] enum.

values.name: FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_ELLIPSOID
values.description: [FogVolume] will be shaped like an ellipsoid (stretched sphere).

values.name: FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_CONE
values.description: [FogVolume] will be shaped like a cone pointing upwards (in local coordinates). The cone's angle is set automatically to fill the size. The cone will be adjusted to fit within the size. Rotate the [FogVolume] node to reorient the cone. Non-uniform scaling via size is not supported (scale the [FogVolume] node instead).

values.name: FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_CYLINDER
values.description: [FogVolume] will be shaped like an upright cylinder (in local coordinates). Rotate the [FogVolume] node to reorient the cylinder. The cylinder will be adjusted to fit within the size. Non-uniform scaling via size is not supported (scale the [FogVolume] node instead).

values.name: FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_BOX
values.description: [FogVolume] will be shaped like a box.

values.name: FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_WORLD
values.description: [FogVolume] will have no shape, will cover the whole world and will not be culled.

values.name: FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum FogVolumeShape] enum.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SCALING_3D_MODE_BILINEAR
values.description: Use bilinear scaling for the viewport's 3D buffer. The amount of scaling can be set using [member Viewport.scaling_3d_scale]. Values less than [code]1.0[/code] will result in undersampling while values greater than [code]1.0[/code] will result in supersampling. A value of [code]1.0[/code] disables scaling.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SCALING_3D_MODE_FSR
values.description: Use AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0 upscaling for the viewport's 3D buffer. The amount of scaling can be set using [member Viewport.scaling_3d_scale]. Values less than [code]1.0[/code] will result in the viewport being upscaled using FSR. Values greater than [code]1.0[/code] are not supported and bilinear downsampling will be used instead. A value of [code]1.0[/code] disables scaling.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SCALING_3D_MODE_FSR2
values.description: Use AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 2.2 upscaling for the viewport's 3D buffer. The amount of scaling can be set using [member Viewport.scaling_3d_scale]. Values less than [code]1.0[/code] will result in the viewport being upscaled using FSR2. Values greater than [code]1.0[/code] are not supported and bilinear downsampling will be used instead. A value of [code]1.0[/code] will use FSR2 at native resolution as a TAA solution.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SCALING_3D_MODE_METALFX_SPATIAL
values.description:
Use MetalFX spatial upscaling for the viewport's 3D buffer. The amount of scaling can be set using [member Viewport.scaling_3d_scale]. Values less than [code]1.0[/code] will result in the viewport being upscaled using MetalFX. Values greater than [code]1.0[/code] are not supported and bilinear downsampling will be used instead. A value of [code]1.0[/code] disables scaling.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when the Metal rendering driver is in use, which limits this scaling mode to macOS and iOS.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SCALING_3D_MODE_METALFX_TEMPORAL
values.description:
Use MetalFX temporal upscaling for the viewport's 3D buffer. The amount of scaling can be set using [member Viewport.scaling_3d_scale]. Values less than [code]1.0[/code] will result in the viewport being upscaled using MetalFX. Values greater than [code]1.0[/code] are not supported and bilinear downsampling will be used instead. A value of [code]1.0[/code] will use MetalFX at native resolution as a TAA solution.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when the Metal rendering driver is in use, which limits this scaling mode to macOS and iOS.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SCALING_3D_MODE_NEAREST
values.description:
Use nearest-neighbor filtering for the viewport's 3D buffer. This looks crisper than [constant VIEWPORT_SCALING_3D_MODE_BILINEAR] and has no additional rendering cost. The amount of scaling can be set using [member Viewport.scaling_3d_scale]. Values greater than [code]1.0[/code] are not supported and bilinear downsampling will be used instead. A value of [code]1.0[/code] disables scaling.
[b]Note:[/b] When using the [b]Nearest[/b] scaling mode, to avoid uneven pixel scaling, it's highly recommended to use a value equal to an integer divisor with a dividend of [code]1[/code]. For example, it's best to use a scale of [code]0.5[/code] (1/2), [code]0.3333[/code] (1/3), [code]0.25[/code] (1/4), [code]0.2[/code] (1/5), and so on.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SCALING_3D_MODE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum ViewportScaling3DMode] enum.

values.name: VIEWPORT_UPDATE_DISABLED
values.description: Do not update the viewport's render target.

values.name: VIEWPORT_UPDATE_ONCE
values.description: Update the viewport's render target once, then switch to [constant VIEWPORT_UPDATE_DISABLED].

values.name: VIEWPORT_UPDATE_WHEN_VISIBLE
values.description: Update the viewport's render target only when it is visible. This is the default value.

values.name: VIEWPORT_UPDATE_WHEN_PARENT_VISIBLE
values.description: Update the viewport's render target only when its parent is visible.

values.name: VIEWPORT_UPDATE_ALWAYS
values.description: Always update the viewport's render target.

values.name: VIEWPORT_CLEAR_ALWAYS
values.description: Always clear the viewport's render target before drawing.

values.name: VIEWPORT_CLEAR_NEVER
values.description: Never clear the viewport's render target.

values.name: VIEWPORT_CLEAR_ONLY_NEXT_FRAME
values.description: Clear the viewport's render target on the next frame, then switch to [constant VIEWPORT_CLEAR_NEVER].

values.name: VIEWPORT_ENVIRONMENT_DISABLED
values.description: Disable rendering of 3D environment over 2D canvas.

values.name: VIEWPORT_ENVIRONMENT_ENABLED
values.description: Enable rendering of 3D environment over 2D canvas.

values.name: VIEWPORT_ENVIRONMENT_INHERIT
values.description: Inherit enable/disable value from parent. If the topmost parent is also set to [constant VIEWPORT_ENVIRONMENT_INHERIT], then this has the same behavior as [constant VIEWPORT_ENVIRONMENT_ENABLED].

values.name: VIEWPORT_ENVIRONMENT_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum ViewportEnvironmentMode] enum.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SDF_OVERSIZE_100_PERCENT
values.description: Do not oversize the 2D signed distance field. Occluders may disappear when touching the viewport's edges, and [GPUParticles3D] collision may stop working earlier than intended. This has the lowest GPU requirements.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SDF_OVERSIZE_120_PERCENT
values.description: 2D signed distance field covers 20% of the viewport's size outside the viewport on each side (top, right, bottom, left).

values.name: VIEWPORT_SDF_OVERSIZE_150_PERCENT
values.description: 2D signed distance field covers 50% of the viewport's size outside the viewport on each side (top, right, bottom, left).

values.name: VIEWPORT_SDF_OVERSIZE_200_PERCENT
values.description: 2D signed distance field covers 100% of the viewport's size outside the viewport on each side (top, right, bottom, left). This has the highest GPU requirements.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SDF_OVERSIZE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum ViewportSDFOversize] enum.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SDF_SCALE_100_PERCENT
values.description: Full resolution 2D signed distance field scale. This has the highest GPU requirements.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SDF_SCALE_50_PERCENT
values.description: Half resolution 2D signed distance field scale on each axis (25% of the viewport pixel count).

values.name: VIEWPORT_SDF_SCALE_25_PERCENT
values.description: Quarter resolution 2D signed distance field scale on each axis (6.25% of the viewport pixel count). This has the lowest GPU requirements.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SDF_SCALE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum ViewportSDFScale] enum.

values.name: VIEWPORT_MSAA_DISABLED
values.description: Multisample antialiasing for 3D is disabled. This is the default value, and also the fastest setting.

values.name: VIEWPORT_MSAA_2X
values.description: Multisample antialiasing uses 2 samples per pixel for 3D. This has a moderate impact on performance.

values.name: VIEWPORT_MSAA_4X
values.description: Multisample antialiasing uses 4 samples per pixel for 3D. This has a high impact on performance.

values.name: VIEWPORT_MSAA_8X
values.description: Multisample antialiasing uses 8 samples per pixel for 3D. This has a very high impact on performance. Likely unsupported on low-end and older hardware.

values.name: VIEWPORT_MSAA_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum ViewportMSAA] enum.

values.name: VIEWPORT_ANISOTROPY_DISABLED
values.description: Anisotropic filtering is disabled.

values.name: VIEWPORT_ANISOTROPY_2X
values.description: Use 2× anisotropic filtering.

values.name: VIEWPORT_ANISOTROPY_4X
values.description: Use 4× anisotropic filtering. This is the default value.

values.name: VIEWPORT_ANISOTROPY_8X
values.description: Use 8× anisotropic filtering.

values.name: VIEWPORT_ANISOTROPY_16X
values.description: Use 16× anisotropic filtering.

values.name: VIEWPORT_ANISOTROPY_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum ViewportAnisotropicFiltering] enum.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SCREEN_SPACE_AA_DISABLED
values.description: Do not perform any antialiasing in the full screen post-process.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SCREEN_SPACE_AA_FXAA
values.description: Use fast approximate antialiasing. FXAA is a popular screen-space antialiasing method, which is fast but will make the image look blurry, especially at lower resolutions. It can still work relatively well at large resolutions such as 1440p and 4K.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SCREEN_SPACE_AA_SMAA
values.description: Use subpixel morphological antialiasing. SMAA may produce clearer results than FXAA, but at a slightly higher performance cost.

values.name: VIEWPORT_SCREEN_SPACE_AA_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum ViewportScreenSpaceAA] enum.

values.name: VIEWPORT_OCCLUSION_BUILD_QUALITY_LOW
values.description: Low occlusion culling BVH build quality (as defined by Embree). Results in the lowest CPU usage, but least effective culling.

values.name: VIEWPORT_OCCLUSION_BUILD_QUALITY_MEDIUM
values.description: Medium occlusion culling BVH build quality (as defined by Embree).

values.name: VIEWPORT_OCCLUSION_BUILD_QUALITY_HIGH
values.description: High occlusion culling BVH build quality (as defined by Embree). Results in the highest CPU usage, but most effective culling.

values.name: VIEWPORT_RENDER_INFO_OBJECTS_IN_FRAME
values.description: Number of objects drawn in a single frame.

values.name: VIEWPORT_RENDER_INFO_PRIMITIVES_IN_FRAME
values.description: Number of points, lines, or triangles drawn in a single frame.

values.name: VIEWPORT_RENDER_INFO_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME
values.description: Number of draw calls during this frame.

values.name: VIEWPORT_RENDER_INFO_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum ViewportRenderInfo] enum.

values.name: VIEWPORT_RENDER_INFO_TYPE_VISIBLE
values.description: Visible render pass (excluding shadows).

values.name: VIEWPORT_RENDER_INFO_TYPE_SHADOW
values.description: Shadow render pass. Objects will be rendered several times depending on the number of amounts of lights with shadows and the number of directional shadow splits.

values.name: VIEWPORT_RENDER_INFO_TYPE_CANVAS
values.description: Canvas item rendering. This includes all 2D rendering.

values.name: VIEWPORT_RENDER_INFO_TYPE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum ViewportRenderInfoType] enum.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_DISABLED
values.description: Debug draw is disabled. Default setting.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_UNSHADED
values.description: Objects are displayed without light information.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_LIGHTING
values.description:
Objects are displayed with only light information.
[b]Note:[/b] When using this debug draw mode, custom shaders are ignored since all materials in the scene temporarily use a debug material. This means the result from custom shader functions (such as vertex displacement) won't be visible anymore when using this debug draw mode.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_OVERDRAW
values.description:
Objects are displayed semi-transparent with additive blending so you can see where they are drawing over top of one another. A higher overdraw (represented by brighter colors) means you are wasting performance on drawing pixels that are being hidden behind others.
[b]Note:[/b] When using this debug draw mode, custom shaders are ignored since all materials in the scene temporarily use a debug material. This means the result from custom shader functions (such as vertex displacement) won't be visible anymore when using this debug draw mode.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_WIREFRAME
values.description:
Debug draw draws objects in wireframe.
[b]Note:[/b] [method set_debug_generate_wireframes] must be called before loading any meshes for wireframes to be visible when using the Compatibility renderer.
[b]Note:[/b] In the Compatibility renderer, backfaces are always visible when using wireframe rendering. In the Forward+ and Mobile renderers, wireframes follow the material's backface culling properties instead.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_NORMAL_BUFFER
values.description: Normal buffer is drawn instead of regular scene so you can see the per-pixel normals that will be used by post-processing effects.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_VOXEL_GI_ALBEDO
values.description:
Objects are displayed with only the albedo value from [VoxelGI]s. Requires at least one visible [VoxelGI] node that has been baked to have a visible effect.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_VOXEL_GI_LIGHTING
values.description:
Objects are displayed with only the lighting value from [VoxelGI]s. Requires at least one visible [VoxelGI] node that has been baked to have a visible effect.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_VOXEL_GI_EMISSION
values.description:
Objects are displayed with only the emission color from [VoxelGI]s. Requires at least one visible [VoxelGI] node that has been baked to have a visible effect.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SHADOW_ATLAS
values.description: Draws the shadow atlas that stores shadows from [OmniLight3D]s and [SpotLight3D]s in the upper left quadrant of the [Viewport].

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_DIRECTIONAL_SHADOW_ATLAS
values.description:
Draws the shadow atlas that stores shadows from [DirectionalLight3D]s in the upper left quadrant of the [Viewport].
The slice of the camera frustum related to the shadow map cascade is superimposed to visualize coverage. The color of each slice matches the colors used for [constant VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_PSSM_SPLITS]. When shadow cascades are blended the overlap is taken into account when drawing the frustum slices.
The last cascade shows all frustum slices to illustrate the coverage of all slices.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SCENE_LUMINANCE
values.description:
Draws the estimated scene luminance. This is a 1×1 texture that is generated when autoexposure is enabled to control the scene's exposure.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ or Mobile rendering methods.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SSAO
values.description:
Draws the screen space ambient occlusion texture instead of the scene so that you can clearly see how it is affecting objects. In order for this display mode to work, you must have [member Environment.ssao_enabled] set in your [WorldEnvironment].
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SSIL
values.description:
Draws the screen space indirect lighting texture instead of the scene so that you can clearly see how it is affecting objects. In order for this display mode to work, you must have [member Environment.ssil_enabled] set in your [WorldEnvironment].
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_PSSM_SPLITS
values.description:
Colors each PSSM split for the [DirectionalLight3D]s in the scene a different color so you can see where the splits are. In order (from closest to furthest from the camera), they are colored red, green, blue, and yellow.
[b]Note:[/b] When using this debug draw mode, custom shaders are ignored since all materials in the scene temporarily use a debug material. This means the result from custom shader functions (such as vertex displacement) won't be visible anymore when using this debug draw mode.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ or Mobile rendering methods.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_DECAL_ATLAS
values.description:
Draws the decal atlas that stores decal textures from [Decal]s.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ or Mobile rendering methods.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SDFGI
values.description:
Draws SDFGI cascade data. This is the data structure that is used to bounce lighting against and create reflections.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SDFGI_PROBES
values.description:
Draws SDFGI probe data. This is the data structure that is used to give indirect lighting dynamic objects moving within the scene.
When in the editor, left-clicking a probe will display additional bright dots that show its occlusion information. A white dot means the light is not occluded at all at the dot's position, while a red dot means the light is fully occluded. Intermediate values are possible.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_GI_BUFFER
values.description:
Draws the global illumination buffer from [VoxelGI] or SDFGI. Requires [VoxelGI] (at least one visible baked VoxelGI node) or SDFGI ([member Environment.sdfgi_enabled]) to be enabled to have a visible effect.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_DISABLE_LOD
values.description: Disable mesh LOD. All meshes are drawn with full detail, which can be used to compare performance.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_CLUSTER_OMNI_LIGHTS
values.description:
Draws the [OmniLight3D] cluster. Clustering determines where lights are positioned in screen-space, which allows the engine to only process these portions of the screen for lighting.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_CLUSTER_SPOT_LIGHTS
values.description:
Draws the [SpotLight3D] cluster. Clustering determines where lights are positioned in screen-space, which allows the engine to only process these portions of the screen for lighting.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_CLUSTER_DECALS
values.description:
Draws the [Decal] cluster. Clustering determines where decals are positioned in screen-space, which allows the engine to only process these portions of the screen for decals.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_CLUSTER_REFLECTION_PROBES
values.description:
Draws the [ReflectionProbe] cluster. Clustering determines where reflection probes are positioned in screen-space, which allows the engine to only process these portions of the screen for reflection probes.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_OCCLUDERS
values.description:
Draws the occlusion culling buffer. This low-resolution occlusion culling buffer is rasterized on the CPU and is used to check whether instances are occluded by other objects.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ or Mobile rendering methods.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_MOTION_VECTORS
values.description:
Draws the motion vectors buffer. This is used by temporal antialiasing to correct for motion that occurs during gameplay.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

values.name: VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_INTERNAL_BUFFER
values.description:
Internal buffer is drawn instead of regular scene so you can see the per-pixel output that will be used by post-processing effects.
[b]Note:[/b] Only supported when using the Forward+ or Mobile rendering methods.

values.name: VIEWPORT_VRS_DISABLED
values.description: Variable rate shading is disabled.

values.name: VIEWPORT_VRS_TEXTURE
values.description: Variable rate shading uses a texture. Note, for stereoscopic use a texture atlas with a texture for each view.

values.name: VIEWPORT_VRS_XR
values.description: Variable rate shading texture is supplied by the primary [XRInterface]. Note that this may override the update mode.

values.name: VIEWPORT_VRS_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum ViewportVRSMode] enum.

values.name: VIEWPORT_VRS_UPDATE_DISABLED
values.description: The input texture for variable rate shading will not be processed.

values.name: VIEWPORT_VRS_UPDATE_ONCE
values.description: The input texture for variable rate shading will be processed once.

values.name: VIEWPORT_VRS_UPDATE_ALWAYS
values.description: The input texture for variable rate shading will be processed each frame.

values.name: VIEWPORT_VRS_UPDATE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum ViewportVRSUpdateMode] enum.

values.name: SKY_MODE_AUTOMATIC
values.description: Automatically selects the appropriate process mode based on your sky shader. If your shader uses [code]TIME[/code] or [code]POSITION[/code], this will use [constant SKY_MODE_REALTIME]. If your shader uses any of the [code]LIGHT_*[/code] variables or any custom uniforms, this uses [constant SKY_MODE_INCREMENTAL]. Otherwise, this defaults to [constant SKY_MODE_QUALITY].

values.name: SKY_MODE_QUALITY
values.description: Uses high quality importance sampling to process the radiance map. In general, this results in much higher quality than [constant SKY_MODE_REALTIME] but takes much longer to generate. This should not be used if you plan on changing the sky at runtime. If you are finding that the reflection is not blurry enough and is showing sparkles or fireflies, try increasing [member ProjectSettings.rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/ggx_samples].

values.name: SKY_MODE_INCREMENTAL
values.description: Uses the same high quality importance sampling to process the radiance map as [constant SKY_MODE_QUALITY], but updates over several frames. The number of frames is determined by [member ProjectSettings.rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/roughness_layers]. Use this when you need highest quality radiance maps, but have a sky that updates slowly.

values.name: SKY_MODE_REALTIME
values.description:
Uses the fast filtering algorithm to process the radiance map. In general this results in lower quality, but substantially faster run times. If you need better quality, but still need to update the sky every frame, consider turning on [member ProjectSettings.rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/fast_filter_high_quality].
[b]Note:[/b] The fast filtering algorithm is limited to 256×256 cubemaps, so [method sky_set_radiance_size] must be set to [code]256[/code]. Otherwise, a warning is printed and the overridden radiance size is ignored.

values.name: COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_FLAG_ACCESS_RESOLVED_COLOR
values.description: The rendering effect requires the color buffer to be resolved if MSAA is enabled.

values.name: COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_FLAG_ACCESS_RESOLVED_DEPTH
values.description: The rendering effect requires the depth buffer to be resolved if MSAA is enabled.

values.name: COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_FLAG_NEEDS_MOTION_VECTORS
values.description: The rendering effect requires motion vectors to be produced.

values.name: COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_FLAG_NEEDS_ROUGHNESS
values.description: The rendering effect requires normals and roughness g-buffer to be produced (Forward+ only).

values.name: COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_FLAG_NEEDS_SEPARATE_SPECULAR
values.description: The rendering effect requires specular data to be separated out (Forward+ only).

values.name: COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_PRE_OPAQUE
values.description: The callback is called before our opaque rendering pass, but after depth prepass (if applicable).

values.name: COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_POST_OPAQUE
values.description: The callback is called after our opaque rendering pass, but before our sky is rendered.

values.name: COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_POST_SKY
values.description: The callback is called after our sky is rendered, but before our back buffers are created (and if enabled, before subsurface scattering and/or screen space reflections).

values.name: COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_PRE_TRANSPARENT
values.description: The callback is called before our transparent rendering pass, but after our sky is rendered and we've created our back buffers.

values.name: COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_POST_TRANSPARENT
values.description: The callback is called after our transparent rendering pass, but before any built-in post-processing effects and output to our render target.

values.name: ENV_BG_CLEAR_COLOR
values.description: Use the clear color as background.

values.name: ENV_BG_COLOR
values.description: Use a specified color as the background.

values.name: ENV_BG_SKY
values.description: Use a sky resource for the background.

values.name: ENV_BG_CANVAS
values.description: Use a specified canvas layer as the background. This can be useful for instantiating a 2D scene in a 3D world.

values.name: ENV_BG_KEEP
values.description: Do not clear the background, use whatever was rendered last frame as the background.

values.name: ENV_BG_CAMERA_FEED
values.description: Displays a camera feed in the background.

values.name: ENV_BG_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum EnvironmentBG] enum.

values.name: ENV_AMBIENT_SOURCE_BG
values.description: Gather ambient light from whichever source is specified as the background.

values.name: ENV_AMBIENT_SOURCE_DISABLED
values.description: Disable ambient light.

values.name: ENV_AMBIENT_SOURCE_COLOR
values.description: Specify a specific [Color] for ambient light.

values.name: ENV_AMBIENT_SOURCE_SKY
values.description: Gather ambient light from the [Sky] regardless of what the background is.

values.name: ENV_REFLECTION_SOURCE_BG
values.description: Use the background for reflections.

values.name: ENV_REFLECTION_SOURCE_DISABLED
values.description: Disable reflections.

values.name: ENV_REFLECTION_SOURCE_SKY
values.description: Use the [Sky] for reflections regardless of what the background is.

values.name: ENV_GLOW_BLEND_MODE_ADDITIVE
values.description: Adds the glow effect to the scene.

values.name: ENV_GLOW_BLEND_MODE_SCREEN
values.description: Adds the glow effect to the scene after modifying the glow influence based on the scene value; dark values will be highly influenced by glow and bright values will not be influenced by glow. This approach avoids bright values becoming overly bright from the glow effect. [member Environment.tonemap_white] is used to determine the maximum scene value where the glow should have no influence. When [member Environment.tonemap_mode] is set to [constant Environment.TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR] and [member Viewport.use_hdr_2d] is [code]true[/code], the parent window's [method Window.get_output_max_linear_value] will be used as the maximum scene value.

values.name: ENV_GLOW_BLEND_MODE_SOFTLIGHT
values.description:
Adds the glow effect to the tonemapped image after modifying the glow influence based on the image value; dark values and bright values will not be influenced by glow and mid-range values will be highly influenced by glow. This approach avoids bright values becoming overly bright from the glow effect. The glow will have the largest influence on image values of [code]0.25[/code] and will have no influence when applied to image values greater than [code]1.0[/code].
[b]Note:[/b] This blend mode does not support HDR output because expects a maximum output value of [code]1.0[/code]. It is recommended to use a different blend mode when rendering to an HDR screen.

values.name: ENV_GLOW_BLEND_MODE_REPLACE
values.description: Replaces all pixels' color by the glow effect. This can be used to simulate a full-screen blur effect by tweaking the glow parameters to match the original image's brightness or to preview glow configuration in the editor.

values.name: ENV_GLOW_BLEND_MODE_MIX
values.description: Mixes the glow image with the scene image. Best used with [member Environment.glow_bloom] to avoid darkening the scene.

values.name: ENV_FOG_MODE_EXPONENTIAL
values.description: Use a physically-based fog model defined primarily by fog density.

values.name: ENV_FOG_MODE_DEPTH
values.description: Use a simple fog model defined by start and end positions and a custom curve. While not physically accurate, this model can be useful when you need more artistic control.

values.name: ENV_TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR
values.description: Does not modify color data, resulting in a linear tonemapping curve which unnaturally clips bright values, causing bright lighting to look blown out. The simplest and fastest tonemapper.

values.name: ENV_TONE_MAPPER_REINHARD
values.description:
A simple tonemapping curve that rolls off bright values to prevent clipping. This results in an image that can appear dull and low contrast. Slower than [constant ENV_TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR].
[b]Note:[/b] When [member Environment.tonemap_white] is left at the default value of [code]1.0[/code], [constant ENV_TONE_MAPPER_REINHARD] produces an identical image to [constant ENV_TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR].

values.name: ENV_TONE_MAPPER_FILMIC
values.description:
Uses a film-like tonemapping curve to prevent clipping of bright values and provide better contrast than [constant ENV_TONE_MAPPER_REINHARD]. Slightly slower than [constant ENV_TONE_MAPPER_REINHARD].
[b]Note:[/b] This tonemapper does not support HDR output because it produces output in the SDR range. It is recommended to use a different tonemapper when rendering to an HDR screen.

values.name: ENV_TONE_MAPPER_ACES
values.description:
Uses a high-contrast film-like tonemapping curve and desaturates bright values for a more realistic appearance. Slightly slower than [constant ENV_TONE_MAPPER_FILMIC].
[b]Note:[/b] This tonemapping operator is called "ACES Fitted" in Godot 3.x.
[b]Note:[/b] This tonemapper does not support HDR output because it produces output in the SDR range. It is recommended to use a different tonemapper when rendering to an HDR screen.

values.name: ENV_TONE_MAPPER_AGX
values.description: Uses an adjustable film-like tonemapping curve and desaturates bright values for a more realistic appearance. Better than other tonemappers at maintaining the hue of colors as they become brighter. The slowest tonemapping option.

values.name: ENV_SSR_ROUGHNESS_QUALITY_DISABLED
values.description: Lowest quality of roughness filter for screen-space reflections. Rough materials will not have blurrier screen-space reflections compared to smooth (non-rough) materials. This is the fastest option.

values.name: ENV_SSR_ROUGHNESS_QUALITY_LOW
values.description: Low quality of roughness filter for screen-space reflections.

values.name: ENV_SSR_ROUGHNESS_QUALITY_MEDIUM
values.description: Medium quality of roughness filter for screen-space reflections.

values.name: ENV_SSR_ROUGHNESS_QUALITY_HIGH
values.description: High quality of roughness filter for screen-space reflections. This is the slowest option.

values.name: ENV_SSAO_QUALITY_VERY_LOW
values.description: Lowest quality of screen-space ambient occlusion.

values.name: ENV_SSAO_QUALITY_LOW
values.description: Low quality screen-space ambient occlusion.

values.name: ENV_SSAO_QUALITY_MEDIUM
values.description: Medium quality screen-space ambient occlusion.

values.name: ENV_SSAO_QUALITY_HIGH
values.description: High quality screen-space ambient occlusion.

values.name: ENV_SSAO_QUALITY_ULTRA
values.description: Highest quality screen-space ambient occlusion. Uses the adaptive target setting which can be dynamically adjusted to smoothly balance performance and visual quality.

values.name: ENV_SSIL_QUALITY_VERY_LOW
values.description: Lowest quality of screen-space indirect lighting.

values.name: ENV_SSIL_QUALITY_LOW
values.description: Low quality screen-space indirect lighting.

values.name: ENV_SSIL_QUALITY_MEDIUM
values.description: High quality screen-space indirect lighting.

values.name: ENV_SSIL_QUALITY_HIGH
values.description: High quality screen-space indirect lighting.

values.name: ENV_SSIL_QUALITY_ULTRA
values.description: Highest quality screen-space indirect lighting. Uses the adaptive target setting which can be dynamically adjusted to smoothly balance performance and visual quality.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_Y_SCALE_50_PERCENT
values.description: Use 50% scale for SDFGI on the Y (vertical) axis. SDFGI cells will be twice as short as they are wide. This allows providing increased GI detail and reduced light leaking with thin floors and ceilings. This is usually the best choice for scenes that don't feature much verticality.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_Y_SCALE_75_PERCENT
values.description: Use 75% scale for SDFGI on the Y (vertical) axis. This is a balance between the 50% and 100% SDFGI Y scales.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_Y_SCALE_100_PERCENT
values.description: Use 100% scale for SDFGI on the Y (vertical) axis. SDFGI cells will be as tall as they are wide. This is usually the best choice for highly vertical scenes. The downside is that light leaking may become more noticeable with thin floors and ceilings.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_4
values.description: Throw 4 rays per frame when converging SDFGI. This has the lowest GPU requirements, but creates the most noisy result.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_8
values.description: Throw 8 rays per frame when converging SDFGI.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_16
values.description: Throw 16 rays per frame when converging SDFGI.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_32
values.description: Throw 32 rays per frame when converging SDFGI.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_64
values.description: Throw 64 rays per frame when converging SDFGI.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_96
values.description: Throw 96 rays per frame when converging SDFGI. This has high GPU requirements.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_128
values.description: Throw 128 rays per frame when converging SDFGI. This has very high GPU requirements, but creates the least noisy result.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum EnvironmentSDFGIRayCount] enum.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_CONVERGE_IN_5_FRAMES
values.description: Converge SDFGI over 5 frames. This is the most responsive, but creates the most noisy result with a given ray count.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_CONVERGE_IN_10_FRAMES
values.description: Configure SDFGI to fully converge over 10 frames.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_CONVERGE_IN_15_FRAMES
values.description: Configure SDFGI to fully converge over 15 frames.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_CONVERGE_IN_20_FRAMES
values.description: Configure SDFGI to fully converge over 20 frames.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_CONVERGE_IN_25_FRAMES
values.description: Configure SDFGI to fully converge over 25 frames.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_CONVERGE_IN_30_FRAMES
values.description: Configure SDFGI to fully converge over 30 frames. This is the least responsive, but creates the least noisy result with a given ray count.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_CONVERGE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum EnvironmentSDFGIFramesToConverge] enum.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_UPDATE_LIGHT_IN_1_FRAME
values.description: Update indirect light from dynamic lights in SDFGI over 1 frame. This is the most responsive, but has the highest GPU requirements.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_UPDATE_LIGHT_IN_2_FRAMES
values.description: Update indirect light from dynamic lights in SDFGI over 2 frames.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_UPDATE_LIGHT_IN_4_FRAMES
values.description: Update indirect light from dynamic lights in SDFGI over 4 frames.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_UPDATE_LIGHT_IN_8_FRAMES
values.description: Update indirect light from dynamic lights in SDFGI over 8 frames.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_UPDATE_LIGHT_IN_16_FRAMES
values.description: Update indirect light from dynamic lights in SDFGI over 16 frames. This is the least responsive, but has the lowest GPU requirements.

values.name: ENV_SDFGI_UPDATE_LIGHT_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum EnvironmentSDFGIFramesToUpdateLight] enum.

values.name: SUB_SURFACE_SCATTERING_QUALITY_DISABLED
values.description: Disables subsurface scattering entirely, even on materials that have [member BaseMaterial3D.subsurf_scatter_enabled] set to [code]true[/code]. This has the lowest GPU requirements.

values.name: SUB_SURFACE_SCATTERING_QUALITY_LOW
values.description: Low subsurface scattering quality.

values.name: SUB_SURFACE_SCATTERING_QUALITY_MEDIUM
values.description: Medium subsurface scattering quality.

values.name: SUB_SURFACE_SCATTERING_QUALITY_HIGH
values.description: High subsurface scattering quality. This has the highest GPU requirements.

values.name: DOF_BOKEH_BOX
values.description: Calculate the DOF blur using a box filter. The fastest option, but results in obvious lines in blur pattern.

values.name: DOF_BOKEH_HEXAGON
values.description: Calculates DOF blur using a hexagon shaped filter.

values.name: DOF_BOKEH_CIRCLE
values.description: Calculates DOF blur using a circle shaped filter. Best quality and most realistic, but slowest. Use only for areas where a lot of performance can be dedicated to post-processing (e.g. cutscenes).

values.name: DOF_BLUR_QUALITY_VERY_LOW
values.description: Lowest quality DOF blur. This is the fastest setting, but you may be able to see filtering artifacts.

values.name: DOF_BLUR_QUALITY_LOW
values.description: Low quality DOF blur.

values.name: DOF_BLUR_QUALITY_MEDIUM
values.description: Medium quality DOF blur.

values.name: DOF_BLUR_QUALITY_HIGH
values.description: Highest quality DOF blur. Results in the smoothest looking blur by taking the most samples, but is also significantly slower.

values.name: INSTANCE_NONE
values.description: The instance does not have a type.

values.name: INSTANCE_MESH
values.description: The instance is a mesh.

values.name: INSTANCE_MULTIMESH
values.description: The instance is a multimesh.

values.name: INSTANCE_PARTICLES
values.description: The instance is a particle emitter.

values.name: INSTANCE_PARTICLES_COLLISION
values.description: The instance is a GPUParticles collision shape.

values.name: INSTANCE_LIGHT
values.description: The instance is a light.

values.name: INSTANCE_REFLECTION_PROBE
values.description: The instance is a reflection probe.

values.name: INSTANCE_DECAL
values.description: The instance is a decal.

values.name: INSTANCE_VOXEL_GI
values.description: The instance is a VoxelGI.

values.name: INSTANCE_LIGHTMAP
values.description: The instance is a lightmap.

values.name: INSTANCE_OCCLUDER
values.description: The instance is an occlusion culling occluder.

values.name: INSTANCE_VISIBLITY_NOTIFIER
values.description: The instance is a visible on-screen notifier.

values.name: INSTANCE_FOG_VOLUME
values.description: The instance is a fog volume.

values.name: INSTANCE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum InstanceType] enum.

values.name: INSTANCE_GEOMETRY_MASK
values.description: A combination of the flags of geometry instances (mesh, multimesh, immediate and particles).

values.name: INSTANCE_FLAG_USE_BAKED_LIGHT
values.description: Allows the instance to be used in baked lighting.

values.name: INSTANCE_FLAG_USE_DYNAMIC_GI
values.description: Allows the instance to be used with dynamic global illumination.

values.name: INSTANCE_FLAG_DRAW_NEXT_FRAME_IF_VISIBLE
values.description: When set, manually requests to draw geometry on next frame.

values.name: INSTANCE_FLAG_IGNORE_OCCLUSION_CULLING
values.description: Always draw, even if the instance would be culled by occlusion culling. Does not affect view frustum culling.

values.name: INSTANCE_FLAG_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum InstanceFlags] enum.

values.description: Disable backface culling when rendering the shadow of the object. This is slightly slower but may result in more correct shadows.

values.name: SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_SHADOWS_ONLY
values.description: Only render the shadows from the object. The object itself will not be drawn.

values.name: VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_DEPENDENCIES

values.name: BAKE_CHANNEL_ALBEDO_ALPHA
values.description: Index of [Image] in array of [Image]s returned by [method bake_render_uv2]. Image uses [constant Image.FORMAT_RGBA8] and contains albedo color in the [code].rgb[/code] channels and alpha in the [code].a[/code] channel.

values.name: BAKE_CHANNEL_NORMAL
values.description: Index of [Image] in array of [Image]s returned by [method bake_render_uv2]. Image uses [constant Image.FORMAT_RGBA8] and contains the per-pixel normal of the object in the [code].rgb[/code] channels and nothing in the [code].a[/code] channel. The per-pixel normal is encoded as [code]normal * 0.5 + 0.5[/code].

values.name: BAKE_CHANNEL_ORM
values.description: Index of [Image] in array of [Image]s returned by [method bake_render_uv2]. Image uses [constant Image.FORMAT_RGBA8] and contains ambient occlusion (from material and decals only) in the [code].r[/code] channel, roughness in the [code].g[/code] channel, metallic in the [code].b[/code] channel and sub surface scattering amount in the [code].a[/code] channel.

values.name: BAKE_CHANNEL_EMISSION
values.description: Index of [Image] in array of [Image]s returned by [method bake_render_uv2]. Image uses [constant Image.FORMAT_RGBAH] and contains emission color in the [code].rgb[/code] channels and nothing in the [code].a[/code] channel.

values.name: CANVAS_TEXTURE_CHANNEL_SPECULAR

values.name: NINE_PATCH_STRETCH

values.name: CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_DEFAULT
values.description: Uses the default filter mode for this [Viewport].

values.name: CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST
values.description: The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel only. This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and grainy from a distance (due to mipmaps not being sampled).

values.name: CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR
values.description: The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels. This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and grainy from a distance (due to mipmaps not being sampled).

values.name: CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST_WITH_MIPMAPS
values.description:
The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel and blends between the nearest 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if [member ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter] is [code]true[/code]). This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and smooth from a distance.
Use this for non-pixel art textures that may be viewed at a low scale (e.g. due to [Camera2D] zoom or sprite scaling), as mipmaps are important to smooth out pixels that are smaller than on-screen pixels.

values.name: CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS
values.description:
The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels and between the nearest 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if [member ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter] is [code]true[/code]). This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and smooth from a distance.
Use this for non-pixel art textures that may be viewed at a low scale (e.g. due to [Camera2D] zoom or sprite scaling), as mipmaps are important to smooth out pixels that are smaller than on-screen pixels.

values.name: CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST_WITH_MIPMAPS_ANISOTROPIC
values.description:
The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel and blends between 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if [member ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter] is [code]true[/code]) based on the angle between the surface and the camera view. This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and smooth from a distance. Anisotropic filtering improves texture quality on surfaces that are almost in line with the camera, but is slightly slower. The anisotropic filtering level can be changed by adjusting [member ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/anisotropic_filtering_level].
[b]Note:[/b] This texture filter is rarely useful in 2D projects. [constant CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST_WITH_MIPMAPS] is usually more appropriate in this case.

values.name: CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS_ANISOTROPIC
values.description:
The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels and blends between 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if [member ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter] is [code]true[/code]) based on the angle between the surface and the camera view. This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and smooth from a distance. Anisotropic filtering improves texture quality on surfaces that are almost in line with the camera, but is slightly slower. The anisotropic filtering level can be changed by adjusting [member ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/anisotropic_filtering_level].
[b]Note:[/b] This texture filter is rarely useful in 2D projects. [constant CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS] is usually more appropriate in this case.

values.name: CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_MAX
values.description: Max value for [enum CanvasItemTextureFilter] enum.

values.name: CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_REPEAT_DEFAULT
values.description: Uses the default repeat mode for this [Viewport].

values.name: CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_REPEAT_DISABLED
values.description: Disables textures repeating. Instead, when reading UVs outside the 0-1 range, the value will be clamped to the edge of the texture, resulting in a stretched out look at the borders of the texture.

values.name: CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_REPEAT_ENABLED
values.description: Enables the texture to repeat when UV coordinates are outside the 0-1 range. If using one of the linear filtering modes, this can result in artifacts at the edges of a texture when the sampler filters across the edges of the texture.

values.name: CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_REPEAT_MIRROR
values.description: Flip the texture when repeating so that the edge lines up instead of abruptly changing.

values.name: CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_REPEAT_MAX
values.description: Max value for [enum CanvasItemTextureRepeat] enum.

values.name: CANVAS_GROUP_MODE_DISABLED

values.name: CANVAS_GROUP_MODE_CLIP_ONLY

values.name: CANVAS_GROUP_MODE_CLIP_AND_DRAW

values.name: CANVAS_LIGHT_MODE_DIRECTIONAL

values.name: CANVAS_LIGHT_BLEND_MODE_SUB

values.name: CANVAS_LIGHT_BLEND_MODE_MIX

values.name: CANVAS_LIGHT_FILTER_PCF5

values.name: CANVAS_LIGHT_FILTER_PCF13

values.name: RENDERING_INFO_TOTAL_OBJECTS_IN_FRAME
values.description: Number of objects rendered in the current 3D scene. This varies depending on camera position and rotation.

values.name: RENDERING_INFO_TOTAL_PRIMITIVES_IN_FRAME
values.description: Number of points, lines, or triangles rendered in the current 3D scene. This varies depending on camera position and rotation.

values.name: RENDERING_INFO_TOTAL_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME
values.description: Number of draw calls performed to render in the current 3D scene. This varies depending on camera position and rotation.

values.name: RENDERING_INFO_TEXTURE_MEM_USED
values.description: Texture memory used (in bytes).

values.name: RENDERING_INFO_BUFFER_MEM_USED
values.description: Buffer memory used (in bytes). This includes vertex data, uniform buffers, and many miscellaneous buffer types used internally.

values.name: RENDERING_INFO_VIDEO_MEM_USED
values.description: Video memory used (in bytes). When using the Forward+ or Mobile renderers, this is always greater than the sum of [constant RENDERING_INFO_TEXTURE_MEM_USED] and [constant RENDERING_INFO_BUFFER_MEM_USED], since there is miscellaneous data not accounted for by those two metrics. When using the Compatibility renderer, this is equal to the sum of [constant RENDERING_INFO_TEXTURE_MEM_USED] and [constant RENDERING_INFO_BUFFER_MEM_USED].

values.name: RENDERING_INFO_PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_CANVAS
values.description: Number of pipeline compilations that were triggered by the 2D canvas renderer.

values.name: RENDERING_INFO_PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_MESH
values.description: Number of pipeline compilations that were triggered by loading meshes. These compilations will show up as longer loading times the first time a user runs the game and the pipeline is required.

values.name: RENDERING_INFO_PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_SURFACE
values.description: Number of pipeline compilations that were triggered by building the surface cache before rendering the scene. These compilations will show up as a stutter when loading a scene the first time a user runs the game and the pipeline is required.

values.name: RENDERING_INFO_PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_DRAW
values.description: Number of pipeline compilations that were triggered while drawing the scene. These compilations will show up as stutters during gameplay the first time a user runs the game and the pipeline is required.

values.name: RENDERING_INFO_PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_SPECIALIZATION
values.description: Number of pipeline compilations that were triggered to optimize the current scene. These compilations are done in the background and should not cause any stutters whatsoever.

values.name: PIPELINE_SOURCE_MESH
values.description: Pipeline compilation that was triggered by loading a mesh.

values.name: PIPELINE_SOURCE_SURFACE
values.description: Pipeline compilation that was triggered by building the surface cache before rendering the scene.

values.name: PIPELINE_SOURCE_DRAW
values.description: Pipeline compilation that was triggered while drawing the scene.

values.name: PIPELINE_SOURCE_SPECIALIZATION
values.description: Pipeline compilation that was triggered to optimize the current scene.

values.name: PIPELINE_SOURCE_MAX
values.description: Represents the size of the [enum PipelineSource] enum.

values.name: SPLASH_STRETCH_MODE_DISABLED

values.description: Stretches the height of the image based on the width of the screen.

values.name: SPLASH_STRETCH_MODE_KEEP_HEIGHT

methods.name: texture_2d_create
methods.description:
Creates a 2-dimensional texture and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all [code]texture_2d_*[/code] RenderingServer functions.
Once finished with your RID, you will want to free the RID using the RenderingServer's [method free_rid] method.
[b]Note:[/b] The equivalent resource is [Texture2D].
[b]Note:[/b] Not to be confused with [method RenderingDevice.texture_create], which creates the graphics API's own texture type as opposed to the Godot-specific [Texture2D] resource.

methods.name: texture_2d_layered_create
methods.description:
Creates a 2-dimensional layered texture and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all [code]texture_2d_layered_*[/code] RenderingServer functions.
Once finished with your RID, you will want to free the RID using the RenderingServer's [method free_rid] method.
[b]Note:[/b] The equivalent resource is [TextureLayered].

methods.name: texture_3d_create
methods.description: [b]Note:[/b] The equivalent resource is [Texture3D].

methods.name: texture_proxy_create
methods.description: This method does nothing and always returns an invalid [RID].

methods.name: texture_create_from_native_handle
methods.description:
Creates a texture based on a native handle that was created outside of Godot's renderer.
[b]Note:[/b] If using only the rendering device renderer, it's recommend to use [method RenderingDevice.texture_create_from_extension] together with [method RenderingServer.texture_rd_create], rather than this method. This way, the texture's format and usage can be controlled more effectively.

methods.name: texture_drawable_create
methods.description:
Creates a 2-dimensional texture and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all [code]texture_drawable*[/code] RenderingServer functions.
Once finished with your RID, you will want to free the RID using the RenderingServer's [method free_rid] method.
[b]Note:[/b] The equivalent resource is [DrawableTexture2D].

methods.name: texture_2d_update
methods.description:
Updates the texture specified by the [param texture] [RID] with the data in [param image]. A [param layer] must also be specified, which should be [code]0[/code] when updating a single-layer texture ([Texture2D]).
[b]Note:[/b] The [param image] must have the same width, height and format as the current [param texture] data. Otherwise, an error will be printed and the original texture won't be modified. If you need to use different width, height or format, use [method texture_replace] instead.

methods.name: texture_3d_update
methods.description:
Updates the texture specified by the [param texture] [RID]'s data with the data in [param data]. All the texture's layers must be replaced at once.
[b]Note:[/b] The [param texture] must have the same width, height, depth and format as the current texture data. Otherwise, an error will be printed and the original texture won't be modified. If you need to use different width, height, depth or format, use [method texture_replace] instead.

methods.name: texture_proxy_update
methods.description: This method does nothing.

methods.name: texture_drawable_blit_rect
methods.description:
Draws to [param rect] on up to 4 given Drawable [param textures], using a TextureBlit Shader from [param material]. [param modulate] and up to 4 [param source_textures] are uniforms for the Shader to process with. [param to_mipmap] can specify to perform this draw to a lower mipmap level.
[b]Note:[/b] All [param textures] must be the same size and format.

methods.name: texture_2d_placeholder_create
methods.description:
Creates a placeholder for a 2-dimensional layered texture and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all [code]texture_2d_layered_*[/code] RenderingServer functions, although it does nothing when used. See also [method texture_2d_layered_placeholder_create].
Once finished with your RID, you will want to free the RID using the RenderingServer's [method free_rid] method.
[b]Note:[/b] The equivalent resource is [PlaceholderTexture2D].

methods.name: texture_2d_layered_placeholder_create
methods.description:
Creates a placeholder for a 2-dimensional layered texture and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all [code]texture_2d_layered_*[/code] RenderingServer functions, although it does nothing when used. See also [method texture_2d_placeholder_create].
[b]Note:[/b] The equivalent resource is [PlaceholderTextureLayered].

methods.name: texture_3d_placeholder_create
methods.description:
Creates a placeholder for a 3-dimensional texture and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all [code]texture_3d_*[/code] RenderingServer functions, although it does nothing when used.
Once finished with your RID, you will want to free the RID using the RenderingServer's [method free_rid] method.
[b]Note:[/b] The equivalent resource is [PlaceholderTexture3D].

methods.name: texture_2d_get
methods.description:
Returns an [Image] instance from the given [param texture] [RID].
[b]Example:[/b] Get the test texture from [method get_test_texture] and apply it to a [Sprite2D] node:
[codeblock]
var texture_rid = RenderingServer.get_test_texture()
var texture = ImageTexture.create_from_image(RenderingServer.texture_2d_get(texture_rid))
$Sprite2D.texture = texture
[/codeblock]

methods.name: texture_2d_layer_get
methods.description: Returns an [Image] instance from the given [param texture] [RID] and [param layer].

methods.name: texture_3d_get
methods.description: Returns 3D texture data as an array of [Image]s for the specified texture [RID].

methods.name: texture_drawable_generate_mipmaps
methods.description: Calculates new MipMaps for the given Drawable [param texture].

methods.name: texture_drawable_get_default_material
methods.description: Returns a ShaderMaterial with the default texture_blit Shader.

methods.name: texture_replace
methods.description: Replaces [param texture]'s texture data by the texture specified by the [param by_texture] RID, without changing [param texture]'s RID.

methods.name: texture_set_size_override
methods.description: Sets the size at which the texture should be [i]displayed[/i] in 2D, ignoring its original size. This does not rescale the texture data itself, only how it is drawn in 2D. Set [param width] and [param height] to 0 to disable the size override.

methods.name: texture_set_path
methods.description:
Sets the resource path for this texture RID. See also [method texture_get_path].
[b]Note:[/b] This is purely a hint and does not cause the texture to be automatically saved when set to a [code]res://[/code] path.

methods.name: texture_get_path
methods.description: Returns the resource path (starting with [code]res://[/code] or [code]uid://[/code]) for the specified texture RID. Returns an empty [String] if the resource is built-in. See also [method texture_set_path].

methods.name: texture_get_format
methods.description: Returns the format for the texture.

methods.name: texture_set_force_redraw_if_visible
methods.description: Sets whether the texture RID should force redrawing when it's visible on screen when [member OS.low_processor_usage_mode] is [code]true[/code]. This is used by [AnimatedTexture] to force redrawing.

methods.name: texture_rd_create
methods.description:
Creates a new texture object based on a texture created directly on the [RenderingDevice]. If the texture contains layers, [param layer_type] is used to define the layer type.
Once finished with your RID, you will want to free the RID using the RenderingServer's [method free_rid] method.
[b]Note:[/b] The RenderingServer's [method free_rid] won't free the underlying [param rd_texture], you will want to free the [param rd_texture] using [method RenderingDevice.free_rid].

methods.name: texture_get_rd_texture
methods.description:
Returns a texture [RID] that can be used with [RenderingDevice].
[param srgb] should be [code]true[/code] when the texture uses nonlinear sRGB encoding and [code]false[/code] when the texture uses linear encoding.

methods.name: texture_get_native_handle
methods.description:
Returns the internal graphics handle for this texture object. For use when communicating with third-party APIs mostly with GDExtension.
[param srgb] should be [code]true[/code] when the texture uses nonlinear sRGB encoding and [code]false[/code] when the texture uses linear encoding.
[b]Note:[/b] This function returns a [code]uint64_t[/code] which internally maps to a [code]GLuint[/code] (OpenGL) or [code]VkImage[/code] (Vulkan).

methods.name: shader_create
methods.description:
Creates an empty shader and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all [code]shader_*[/code] RenderingServer functions.
Once finished with your RID, you will want to free the RID using the RenderingServer's [method free_rid] method.
[b]Note:[/b] The equivalent resource is [Shader].

methods.name: shader_set_code
methods.description: Sets the shader's source code (which triggers recompilation after being changed).

methods.name: shader_set_path_hint
methods.description: Sets the path hint for the specified shader. This should generally match the [Shader] resource's [member Resource.resource_path].

methods.name: shader_get_code
methods.description: Returns a shader's source code as a string.

methods.name: get_shader_parameter_list
methods.description: Returns the parameters of a shader.

methods.name: material_create
methods.description:
Creates an empty material and adds it to the RenderingServer. It can be accessed with the RID that is returned. This RID will be used in all [code]material_*[/code] RenderingServer functions.
Once finished with your RID, you will want to free the RID using the RenderingServer's [method free_rid] method.
[b]Note:[/b] The equivalent resource is [Material].
